#2223. Julien Stephan confirms ‘long-term injury’ for QPR forward ahead of Burnley clash

QPR were beaten 4-1 by Southampton on Saturday, and the result wasn’t the only dampener on a tough day at the office for the Hoops. After being introduced as a second-half substitute, forward Alfie Lloyd hobbled off through injury.

Now, speaking to West London Sport ahead of Tuesday’s tie against Burnley, R’s boss Julien Stephan revealed the 23-year-old looks set for an extended spell on the sidelines. Lloyd is set to be out for two months, likely keeping him sidelined until 2027.

“It’s a long-term injury,” Stephan said. “It will probably be difficult for him to come back before the end of the year.”

Jake Clarke-Salter is also expected to miss the Burnley tie, though his issue is undisclosed at present. Nicolas Madsen, Rumarn Burrell and Tariq Lamptey are on course for returns right after the November international break, and Ilias Chair is set to be eased back in with more substitute appearances after his return on Saturday.

Stephan does not have the biggest of squads at QPR, but he has good depth in all positions. That has been put to the test in the first quarter of the campaign, especially in attack.

Lloyd offers his services across the front three, and his versatility has helped deal with a shortage of options. Up top, all of Richard Kone, Justin Obikwu, Burrell and now Lloyd have had time on the sidelines, while Rayan Kolli was omitted too.

On the wings, Karamoko Dembele is still working back to full fitness after his ACL injury. Chair and Koki Saito, have had their issues as well, so it has been a heavily impacted area.

Stephan’s options have replenished over recent weeks, but Lloyd now drops out to leave the boss without a flexible forward and a strong physical profile. It will be hoped he can recover swiftly to return as soon and as safely as possible.

Lloyd’s long-term absence serves as a blow, but QPR do have the players to deal with the blow.

Stephan could recall one of Leon Scarlett or Justin Obikwu to the bench to cover. Kone will be backed to hold onto his starting berth having netted again in the Southampton loss.

Burnley have conceded 25 times in 13 games this season, and that record is something the Hoops will be ready to target. They have scored nine goals in their last two matches at Loftus Road, and they have the attacking style and talent to find a similar level of success against the Clarets.

#2222. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2221. Alan Shearer names EFL club he nearly managed after Newcastle

The former England legend Alan Shearer has revealed that he almost went back into management in the Championship after his brief spell as the interim manager at Newcastle United.

With a career that ran to over 700 games and almost 400 goals, few other English players of the 1990s or 2000s were as lauded as Alan Shearer. The striker won the Premier League title with Blackburn Rovers in 1995 and captained England thirty times, and since the end of his career has carved himself out a successful niche as a television pundit.

But Shearer also had an extremely brief spell in management when, on the 1st April 2009, it was confirmed that he would be taking interim charge of a Newcastle United team that was floundering towards relegation from the Premier League. Shearer was unable to keep Newcastle up, and to date that unhappy couple of months remains his sole foray into management.

And although the striker subsequently went back into media work, the striker has now revealed that he almost went back into management after the Newcastle debacle in the Championship with Cardiff City.

Speaking to the BBC for their series The Football Interview, Alan Shearer has confirmed that he almost accepted the Cardiff City manager's job after his departure from Newcastle United, but changed his mind following three interviews.

"I always felt like I was going to go into it [management] again, and I wanted to, but then I had a couple of interviews," he told them, "I went for one interview, went for another interview at the same club, went for a third interview, got offered the job..."

How do you think that Alan Shearer would have fared as a manager in the Championship? Let us know in the comments below!

Pressed by the interviewer over the identity of the club involved, Shearer replied, "It was Cardiff," but he went on to explain that he ended up not accepting the offer to manage at The Cardiff City Stadium.

"Things changed in a different interview, and then the last one, it went sort of... again, and then I thought, "What am I doing here? If things are changing throughout the interview process, then what's it going to be like when I'm in?" He confirmed that, having turned down Cardiff's overtures, he didn't receive any other offers: "I didn't get any more after that, and then I just thought, 'You know what, I'm just going to get my head down and stick to the punditry."

When Alan Shearer was called in as the interim Newcastle United manager at the start of April 2009, the appointment felt like a final desperate roll of the dice at the end of a chaotic season. Shearer was Newcastle's fourth manager of the season, following on from Kevin Keegan, Joe Kinnear and Chris Hughton, and at the time of his appointment they were in 18th place in the Premier League, two points adrift of safety.

Shearer was unable to keep Newcastle in the Premier League. They picked up just one win - against Middlesbrough in their third-last game of the season - and two draws from their final eight League matches of the season, ending the season in 18th place in the table, a points shy of safety. When the decision was made over who would lead Newcastle's bid to return to the top-flight, the job was given to Chris Hughton over Shearer.

Who are the most clutch players in the Championship that could whip in a last-minute set piece worldie?

But the former England captain's recent revelations shine a new light on what happened for him afterwards. Shearer didn't reveal when he was interviewed for the Cardiff City job, but the most likely time will have been 2011, when they were looking for a replacement for Dave Jones.

At that time, the club had been under the ownership of the Malaysian businessman Vincent Tan for a year, and Shearer's description of the interview process at the club certainly fits Tan's occasionally eccentric ownership style.

A year after Malky Mackay was appointed as the club's manager, Tan incensed Bluebirds fans by changing the club's colours from blue and white to red and black, but life at The Cardiff City Stadium under his ownership has always been something of a rollercoaster. Under his leadership, has also been promoted to the Premier League twice, for the 2013-14 and 2018-19 seasons, though they were unable to stay up on either occasion.

Collect every point to win the round. Don’t let Neil Warnock catch you.

Swipe on the pitch or use the pad to move.

Given the state that Newcastle United were in by the time that they called on Alan Shearer in 2009, it's difficult to pin the blame for their relegation from the Premier League on him, and Shearer has gone on to have a successful career in punditry which continues to this day.

We'll probably never know whether he could have gone on to have a successful career in management, but if there's one thing that can be confidently predicted about what might have happened had he accepted the Cardiff City job, it's that it would have been eventful.

#2220. Outspoken pundit ends six-month Hampden exile after SFA row

Michael Stewart has returned to Hampden more than six months after being banned from the national stadium by the SFA.

The outspoken pundit was ordered to stay away from the ground earlier this year following his fierce criticism of Scottish referees.

Michael Stewart returns to Hampden today 🎙️ https://t.co/aeJRjc0Z9z

— Premier Sports (@PremSportsTV) October 31, 2026

But Stewart is back inside Hampden for today’s Premier Sports Cup semi-final between Rangers and Aberdeen after the long-running row was resolved.

The former Hearts and Hibs midfielder was initially handed an indefinite ban, which saw him miss both Scottish Cup semi-finals and the final in May.

Stewart even resorted to broadcasting from inside a production truck parked outside Hampden during Dunfermline’s semi-final clash with Falkirk, only to later be told the car park was also off limits.

He has now been allowed to return and has apologised to SFA chiefs for comments he accepts went “over the top”.

A statement released by Premier Sports on Stewart’s behalf read: “On both sides there was an agreement that everyone has the right to an opinion, but I also accept that at times some of my comments may have been over the top and I have apologised for that.

#2219. Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller

Was this evidence of England head coach Thomas Tuchel already learning lessons from the Argentina collapse? Let’s hope so.

With England on the ropes and in danger of throwing away a lead against France, Tuchel resisted the temptation to flood his team with defenders and was rewarded with a World Cup bronze medal.

England looked on course to secure an emphatic victory to clinch the nation’s best World Cup finish since 1966 and yet Tuchel was left with the exact same scenario that had gone so badly against Argentina in the semi-final.

Leading by four goals at half-time, England somehow went into the final hydration break of this bronze medal game with a single-goal advantage. This time, Tuchel steered England over the line by getting his late substitutions right.

Jude Bellingham stepped off the bench to cap a wonderful tournament for him with the goal that made sure England finished the World Cup in third place.

It may have resembled an exhibition match at times, with France failing to turn up in the first half. But England’s thrilling 6-4 victory will send Tuchel home from the United States feeling a little bit better, even though he is not yet off the hook for what happened in Atlanta.

The fact that success against France was earned with a Bukayo Saka hat-trick, as well as goals from Declan Rice, Ezri Konsa and Bellingham, will prompt more debate over Tuchel’s decision-making when it really mattered. Not least why Saka watched the entire Argentina game from the substitutes’ bench.

Tuchel cut a relaxed figure, changing his touchline attire to a casual white T-shirt and tracksuit bottoms. But his team meant business, as they raced into a stunning four-goal first-half lead.

Saka played like a man with a point to prove. He scored twice and produced the shot from which England won the corner for Konsa’s goal in the opening 45 minutes. Was this a message to Tuchel or simply the winger taking out his frustration on France?

France looked uninterested from the start and it was a loose Désiré Doué pass that gifted possession to Rice. As England’s captain for the evening strode forwards, Doué did not bother to track him and Rice curled a lovely shot into the corner of the net to give Tuchel’s team a third-minute lead.

It's a quick start from England! 🦁⚡Declan Rice fires home the opener in the third minute against France ⚽ pic.twitter.com/ID4u3rXOuM

Having been criticised for sending on three defenders against Argentina, Tuchel started with five attacking players on the pitch and just Rice in front of the defence.

Saka had a goal correctly ruled out for offside before his shot was blocked for a corner, from which England doubled their lead. Rice turned provider, as he sent in a perfect delivery that was headed past goalkeeper Mike Maignan by Konsa five minutes before the first hydration break.

The Three Lions double their lead! 🦁⚽Ezri Konsa rises highest from Declan Rice's corner to head home 🙌 pic.twitter.com/8BfI1LSDOQ

While Tuchel would have been delighted with his team’s start to the game, Saka’s influence raises just as many questions as answers.

Saka was the next England player on the scoresheet. He sent Marcus Rashford away on goal. Rashford’s shot was saved, but England kept the ball alive and Saka eventually found the back of the net via a deflection.

The Three Lions lead France by three goals! 🦁🔥Bukayo Saka finishing off a quick England counter-attack ⚽ pic.twitter.com/9SCfE3uH3v

England had been given much sterner tests by DR Congo and Panama, and yet Tuchel’s players deserve praise for capitalising on such a terrible first-half performance from France.

Ebererchi Eze could not have believed that he was given the time and space to turn and pick out Saka on the stroke of half-time. He did so superbly and Saka easily added England’s fourth goal.

🗣 "France are being taken apart by England!" Bukayo Saka scores his second for the Three Lions' FOURTH goal against the two-time world champions 🤯 pic.twitter.com/4RshXY692E

It perhaps summed up France’s mentality that Kylian Mbappé, who threatened on a couple of occasions in the first half, reacted to England’s fourth goal with what appeared to be a slight smirk.

Tuchel’s name had been booed by some of those, mostly neutral supporters, inside the Hard Rock Stadium ahead of kick-off.

His star has undoubtedly fallen as a result of the Argentina defeat and yet nobody could have failed to have been impressed by what his and his players produced in the first half on Saturday night, however bad France had been.

When Tuchel made a change at half-time, there was no Dan Burn sent on to try to see out a 4-0 win. Instead, it was an attacking substitution with Ollie Watkins replacing Rashford. It immediately backfired, but Tuchel was later rewarded for trying to remain positive.

Watkins’s first act was to lose the ball on the halfway line to start a France attack that ended in a goal. Michael Olise played in Mbappé, who slotted the ball past Dean Henderson, who was given a rare chance ahead of Jordan Pickford.

France substitute Bradley Barcola pulled another goal back in the 54th minute, which meant that England’s four-goal advantage had been halved in just nine second-half minutes.

There was still no call for Burn, as Tuchel stuck to his gung-ho approach and Henderson had to save well from Ousmane Dembélé, who had also been sent on at the break. England had lost their balance with the half-time change and Olise was the next France attacker to go close.

Dembélé tested Henderson again before Mbappé got France’s third goal just before the final hydration break to pass Lionel Messi as the World Cup’s all-time top scorer. Like they had against Argentina, England had dropped deep and invited pressure as their opposition grew in confidence.

Kylian Mbappe scores his 22nd World Cup goal to become the leading goalscorer in the history of the competition ⚽🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/sDTNnW0kLZ

Having led so comfortably at half-time, England went into the final quarter of the game with a slender one-goal lead – just as they had against Argentina in Atlanta.

Olise somehow missed a sitter after arriving late on the end of a low ball across the penalty area and Tuchel decided it was time for more changes. But it was Elliot Anderson and Bellingham he called for, rather than any extra defenders, and it ultimately paid dividends.

Bellingham almost dribbled his way through to put the result beyond doubt, before Olise squandered another wonderful opportunity. Mercifully, Djed Spence won an 85th-minute penalty that allowed Saka to complete his hat-trick.

Bukayo Saka completes his hat-trick from the penalty spot! ⚽3️⃣England lead France 5-3 in the closing stages of this game 🦁 pic.twitter.com/EnYOg8UAvT

There was still time for Dembélé to briefly up England’s anxiety levels again, before Bellingham put the finishing touch to what has been an outstanding World Cup for him with a brilliant goal.

Jude Bellingham grabbing England's SIXTH goal against France! 🦁Driving over the halfway line before firing a shot into the bottom corner 🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/l0B0BVs548

The players made sure to invite Jason Steele on to the stage to receive a medal. The Brighton goalkeeper is not in England’s World Cup squad, but travelled to North America as a training goalkeeper.

Of course I would love to have played more but it’s too late to talk about that. I try to do my talking on the pitch and it’s done now, move on. I’m fit.

We built and built across the tournament. We had some amazing results and in the end we fell short against Argentina. It hurts a lot to all of us and I’m sure it’s the same to the fans back home but we have to hold out head high and focus on the next one.

France are not hanging around for the ceremony. They are down the tunnel as organisers set up a stage to hand out the bronze medals. Probably sums up their attitude to the game.

Enough for four matches, what happened here. We had a brilliant first half, then a turbulent second half. You could see the difference of what one day makes and the difference in the schedule. We are so, so tired and drained from the last weeks.

So a massive compliment and full respect - the mentality that we showed. Going through all the adversity is absolutely brilliant.

I was afraid of the physical demands of the match. We know the quality and speed of France, and they have much less schedule for them. It was less demanding.

They had one more day in-between the semi-final to digest, and they had way less travel distances than us.

We played in the heat, at altitude. I was worried physically. You could see it in the second half, the cramps and all the tiredness, but I was never worried about the mentality.

I have said it before, this team has created something very special, and they showed it again.

However we got here England have had their best World Cup since 1966. Whatever criticism Thomas Tuchel received after Argentina defeat he deserves to keep his job and the chance to put things right in 2028 #england

Some players from France and England are huddled near the halfway line praying. Among them are Dayot Upamecano, Maxence Lacroix, Trevoh Chalobah and Bukayo Saka. Very different atmosphere to the Argentina defeat three days ago in Atlanta. They are playing Wonderwall here as they prepare for the bronze medals to be handed out but it is not very celebratory this time.

When does the second set start? That was as much as you could hope for from a third/fourth-place play-off. Some slack defending, some high-quality combination play and lots of entertainment. England’s victory stops things spiralling further for Tuchel, but there will be a sense of what might have been, not least the fact Saka played no part in the semi-final.

Bellingham’s seventh goal of the tournament, which is the highest tally by an England player at a World Cup. The game was stretched, but it was a fantastic individual goal from Bellingham, carrying the ball forward from the halfway line. He showed great composure not to take the shot too early, taking extra touches to finish with aplomb.

A seventh goal of the tournament for Jude Bellingham! 7️⃣⭐The most EVER by an Englishman at a single World Cup 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿👏 pic.twitter.com/YACnNWvqW1

Good work from Reece James to keep the ball and then defend well against Barcola.

What a barmy game this has been. Upamecano started the move with good defending and a surge forward, and then Dembele cuts inside Chalobah and buries a shot into the bottom corner.

🇫🇷 Ousmane Dembele scores France's fourth goal against England ⚽ pic.twitter.com/U4gCVb1tQw

Spence down and receiving some treatment for cramp after winning a challenge against Olise. France not happy with the stoppage in the game.

Excellent Rice challenge, and then Bellingham wins a free-kick in midfield. Rice can hardly run yet managed to time his challenge well. Trevoh Chalobah replaces Marc Guehi.

Seven minutes of added time to play, and France have just been caught offside from their own short corner.

That is England’s first World Cup hat-trick since Harry Kane scored three against Panama in the 2018 finals. But Bukayo Saka’s treble is also the last England hat-trick in all competitions since.... Bukayo Saka. The Arsenal forward also scored three times in the win over North Macedonia in 2023.

That was very unselfish from Jude Bellingham, because had he scored the penalty it would have been his seventh goal of the tournament. That would be the most goals scored by an England player at a World Cup.

Sends Maignan the wrong way, and picks out the bottom corner. Saka has his hat-trick, and England are surely assured of third place and the bronze medal/trophy. England’s players will be most pleased to avoid extra time.

Bukayo Saka completes his hat-trick from the penalty spot! ⚽3️⃣England lead France 5-3 in the closing stages of this game 🦁 pic.twitter.com/EnYOg8UAvT

Won by Djed Spence, who was too sharp by Malo Gusto. Once the England full-back got his toe to the ball, it was a stonewall penalty. Morgan Rogers played the pass to release him on the overlap.

Bellingham or Saka for the hat-trick? Bellingham has the ball in his hands, but then passes it to Saka for the hat-trick.

Qunsah off, Reece James on. That also looks a case of cramp in very humid conditions in Miami.

Now Olise misses a sitter! Great interplay in the box involving Olise and Dembele, five-a-side football between the France forwards, but the finish was lacking. Olise, and then the referee, receive some treatment for cramp.

England with a great chance to wrap the game up but Bellingham fluffed his lines! Burst through, the benefit of fresh legs, but he carried the ball too close to Maignan and then Rogers’s follow up was blocked.

Ivan Toney and Eberechi Eze are the players coming off, Bellingham and Anderson on, which adds some strength to England’s midfield.

That is a big cheer for Bellingham coming on, one of the stars of the World Cup and appreciated by the neutral. His job here is to see out a win.

France continue to dominate, and they have a free-kick in a crossing position. Cleared by Eze. Elliott Anderson is ready to come on, as well as Bellingham. Digne finds Mbappe, but Konsa makes a good block. Rogers then does well to make it stick and buy a foul.

Great chance for France to equalise, but Michael Olise opened up his foot too much and his shot flew past the post. France look like scoring every time they venture into England’s defensive third. Mbappe goes down looking for a penalty, but nothing doing, before Digne fouls Saka in the box. May have been knee on knee contact, looked a sore one for Saka. Bellingham is ready to come on.

Rice is still out there, soldiering on. Somewhat surprising that Tuchel has not added fresh legs since his half-time changes. Better spell of possession in the last few minutes from England. There have been 15 shots on target in this game.

Play has stopped immediately after the goal for the hydration break. Tuchel mist be thinking about changes. Rice is struggling.

A penny for Mikel Arteta's thoughts watching this: if one of his first comments during pre-season isn't an eruption about how Declan Rice has been asked to play again, he will have mellowed. He's as tired as an also ran at the end of the Grand National.

This is a fantastic France goal, razor sharp link up play between Mbappe and Olise at the edge of the box, and the France captain’s finish was unerring. Drilled into the bottom corner with his left foot. Liquid football. Defending remains optional in this game, but that goal would have graced any game. Mbappe’s 22nd World Cup goal.

Over to you Lionel! Mbappe’s 10th goal of the World Cup means he is the clear leader in the Golden Boot table - but Lionel Messi has a chance in the final tomorrow to add to his eight goals. You would not bet against Mbappe adding to his total here. England have been guilty of dropping deep again, just like they did against Argentina. They are a 4-4-2 with Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney partnering each other. This was just before the “hydration”, so Tuchel could change it up now.

Kylian Mbappe scores his 22nd World Cup goal to become the leading goalscorer in the history of the competition ⚽🔥👏 pic.twitter.com/sDTNnW0kLZ

There is a loud chant coming from the stands: “Mexico!” That shows the diversity of the crowd here, with empty seats in sections including the England supporters. In just one small block of fans in front of the press box, there are shirts from Colombia, Inter Miami, Chile and USA.

France should probably be back to within one goal, but Ousmane Dembele scuffed his shot from a favourable position in the box and it was a simple save for Henderson. Then the goalkeeper pushes away a long-range hit by Upamecano.

Delightful scooped pass over the top of the France defence by Eze but Toney could not bring the ball under his spell off his chest. Then Spence does brilliantly to win a tackle and then turn defence into attakc with a surging run forward.

Morgan Rogers with a sloppy pass inside his own half, and Olise fires wide from the edge of the box. He had so much time and space to line it up. Some fatigue starting to show in England’s legs now.

This is what Tuchel was talking about when he discussed England playing under pressure. France have decided to show up and all of a sudden the deficit is only two goals. Get ready for a testing half an hour.

England go close to another set-piece goal, but Maignan saves well after Toney rose to meet Rice’s inswinging delivery. There are surely going to be more goals in this game.

Henderson stands up well to save from Dembele, but the flag belatedly was raised for offside. A lot of wasted energy for Declan Rice, who had sprinted back some 60 yards to defend. England now the team being repeatedly exposed in transition.

Mbappe with the ball inside Quansah, who loses track of Barcola and with his pace that is always fatal. It looked like Barcola might have overrun the ball, but he got his shot off in time to find the bottom corner.

It's a second goal for France! 🇫🇷Kylian Mbappe's long pass finds Bradley Barcola who fires home 🔥 pic.twitter.com/h4GvkBZOSN

Great play from Eze, close control and quick feet to skip through two or three France challenges in midfield, and he tried to chip Maignan from the halfway line. Always drifting wide.

Composed football from England, playing out from deep in their own half with Rice finding Rogers between the lines. Saka with a pass into Watkins but his shot was tame. Then England and Spence were caught forward, but Rice got his toe to the ball ahead of Olise. Then Rabiot volleys not far wide. Chances galore in this game.

France reduce the deficit through Mbappe’s ninth goal of the tournament. Watkins was caught in possession by Upamecano on halfway, and France found Olise free in the No 10 zone. Lovely through ball splits the England defence, and Mbappe finishes first time beyond Henderson with his left foot.

France hit back after the break! 🇫🇷💥Kylian Mbappe pulls one back with his ninth goal at the 2026 World Cup ⚽ pic.twitter.com/Hxfg1s46ER

Hernandez, Konate, Cherki and Doue off, Digne, Upamecano, Barcola and Dembele on for France.

Ollie Watkins replaces Marcus Rashford for England.

England will fly back home tonight with the feel-good factor of a win against a World Cup heavyweight but it would be foolish to think any of Thomas Tuchel’s problems are solved. In fact, Bukayo Saka’s two first-half goals only leads to the question: why was he left on the bench against Argentina? And Ezri Konsa for that matter. England did not lose a game that Konsa started and it was harsh to bench him against Argentina last Wednesday.

No frustration, I’m a little bit emotional, I can’t find the words to describe just how proud I am of these players. They are playing a game with broken hearts, I see 11 lads out there with broken hearts. I’ve seen them around the hotel the last few days, broken hearts. They can build a performance like that just through pride of playing for England, the team spirit we’ve built over the last seven weeks it’s been a privilege to watch. I know the cynics will say it is too late but we still play against a world class opponent.

4 - France have conceded four first half goals for the first time since a EURO qualification match against Yugoslavia in April 1968.WOW. pic.twitter.com/SePSwONNA8

Well, hands up who had this scoreline on their “bronze final” bingo card? A scarcely believable 45 minutes, and England have surely secured third place for this World Cup. There has been a lot to like about their attacking play, but for many it will make the frustration of Argentina sting all the more. France have been half-hearted in their defensive approach, but England have put them to the sword in style.

Just the four minutes of first-half stoppage time to play.

It is not a consequential game, but this is still a heck of a half from England. They are making mincemeat of a ragged France team. Eze with a lovely turn in midfield and through ball to his Arsenal team-mate Saka, and he found the bottom corner with an early finish. Four goals before half time.

🗣 "France are being taken apart by England!" Bukayo Saka scores his second for the Three Lions' FOURTH goal against the two-time world champions 🤯 pic.twitter.com/4RshXY692E

France are playing like they have been on the beach since their semi-final defeat by Spain last Tuesday. Tuchel won’t read too much into England’s best finish at a World Cup since 1966. He wants his team to perform under pressure and there has been none of that in this game.

Almost a fourth for England, Rashford’s low cross seemed to run under Toney’s foot when the striker would have had a tap in. Moments earlier, there was another great defensive recovery from Rice to block a Gusto pass.

Saka with a curling cross which is just beyond Rogers and drifts wide of the far post. France showing no signs of tightening up.

Breaking in behind this France high line has been like shelling peas for England. Saka’s pass initially released Rashford on the break, and he had plenty of time to think when running through on goal. Maignan saved, Saka’s rebound was blocked, but it feel back for Rashford who kept his head and picked out Saka who passed the ball into an unguarded net. Pretty farcical France defending.

That was a very close offside call from VAR for Saka’s goal. With Mike Maignan out of his goal, England needed to stay behind two France defenders. Marcus Rashford was about a foot onside before teeing up the third.

The Three Lions lead France by three goals! 🦁🔥Bukayo Saka finishing off a quick England counter-attack ⚽ pic.twitter.com/9SCfE3uH3v

Good save from Dean Henderson to deny Mbappe, who sat down two England defenders. You were waiting for the net to ripple, but his effort was too close to Henderson.

Then England break and Saka is in behind the France back four again, but his first touch is a little heavy, and he can neither get his shot off nor round Maignan.

England looking lively in attack again, Rashford with a delicious nutmeg on Zaire-Emery, before unleashing a swerving shot from almost 30 yards. Maignan was scrambling but he made the save. Rice then makes another ball recovery in midfield.

There is a bronze medal at stake but this match has the feel of an exhibition. There is no intensity to France’s press. Michael Olise is extremely hard-working usually but has allowed opponents to run past him. Players are only coming alive with the ball at their feet.

Quick feet from Mbappe inside the England box, but Declan Rice was well-positioned to win an important challenge. Half an hour into the game, and Mbappe is yet to nudge ahead of Messi in the Golden Boot race.

Guehi with a goal-line clearance after Mbappe squeezed a shot beyond Henderson, but the flag was up for offside in any case. It looked a close call on the replays, was a clever pass by Doue to find Mbappe. Henderson also did well to get something on the shot.

Play has now resumed, and England are back on the front foot after a Rice diagonal out to Quansah.

Time for the first hydration break of the game. Miami is one of the World Cup venues where it is probably appreciated.

You can only play the game in front of you, but England have done that well so far. They find Toney free in the box, but he cannot get his shot off on the swivel.

Mbappe laughing as we walks back to the halfway line, so France are not feeling too stressed, but England are 2-0 up in Miami. Good inswinging delivery from Rice, and Konsa rose highest on the six-yard line to glance a header into the far corner.

The Three Lions double their lead! 🦁⚽Ezri Konsa rises highest from Declan Rice's corner to head home 🙌 pic.twitter.com/8BfI1LSDOQ

Saka is causing France’s defence all manner of problems, this time Eze released him in behind the French defence. Lacroix did well to stick to his task and deflect Saka’s shot over the bar for a corner.

Marc Guehi sticks out a leg to block Mbappe’s low cross after the French forward dropped a shoulder and showed his burst of speed over a few yards. England defend the corner. The game continues to feel open, there’s more space for the attackers on the pitch than there would be in a semi-final.

Bukayo Saka has the ball in the net but the flag goes up for offside. Correct decision, he had just strayed a yard ahead of Hernandez. It was a crisp finish, cutting back inside and finding the bottom corner with his left foot. England finding it quite easy to get in behind France.

The entertainment continues: Cherki with a strike from the edge of the D, which was parried by Henderson before Spence hurried his clearance. Zaire-Emery picked up the loose ball but could not do enough with it.

He did not know too much about it, but an important recovery run from Spence enables him to get his heel to the ball when it looked like Mbappe was away. England continue to move the ball well, looking quite fluent going forward, which will only serve to frustrate fans further.

England flowing forward again, Saka in behind Hernandez and lifting in a cross that came all the way to Rashford at the far post. One touch to control, the second to shoot, but his effort was blocked, deflected behind for a corner. Rice’s delivery is too deep.

Mbappe with a shot inside the England box but it is blocked by the legs of Rice. This kind of game tends to be either soporific or care-free and entertaining, and it feels like this is going to be the latter.

That was Declan Rice’s first World Cup goal – and a beauty of a strike at that. It is still a strange decision to play him and add to his workload. This is not a game to judge Thomas Tuchel’s team on either, as France are not playing with urgency.

Doue with a sloppy pass across midfield when there was a chance for France to break, and Declan Rice intercepted. No France defender stepped out to engage the Arsenal man, and he was able to carry the ball forward unopposed. The finish was sweet, the ball was passed into the bottom corner from just outside the box.

It's a quick start from England! 🦁⚡Declan Rice fires home the opener in the third minute against France ⚽ pic.twitter.com/ID4u3rXOuM

The early indications are that Eze is playing in a deeper midfield position alongside Rice. Good pass from Dean Henderson into the free man Djed Spece behind France’s press. Then Rashford whips in a promising cross form the left towards Ivan Toney.

As expected, there are a fair few empty seats here. In the end where some England fans seem to be congregated there are blocks of green seats visible from the opposite end of the stadium. It could be quite a strange atmosphere with most of the supporters inside the stadium neutrals. There are a lot of Mexico and Colombia shirts.

For the penultimate time in this tournament, it’s time for the giant flags on the pitch and the anthems. Rice and Mbappe lead out their teams.

Tuchel booed when his name read out and picture shown at the Miami Stadium

This is a big evening for Dean Henderson making his first World Cup appearance. The Crystal Palace goalkeeper, 29, earns his sixth cap and an opportunity to stake his claim for the No1 jersey next season.

No, never [did he hesitate about playing them] because Declan gets more and more fit. He gets his fitness back and his health back and for Bukayo there’s no concerns. He didn’t start, he didn’t play in the semi-finals. He’s a key player for us and ready to go.

It’s just common sense. We have so many kilometres in the legs. We have so many travel kilometres in our bones. We have a day less recovery. We come from 10 men in altitude. We come from overtime here in Miami. These two guys, they gave everything physically in every match,. They were ready to go again but we keep them and have them to finish the match for us.

0 - This is England's first FIFA World Cup campaign to not see a Manchester United player feature in any of their games since 1958.Unused. pic.twitter.com/LN3L3e7q5q

We have to regroup, and we have to pick ourselves up and try to finish the tournament on a high.

I have always been hungry for this opportunity. It was frustrating. I only got a few minutes, but that is how football goes sometimes.

Now is my chance to prove I should have got more minutes. There’s a lot of goals in the team and on the bench.

Hopefully, we can bring goals, and hopefully we can finish the tournament on a win.

Thomas Tuchel has risked angering Arsenal by selecting Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka for this game. Rice has been recovering from illness and was running on empty for the last two games. He has also suffered neural pain in his hamstring and describes himself as playing “an obscene amount of games”. This is surely a chance to have a breather. Saka has been managing an Achilles injury all tournament and did not feature against Argentina on Wednesday.

2 - Declan Rice is the second Arsenal player to start a major tournament game for England as captain (World Cup/EURO) after Tony Adams at EURO 1996.Privilege. pic.twitter.com/MWlX7HiWXX

Seven changes to the team that was beaten by Spain, with Zaire-Emery starting in midfield. Rayan Cherki is preferred to Ousmane Dembele.

France XI: Maignan; T. Hernández, Lacroix, Konate, Gusto; Rabiot, Zaïre-Emery; Doue, Cherki, Olise, Mbappe

Subs: Akliouche, Barcola, Dembele, Digne, L. Hernandez, Kante, Kone, Kounde, Mateta, Risser, Saliba, Samba, Tchouameni, Thuram, Upamecano

Some of Tuchel’s regular starters do drop to the bench: Pickford, Kane and Bellingham the notable names. Slightly surprising that Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka both start given their ongoing niggles. It is a very attacking team with Rice sitting behind Morgan Rogers and Eze. Is Tuchel making a point there?

England XI: D. Henderson; Quansah, Konsa, Guehi, Spence; Rice, Eze; Saka, Rogers, Rashford; Toney

Subs: Pickford, O’Reilly, Stones, Anderson, Kane, Bellingham, Chalobah, J. Henderson, Burn, Gordon, Watkins, Madueke, Trafford, James

Kobbie Mainoo’s back injury means that he not only misses out today, but it also means he ends this World Cup without playing a single minute of the tournament. Ivan Toney gets his first start and you’d imagine Trevoh Chalobah will get off the substitutes’ bench at some stage for his first World Cup minutes. It’s certainly an attacking team, but it’s also a slightly strange one.

Our XI to face France 💪 pic.twitter.com/UexpADmHPr

Matt Law was one of the journalists in Tuchel’s absorbing pre-match press conference, and says he appeared wounded and possibly shaken. Matt writes: “There was some spikiness from Tuchel, when he deflected the odd question back to the reporter who asked it, and he was fidgety when not speaking, messing with the earpiece in front of him on the desk and twisting the wires. He did not look comfortable.”

The Morgan Rogers transfer to Chelsea means that two England players have moved for a British record fee during this World Cup.

Elliot Anderson moved to Manchester City for £116m and Rogers has cost Chelsea £117m. That means England have two players who have moved for a combined £233m during this tournament.

England vice-captain Declan Rice cost Arsenal more than £100m in 2023. I haven’t done the maths, but it’s fair to guess that England’s first-choice starting line up would be worth near enough £1bn.

He takes an excellent set-piece and his athleticism is to be admired, but do you ever see him dictate the tempo of a match in the way that Rodri will attempt to do for Spain when they face Argentina on Sunday in New Jersey? The blunt answer is no. He doesn’t have cute, clever balls in his armoury.

There was a bolt of lightning in the distance on arrival at the Hard Rock Stadium. The last thing this Bronze match needs is a delay to prolong the agony of this match. John Stones was distraught doing his pre-match media duties yesterday. It is harsh to ask players to get themselves up for this game after the devastation of losing to Argentina on Wednesday.

Morgan Rogers is on his way to Chelsea for a record £117m fee, in news which comes as a blow to Arsenal’s summer transfer plans. Rogers started the semi-final on England’s right flank and he is likely to be involved again tonight.

He leaves France having won a World Cup and reached the final in another. This team has arguably played the best football of the lot, but will finish empty-handed. The smart money is on Zinedine Zidane replacing him, who won three consecutive Champions Leagues while Real Madrid head coach. So he knows his way around knockout football.

Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

#2218. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

#2217. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2216. Motherwell boss' ‘Sunday off’ threat revealed after ending seven-game wait

Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson admits he was left to sweat as his side broke a seven-game winless run with a 1-0 win over St Mirren.

Lukas Fadinger rattled home a penalty eight minutes from time to relieve some pressure on the Swede as the Fir Park side climbed into eighth spot in the Willian Hill Premiership table.

Johansson was adamant his team were well worthy of a result, which brought welcome relief to both him and his players.

He said: “Even more than relief, I felt good, happy, joy, determination. This group has done really well lately and I think it’s very well deserved to get the victory and have at least four points from these last two games.

“It’s important to build on it, the most important thing today is that we didn’t give away easy goals or big chances at all.

“We kept St Mirren so quiet and that means for me the way we were fighting in the second half but also how we did the first 60 minutes, how we were defending even before we made the changes.

“I think we were very solid defensively and we were also pressing well, and we were forcing long balls off them. Defensively there was a lot of solidity and that’s something we definitely need to continue to build on.

“Offensively, we still need to improve how we convert those chances and create even more.

“When St Mirren had a late corner I was thinking ‘if we beep this up again, then I don’t know what’s going to happen, the Sunday off will not be a day off, everyone has to come in and defend corner kicks’.

“I haven’t seen the penalty incident, but referees are human and sometimes you get them and sometimes you don’t that’s how it works.”

Saints boss Craig McLeish insists another defeat came down to a lack of belief from his side, who were second best for most of the contest and he believes the penalty call was another bitter blow for St Mirren.

He said: “We’ve not had a good look at the penalty, but the angle from the bench wasn’t great.

“It’s his arm, but it looks like he’s pushed and VAR may have a different angle to the one we have.

“They may not have thought the push was enough, but it’s a frustrating one as we thought we did enough to take a point and we were trying to be tough to break down.

“We need to play with more freedom and maybe there’s a bit of scarring from the recent run we have been on as we didn’t ask enough questions offensively of Motherwell.

“We can’t be relying on clean sheets to pick up points, we need to be a threat, but we will work on that and that is the message, players are getting opportunities and people need to step up.”

#2215. Fan notices something strange about Dave Challinor appointment at Sheffield Wednesday

Sheffield Wednesday's latest era in the dugout is now officially underway after the appointment of Dave Challinor was first confirmed by the Steel City outfit on Sunday ahead of the clash with Blackpool at Hillsborough.

Henrik Pedersen was initially given the opportunity to continue his role as head coach in S6 following the completion of David Storch's long-awaited takeover in May after Wednesday were relegated to League One for the first time in three years.

Despite overseeing a major reshuffle of the squad, the Dane failed to win over sections of the Owls' fanbase, and he was duly dismissed from his role following the 2-0 loss at Doncaster Rovers on October 24th.

Wednesday have since drawn successive home fixtures 1-1 with Cambridge United and the Tangerines, with the last 180 minutes' worth of action overseen by Matt Hamshaw.

Challinor was previously out of work having left Stockport County in the summer, with his last outing in charge of the Hatters being the dismal 4-1 loss to Bolton Wanderers in last season's play-off final.

Supporters in South Yorkshire will be hoping he can go one better with his new employers, although a bizarre coincidence has been noted on social media.

It was reported last month that Challinor, 51, was waiting on a Championship vacancy to become available, or the managerial role at Hillsborough, before considering a swift return to management.

With the latter opportunity arising, it will be the Chester-born man's fifth managerial role, and by far the most pressurised given Wednesday's stature in the EFL as a whole.

The former defender has worked himself up the pyramid to earn such a challenge, with his previous roles coming with Colwyn Bay, AFC Fylde, Hartlepool United and Stockport.

However, an eagle-eyed Owls supporter was glad to see that Challinor wouldn't get his feet under the table in S6 until Monday, with it coincidentally being the third time in his career in which he has started a job on November 2nd.

Sunday's draw led to mixed reviews from Wednesday supporters, largely due to the fact the Owls played the final 60 minutes a man down through Sil Swinkels' red card after Davis Keillor-Dunn gave them the lead on 25 minutes, with ex-Hillsborough man, Jerry Yates, equalising nine minutes from time.

However, some have already set their demands out following the pre-match announcement that Challinor would be taking over.

"Good luck to Dave Challinor at Sheffield Wednesday. His record suggests success at this level and I’m sure he’ll be much better than the last DC we had here," said one Wednesday fan.

"Dave Challinor has a big job on his hands, especially with the club in the middle of a difficult transition period. Patience is key now. This is going to take time to turn around," wrote another supporter.

Former Sheffield Wednesday starlet Josh Windass has reacted to the Owls' impending appointment of Clint Hill alongside Dave Challinor

"Weaver, Lowe, DKD, Slattery and Burstow brilliant today. Ref was shocking. Subs were shocking. Hopefully Challinor brings his own men in now," was another verdict.

Another encouraged Wednesdayite wrote: "Challinor appointment makes sense, knows the league, knows our SD (sporting director) and had Barry purring last season. His next 6 in the league up to Xmas are pivotal IMO. Play some decent sides in and around us. He has a brilliant chance to put a marker down."

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

Challinor has won seven promotions during his managerial career, although given the vast amount of change at Hillsborough in recent times, it may take a while until the signs of an eighth come into view.

That said, he has also won 47 of his 92 regular-season matches in the division, with Stockport finishing inside the play-offs in both of those seasons, and that was certainly the minimum expectation set on Wednesday before a ball was kicked.

Owls fans, what do you make of Dave Challinor's appointment? Comment below!

The new boss doesn't take charge of a league fixture until mid-November against Plymouth Argyle, but could learn very quickly about the capabilities of his squad with clashes against Reading, Oxford United, Leicester City and Luton Town on the horizon afterwards.

#2214. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2212. West Ham identify 3 managers to replace Nuno ft ex-Ipswich Town hero

Speculation and scrutiny surrounding Nuno Espirito Santo's future in charge of West Ham is intensifying following a downturn in recent results, which has led the Hammers to begin running the rule over a number of potential replacements.

West Ham headed into the 2026/27 Championship campaign as overwhelming title favourites after suffering an unprecedented relegation out of the Premier League, bringing their 14 years of uninterrupted top-flight status to an abrupt close.

Retaining the position of Nuno, whose only previous full campaign at this level resulted in a memorable 2017/18 title-winning campaign with Wolves, alongside keeping stars such as Jarrod Bowen, Taty Castellanos and Konstantinos Mavropanos at the London Stadium, only further reinforced those ambitions.

Recent form, however, is suggesting that the East Londoners could end up spending more than one season in the second-tier unless the team's form turns around, with Nuno's side having slumped to successive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion in their last two outings.

The Hammers have fallen to eighth position and are now eight points shy of second-placed Swansea City despite claiming a 1-0 victory in South Wales just over two weeks ago, which has placed increasing pressure on Nuno.

Supporters have rarely been too sold on the Portuguese manager's position, but questions are now being asked from the hierarchy and a new report from Alan Nixon of The Sun - via his Patreon service - has revealed THREE bosses that West Ham have now decided to set their sights on as potential replacements are considered in the event that change occurs in the dugout before long.

The first name to appear on what is described as a "three-man emergency shortlist" of managers to pick from in the near future if Nuno falls short of turning West Ham's fortunes around is that of Kieran McKenna, who remains out of work following his surprise departure from Ipswich Town at the start of the summer.

McKenna achieved his second successive second-tier promotion at Portman Road last season by guiding the Tractor Boys to a second-placed finish behind Frank Lampard's Coventry City, but would decide to walk away in June in order to step back from the game and spend more time with his family.

The 40-year-old had been linked with the Fulham job as a replacement for Marco Silva and was also of interest to Bournemouth before the appointment of Marco Rose, although the Cherries were reportedly deterred by an £8 million compensation figure.

Interestingly, that sum remains at play despite McKenna's departure as Ipswich sought to protect themselves when negotiating his exit, even if reports note that the fee could be knocked down closer to next year's 1 July cut-off point to prevent Town from essentially losing the three-time promotion winner for nothing.

If West Ham want to replace Nuno with McKenna, however, they will have to cough up the cash and would be investing in a young head coach who maintains a glowing reputation for front-footed possession-based football with three promotions - two of them at Championship level - on his CV with some Premier League experience, too.

Scott Parker, meanwhile, is another manager to feature in West Ham's thinking involving life after Nuno, which is becoming an ever-increasing possibility and this particular interest perhaps comes as little surprise owing to the ex-England international's availability and prior Hammers history.

Indeed, many supporters have urged the club to consider returning Parker to management in recent times, with the 46-year-old available after his own exit from Burnley towards the end of the previous campaign.

A proven promotion specialist with heavily-fancied and freshly-relegated Championship squads by this stage, Parker took Fulham back to the Premier League at the first time of asking via the play-offs in his opening full season at Craven Cottage before wrapping up a second-placed finish with Bournemouth behind his former side in the 2021/22 term.

Parker would then repeat the same trick at Burnley two seasons ago by finishing as runners-up behind Daniel Farke's star-studded Leeds United outfit on goal difference, having also amassed no fewer than 100 points.

West Ham United head coach Nuno Espirito Santo has reacted to calls for him to be sacked following Saturday's 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion.

The former Premier League midfielder, who made 126 appearances for West Ham in between spells with Newcastle United and Tottenham Hotspur, has found top-flight management much more difficult, and two of his stints at the top level have resulted in relegations at Fulham and Burnley.

His return to West Ham could just split opinion, too, as while Parker retains plenty of goodwill among supporters, others have never forgiven the manner of his 2011 post-relegation exit to rivals Spurs and will be skeptical of his top-flight managerial record, too.

Parker's body of work at Championship level speaks volumes, though, and Nixon has noted how the 46-year-old is even more ready than McKenna with no compensation-related complications, whereas his history with West Ham means the club's interest in his services would appear to make plenty of sense.

The third and final boss on West Ham's emergency list of replacement candidates comes in the form of Rob Edwards, who, much like both McKenna and Parker, has not managed since last season.

Indeed, Nixon has claimed that sources close to the club are pushing Edwards' name particularly hard and pleading his case to the Hammers' top power-brokers in the event that significant action is taken on Nuno's future, with the former Middlesbrough and Wolves boss clearly having no shortage of admirers at the London Stadium.

Edwards has been linked with a number of jobs following his sacking from Wolves, which abruptly arrived when pre-season preparations and new post-relegation signings were sought in favour of appointing Cesar Peixoto instead.

His time back at Molineux would last just seven months, and with Edwards having been appointed for his Championship pedigree in November of last year when the Old Gold were already cut adrift at the foot of the table without a win from their opening 11 matches, his sacking was widely viewed to be harsh.

Edwards had, however, jumped ship from Middlesbrough, whom he had led on an early-season promotion charge after only taking charge in the previous summer. Naturally, then, Edwards endures a frosty reputation on Teesside, and has dealt with mixed fortunes in recent years.

He first made his name at Forest Green Rovers by winning the 2021/22 League Two title before leaving for Watford, where, like most at Vicarage Road, his tenure was brutally up after a matter of months.

#2210. Simo Valakari’s ‘two men short’ reveal as St Johnstone defy red card

Simo Valakari dedicated St Johnstone’s battling 2-2 draw at Kilmarnock to red-carded goalkeeper Toby Steward.

The on-loan Portsmouth man was dismissed in the 14th minute after misjudging a long ball and handling outside his penalty box.

Saints then twice fell behind to Cathal McCarthy and Djenairo Daniels, but equalised both times with goals from Danny Schmidt and Joel Cotterill to capture an unlikely point.

Substitute goalkeeper Ross Sinclair also made multiple second-half saves to help Saints move up to seventh in the William Hill Premiership.

It was the fourth occasion Valakari’s team has had come from behind to earn a point this season, and the St Johnstone boss said: “Toby has held his hands up and said: ‘I am sorry, boys, for what I did.’

“But our team did it for Toby, the boys did it for Taylor (Steven), who I needed to take out straight away.

“We are all here playing for each other. We have got each other’s backs when things happen. That tells me my players are ready to accept any responsibility.

“Early red card, with Toby that’s my tactical choice. I ask my keeper to play very high, like a ‘sweeper keeper’ for those long balls.

“In those moments, for a year, Toby has been fantastic in clearing the ball, reading the ball. It’s a thin line, a little outside the box, that can happen.”

Valakari made his fifth and final substitution – Dan Finlayson for Bozo Mikulic – immediately after Cotterill’s 65th-minute equaliser.

German forward Schmidt then suffered an ankle injury but hobbled bravely on to complete the game and prevent Saints finishing with nine men.

Valakari said: “Because of my substitutions we didn’t have anyone left.

“When Danny played the last 20 minutes, he couldn’t move so we basically played two men short.

“If I had another sub, Danny would’ve come off, his ankle is in a horrible state. But he was there, still fighting with the centre-backs and doing anything he could for the team.”

The point saw Killie inch above Hibernian at the bottom of the table but that did not spare manager Neil McCann the fury of the home fans at the end.

McCann said: “The quality evaded us. We’re in a 2-1 lead and we concede from our set-piece – that’s not good enough against 10 men.

“It’s really painful because we do a lot of work on set-pieces. It feels like a defeat. Even though we’ve taken a point, it’s like we’ve thrown away two.

“I completely understand why the fans are angry because I am too. We had lots of control in the game but that Achilles heel of chucking up soft goals is something that’s plaguing us right now.”

#2209. Why must Manchester United move beyond the Glazers?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Glazers took control of Manchester United in 2005. That takeover has since caused so many disruptions and protests by the fans over massive debts and insufficient backing of the team in the transfer market, despite successful periods in the Premier League and Europe.

Now Manchester United need to think about who should control the club in the future. Laurie Whitwell has now shared his views on why Manchester United need an ownership change. He simply wants the Glazers gone from Old Trafford. However, he also recognizes that replacing the current ownership doesn’t automatically mean things will improve for United.

The journalist believes the change in ownership has had a lasting effect on United, with the club still feeling its consequences today. A fresh start might be welcome, but the identity of the next owners would matter just as much as the departure of the existing ones.

“Personally, I would like to see the Glazers gone from Manchester United,” Laurie Whitwell said on The Rest is Football podcast with Gary Lineker.

“That change, you know, just really affected and still impacts United now.”

The desire for different ownership is one thing, but finding people capable of taking the club forward is another.

Whitwell admitted there is no perfect answer when it comes to who should take charge.

That leaves United facing a difficult choice. A sale could offer the chance to change how the club is run, but simply bringing in a new owner would not guarantee better decisions or a brighter future.

Whitwell also raised the idea of United supporters having a greater say in the club’s ownership and decisions, much like the Barcelona model where fans own the club itself. However, he highlighted that the Barcelona model isn’t ideal either and has its own shortcomings.

Changing the names at the top would only be one part of the change. The club would also need an ownership structure capable of making sound decisions and providing a direction.

The issue of ownership goes beyond whether the Glazers should stay or leave. Manchester United needs to find the right people and the right model to secure the club’s future. Getting that decision wrong could leave them facing the same circus the fans are enduring under the Glazers.

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

The Argentinian defender has also apologized to the United higher ups as well over his comments, as shared by Fabrizio Romano.

Lisandro Martinez has held discussions with Jason Wilcox and Michael Carrick after speaking out following United’s 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Martinez had questioned whether Carrick was backed enough in the summer and suggested the club needed changes.

Fabrizio Romano has now confirmed that United consider the matter resolved for now and expect Martinez to remain available for selection.

Speaking about the situation on his YouTube channel, as quoted by Football 365, Romano explained why Martinez’s comments caused concern inside the club.

“He spoke very strongly after the game against Atletico Madrid, which Man Utd lost. It was a very negative moment for the Red Devils. We know that Licha was very strong in his comments. He said that Michael Carrick was not backed enough during the summer transfer window.”

Romano added that Martinez had spoken directly to those at the club after the incident.

“Licha apologised to Man Utd as a club. He spoke to the directors, he spoke to Jason Wilcox, and he spoke to Michael Carrick, who was also involved in this conversation.”

“So, the underlying message remains the same. Lisandro is apologising for the way he expressed himself after a game during a difficult moment for Man Utd, but there was a discussion about the substance of what he said.”

Romano also revealed that United had imposed a financial penalty on the centre-back. However, the punishment does not appear to involve removing him from the squad.

“According to the information available tonight, Lisandro Martinez has been fined.”
