#2191. Danny Drinkwater on Chelsea move he ‘could never turn down’

The Danny Drinkwater Chelsea story still carries a sting. Five years at Stamford Bridge gave him plenty of time to think about how it all turned out, and his own verdict is not a happy one.

Drinkwater opened up in a Truth or Padel appearance alongside David Ornstein. He said the move was one he could never have turned down, even with the benefit of hindsight. “No, I don’t regret moving. I regret, in hindsight, how it’s turned out. I think I could never turn it down,” he said.

Strip away the headlines and the numbers alone tell an uncomfortable story. Drinkwater spent five years on Chelsea’s books. In that time he made just 23 appearances, according to the original interview report.

Do the maths and it barely comes to five games a year. That is a thin return for a central midfielder signed to compete for a first-team place. It is also the kind of record that rarely sits well at a club of Chelsea’s size and ambition.

Chelsea’s best attacking spells over a similar stretch of seasons look far more productive, as our striker rankings show. Set next to those numbers, Drinkwater’s five quiet years stand out even more starkly.

Five years. Twenty three games. These numbers alone explains why this transfer still gets talked about by Drinkwater, long after the headlines faded.

The numbers only tell part of the story. A string of incidents turned a quiet, underwhelming spell into something far more pointed.

Drinkwater had a training-ground bust-up while out on loan. He was also involved in an on-pitch brawl with Chelsea’s own under-23s side. Flashpoints between a first-team player and a development squad are rare at any club, let alone one with Chelsea’s standards.

Taken alone, either incident might have passed as a bad day. Taken together, it became harder to see Drinkwater simply as an unlucky squad player who could not catch a break.

The most serious moment came during his time at Aston Villa. Drinkwater headbutted team-mate Jota and was fined two weeks’ wages for it. He says the consequences at Chelsea did not stop there.

“They didn’t formally ban me, but I got removed from the first team building after the incident at Villa,” Drinkwater said.

One off-field incident, at another club, pushed him out of the manager’s day-to-day plans back home. No formal punishment at Chelsea followed. The effect was much the same.

Chelsea fans saw a similar breakdown of trust play out when Graham Potter struggled to win over the dressing room during another difficult Chelsea transition. Trust can break down fast once results or behaviour turn against the person at the centre of it.

Drinkwater’s comments matter beyond his own career. They are a reminder that saying yes to a big move does not guarantee it will work once a player walks through the door.

That tension has not gone away. Chelsea’s current transfer business, covered in our transfer watch, shows the club still weighing big calls on players whose futures depend on more than form alone.

Squad management under Xabi Alonso, assessed in our bomb squad verdict, raises a familiar issue. Players who fall outside a manager’s plans rarely find a quick way back in, whether the exile is formal or not.

Drinkwater never found his way back into Chelsea’s plans after the Villa incident. His account of the Danny Drinkwater Chelsea years stands as a blunt warning. A move that looks impossible to refuse can still become one of the hardest spells of a career.

#2190. Arsenal Women v Tottenham: Stanway Strikes as Arsenal Women and Spurs Level in North London Derby

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women v Tottenham: Georgia Stanway has dragged Arsenal Women back into the north London derby. She hit a fierce 17th-minute equaliser at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, her first WSL goal for the club. The match is under way, and the score is 1-1.

Renée Slegers made bold changes for the trip across north London. Ona Batlle, Stina Blackstenius and Lotte Wubben-Moy dropped to the bench. Steph Catley, Taylor Hinds and Caitlin Foord all came into the side.

Misa started in goal. Emily Fox, Captain Leah Williamson, Catley and Hinds formed the back four. Stanway and Kyra Cooney-Cross played in midfield. Lisa Baum and Foord took the wings.

Alessia Russo played in a deeper role behind Olivia Smith. It was a roll of the dice. Russo scored a hat trick in the last derby in March, a 5-2 win.

The visitors got off to a strong start, but Stanway stepped up. She put it into the back of the net after a great lead up from Russo. Despite a brave effort by Lize Kop, the ball flew into the net.

“It was a perfect response from Arsenal. Stanway has been scoring for her country recently so it’s nice to see that quality come through at club level,” said Sky Sports pundit Callum Bishop.

Arsenal arrived in poor form. They had won just one of their six WSL games and sat eighth with six points. That win came on the opening day against Brighton.

A 1-1 draw with newly promoted Birmingham last weekend made it five league games without a win. That is a first for the club in the WSL. Olivia Smith rescued a point that day with a fine second-half strike.

Arsenal were also 12 points behind leaders Manchester City. Slegers faced questions about her future and gave little away. “At the moment, I’m not looking at the table,” she said. She added that the motivation in her squad was sky high.

Tottenham started fourth on 10 points. It was the first time they had begun a WSL north London derby above Arsenal.

Their form was shaky, though. Spurs lost 6-1 to London City Lionesses and then 6-2 at Chelsea.

History favours the visitors. Arsenal have won 10 of the 13 WSL derbies, with two draws and one defeat. That defeat came in December 2023, when Martha Thomas scored the only goal at this ground. Last season’s meeting here finished 0-0.

#2189. Rangers 1 Aberdeen 0: Gers into final as Naderi pops up to break Dons hearts

A late Ryan Naderi goal broke Aberdeen hearts and resistance as Rangers booked their place in the Premier Sports cup final after a hard-fought encounter at Hampden.

The Dons were in disarray and hugely unfancied heading into this clash, but they fought gamely and frustrated Rangers for long spells at the national stadium. Just as they looked to be heading towards extra-time at worst though, Naderi popped up with an opportunistic finish to ensure Derek McInnes and his men will be back in Mount Florida on December 13th to face either Hearts or Hibs for the first silverware of the season.

Here are the talking points from Hampden…

The injuries to Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti were a huge blow to Rangers when they occurred, but the supporting cast have more than stepped up to the plate in their absence. In fact, the partnership of Naderi and Kevin Kelsy may take some shifting.

Naderi’s winner here was his eighth goal of the season, while Kelsy has five in his last five starts, and he too more than played his part in constructing the move that led to the critical moment of the match, carrying the ball up the pitch on the counter after an Aberdeen attack.

The pair combined well for the Rangers opener at Tynecastle on Wednesday, too, and the imminent return of Shankland will give McInnes a welcome headache when it comes to the make-up of his attack.

Electric Badredine Bouanani lights up Hampden

The decision to leave Bouanani out of the starting line-up in favour of Djeidi Gassama for the game at Tynecastle was a puzzling one at the time, and he was never in any danger of being left out here.

If anyone was going to unlock the door for Rangers, it appeared the exciting winger was the best bet. He did everything but score himself, in fact, particularly in the second half as Aberdeen dropped deeper and deeper, flashing a couple of brilliant efforts just past the far post and being denied by a goal line block from Nicky Devlin after twisting and turning two Dons defenders inside out in the area.

In the end, others eventually stepped up to the plate for Rangers, but it was Bouanani who again caught the eye.

Aberdeen stretched to the limit, but fighting for their manager

The Dons limped into this contest both figuratively in terms of their form and literally in terms of their injury list, missing four centre backs – one through suspension - and their starting right back, though at least their manager could call on the experience of Devlin.

Both he and Emmanuel Gyamfi made their first starts of the season, as Robinson somehow constructed a solid base to build from. The last thing that the Dons gaffer needed was any further injury woes in-game, but it seems as though he is slap bang in the never raining but it pours period of his Pittodrie tenure. Gyamfi lasted all of 13 minutes, stumbling and collapsing into Kim Minsu as he pursued the Rangers winger down the line, injuring his knee in the process.

The early reshuffle saw Stuart Armstrong coming into the centre of the park and Brad Lyons shunted out to the right, but the Dons remained impressively organised and stout in their defending.

For all that Robinson has been under severe pressure, and looked a broken man after the midweek defeat at home to Falkirk, he managed to rouse a huge effort from his men here, and reports of his Pittodrie demise may well yet be premature on this evidence.

At the death, they almost hauled themselves off the canvas as Armstrong curled just wide, but while that wasn’t to be, there were signs of life in this performance that have been few and far between of late.

Square pegs in round holes as McInnes tries to fit in best players

It was something of an eyebrow raiser when the team-lines dropped and two left backs in James Penrice and Tuur Rommens were included in McInnes’s starting XI, with Penrice moving from his hybrid full-back/midfield role into the middle of the park on a full-time basis.

A penny for the thoughts of Tochi Chukwuani and Vanja Dragojevic, who were left kicking their heels on the bench despite their manager’s decision to give captain Dan Neil a rest from the start of the game.

How much that decision affected Rangers is open to debate, but what isn’t in question is that the men in blue struggled to find their rhythm or any real attacking impetus despite plenty of the ball in a stuffy opening hour.

A manager will never complain about having too many good players at his disposal, but it will be a conundrum for McInnes going forward as to how he gets his preferred personnel into his team.

Perhaps it is indicative of how little goalmouth action there was in a drab first half that the big talking points centred around potential penalties for handball, with incidents at either end that you may have thought would catch the attention of John Beaton and Chris Graham in the VAR room.

The first looked the stronger claim, with the ball making contact with the outstretched arm of Aberdeen striker Ayoub Mouloua in his own box, but referee Ryan Lee saw nothing amiss, and he wasn’t invited over to the pitchside screen for another look. It may well have been the proximity of the players directly in front of Mouloua as he was caught under the cross that saved his skin.

Aberdeen had a spot-kick shout of their own as Dujon Sterling missed a header and the ball carried on down to make contact with his arm, but in fairness to the Rangers defender, his arm did appear to be in a natural position.

The fact that we have seen penalties awarded for comparable incidents to these in the past maybe says more about the mess that has been made of the handball rule than pointing to obvious errors from the officials here, mind you.

#2188. Arsenal v Everton preview: depleted champions look to extend dominance over the Toffees

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal host Everton at the Emirates Stadium today with Bukayo Saka missing and a point to prove after a bruising midweek in Munich. The Premier League champions sit second in the table. A stuttering Everton arrives looking for a response to their first defeat of the season.

Mikel Arteta’s side have started the campaign strongly, collecting 18 points from their opening seven league games. They beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 in their last league outing. Bouncing back from a defeat at Brighton before the international break with a four-game unbeaten run.

Arsenal extended their winning streak on Wednesday with a hard-fought 2-2 draw against Bayern Munich in the Champions League. Saka went off injured with a muscular injury in the first ten minutes at the Allianz Arena.

The extent of his injury is still to be determined. Bruno Guimaraes made his first appearance of the season for Arsenal after being signed in the summer from Newcastle United. He played in midfield alongside Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard.

Saka will be missing, but so will William Saliba as he continues his recovery from a back complaint. Christos Tzolis has a hamstring injury to overcome. The good news, however, is that Piero Hincapie has recovered from his ankle injury and is back in contention.

With the third game in six days, Arteta may try to bring some fresh faces into midfield and attack with Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke to choose from.

Everton made a perfect start to the season, but Chelsea brought their run to an end last week with a 2-0 win at the Hill Dickinson Stadium. Pedro Neto scored both goals. David Moyes admitted afterwards that his side offered little attacking threat, managing just six shots on target.

The Toffees are sitting on 10 points from 7 games after starting the weekend in 8th. They’ve had a very draw-heavy start to the season with 4 draws in 7 games. However, they do have two familiar faces in their squad, as Christian Norgaard and Ainsley Maitland-Niles are both ex-Arsenal players.

History is firmly on Arsenal’s side. Everton have not beaten them in the league since February 2023, and Arsenal are unbeaten in their last seven league meetings between the sides. Their most recent home meeting ended 2-0 in March 2026.

Arsenal will be expected to dominate possession and territory against an Everton side who will probably sit deep and look to counter. Moyes has a habit of making his sides difficult to beat, as those four draws show. They have yet to win away from home this season. For Arsenal, anything less than three points would be a setback in the title race.

#2187. Keira Walsh adds another Chelsea weapon as former Arsenal target scores THIRD goal of the season

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Keira Walsh is giving Chelsea opponents another decision to make: protect the penalty area or step out to stop her shooting.

Her goal in Sunday’s 3-0 victory at West Ham took her to three for the season across all competitions. Each has come from outside the box.

For a player whose passing helps organise Chelsea’s attacks, that threat adds another way to influence matches. Recent performances show her contributing both to the construction of chances and their finish.

Against Sociedad, Walsh struck from distance after a corner, helping Chelsea complete their passage into the Champions League’s league phase.

The club’s account of that qualifying victory describes a tight encounter in which clear opportunities were limited.

At Manchester United, Lucy Bronze found her near the edge of the box and Walsh drove her finish into the bottom corner.

She also supplied Lauren James’ goal that afternoon, as Chelsea’s match report records. It was a useful illustration of the choices she offers: attempt the finish herself or release somebody closer to goal.

West Ham provided another example of that balance.

Walsh had already struck the post before Alyssa Thompson carried the ball in from the left and found Wieke Kaptein. Kaptein moved it on to Walsh, whose finish gave Chelsea breathing space.

The official report also records an earlier Walsh run down the channel and delivery towards Sjoeke Nüsken.

Her involvement therefore extended beyond waiting for opportunities to shoot. She helped Chelsea approach the penalty area from different positions.

There was a similar reward against Arsenal a week earlier. Walsh’s saved effort fell to Thompson for the only goal, as covered in our report of Chelsea’s derby victory.

That sequence illustrates why a dangerous shot can matter even when the goalkeeper stops it. Chelsea had a runner ready to attack the rebound.

Our assessment is that Walsh’s shooting gives defenders an additional problem. Closing her down can open a passing route; allowing her time leaves the goalkeeper exposed to a player already finding her range.

Walsh has also explained why she feels comfortable alongside Potter.

Speaking after the Arsenal victory in an interview published by Chelsea, she said:

“Lexi is really intelligent. She makes me feel really comfortable when I’m playing next to her.”

Her wider assessment emphasised collective responsibility, with team-mates covering for each other and working to make Chelsea harder to beat.

That matters when assessing midfield influence. Walsh’s freedom to help an attack depends partly on the positioning and decisions of those around her.

Potter subsequently started alongside her in Chelsea’s confirmed team against Lyon, giving their partnership another demanding European assignment.

The encouraging feature is the trust Walsh describes. Bompastor has an experienced organiser working with a younger midfielder whose reading of the game she clearly values.

BBC Sport reported that Barcelona rejected Arsenal’s bid for Walsh in September 2024.

Chelsea completed her signing in January 2025 on a four-and-a-half-year contract. Her official club profile outlines the technical quality and ability to dictate tempo that underpinned that recruitment.

Those qualities remain central to her value. Three early goals strengthen the attacking contribution around them, without establishing that she has changed position or should abandon her deeper responsibilities.

For Bompastor, the opportunity is to preserve that balance: Walsh helping Chelsea progress through midfield, supporting those around her and recognising when the space opens for a finish.

#2186. Russo penalty settles scrappy derby as Arsenal end winless run at Spurs

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Tottenham 1-2 Arsenal | Barclays Women’s Super League | Tottenham Hotspur Stadium | Saturday 24 October 2026

Arsenal ended a five-match winless league run in the most satisfying setting imaginable, with Alessia Russo’s second-half penalty sealing a 2-1 North London derby victory at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

Renée Slegers’ team entered the match having failed to win in the league in their past five games, which is a new record for them in the WSL.

They were also sitting in fourth place ahead of their opponents going into the game, which has not happened before in a WSL derby.

Slegers made three changes to her starting line-up, with Steph Catley, Taylor Hinds, and Caitlin Foord coming into the side.

Ona Batlle, Stina Blackstenius and Lotte Wubben-Moy were left on the bench. Russo came into the game playing behind Olivia Smith after scoring a hat-trick in the 5-2 victory in March.

The early signs were ominous. Martin Ho’s hosts, still smarting from a 6-2 defeat at Chelsea, struck first in 13 minutes. Victoria Pelova swung over a corner, Cathinka Tandberg rose above Catley to head in, and Leah Williamson could not keep it out on the line.

They responded quickly; however, as Hinds played the ball into the path of Russo on the left side of the box, four minutes later. She played a low cross to Stanway, who powered her shot past Kop. Kop got a hand to the shot but couldn’t keep it out. It was her first WSL goal for the club, and the remainder of the half was a tense, niggly affair, with the game levelling out at 1-1.

The second half began with a blow for the hosts, as Alice Sombath was forced off injured and replaced by Ellia Morris. Arsenal gradually took control, and Kop twice denied Russo, palming away one first-time effort and then blocking another from close range.

After 56 minutes, Lisa Baum fired against the post, following a flick-on from Williamson. A desperate clearance from Tandberg was caught by Morris’ raised arm, and the referee called for the penalty to be awarded. The composed Russo, who had already provided the equaliser, calmly put it into the back of the net to win the game.

Arsenal finished with 14 shots to Spurs’ five, 11 of them inside the box to the hosts’ two, and an expected goals total of 2.24 to 0.30, according to FotMob. Tandberg’s header was Tottenham’s only effort on target. Pelova was the home side’s best player, but Spurs could not rediscover their early spark.

The contest grew increasingly bad-tempered, with Stanway and Kyra Cooney-Cross both booked and Tottenham committing 15 fouls to Arsenal’s eight. Ho introduced Kirsty Hanson, Shekiera Martinez and Olivia Holdt in search of an equaliser, while Slegers brought on Batlle, Élisa de Almeida, Blackstenius and Smilla Holmberg to help see out seven minutes of added time.

For Slegers, the result stops the slide. It follows draws with Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Birmingham City, and defeats at Chelsea and Manchester City. Arsenal began the day eighth on six points and now have nine.

Next up is the Champions League, with Benfica visiting on Wednesday, before Aston Villa arrive in the WSL on 1 November.

Graduate Sports Journalist with a love for football.

Chelsea target Alex Scott has withdrawn from England duty with an injury that threatens his involvement in Bournemouth’s visit to Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

England confirmed on Monday morning that Scott had returned to his club for further assessment and would miss Tuesday’s Nations League match against Czechia.

Sky Sports reports a tendon injury, with initial indications suggesting an absence of several weeks. Further scans are planned.

Bournemouth face Chelsea on 10 October, the first game in the Blues’ run of fixtures after the international break.

The injury comes after fresh reporting on Chelsea’s continuing interest in Scott, following rejected summer bids thought to exceed £60million.

#2184. Arsenal 2-0 Everton: Gabriel seals a comfortable victory as Gunners join Man City at the top

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal vs Everton: Arsenal capitalised on Manchester City’s defeat against Aston Villa with a convincing 2-0 victory over Everton at the Emirates Stadium on Saturday.

Ezri Konsa gave Arsenal the lead in the seventh minute before Gabriel Magalhães scored a header to put them two up after the break and earn Mikel Arteta’s side three crucial points in the Premier League.

The Arsenal vs Everton win brings them level at 21 points with City at the top of the table. They showed a positive response to their 2-2 Champions League draw with Bayern Munich on Wednesday by dominating and keeping Everton from threatening their goal.

Arsenal wasted little time taking control, breaking the deadlock in the seventh minute following their third consecutive corner.

A goalmouth scramble ended with Konsa getting the final touch, giving the hosts an early advantage and scoring their first corner-kick goal of the season.

Everton applied some early pressure and played some good football after some sloppy Arsenal play in wet conditions, but they quickly got back into their rhythm.

Eberechi Eze could not take his chance; Noni Madueke hit two great chances off target, and Mikel Merino had an excellent chance blocked, then headed over from a set piece.

Arsenal controlled the first half and had plenty of chances to increase their lead but could not do so, which allowed Everton to stay in the game.

Thierno Barry almost took advantage of a defensive error after he won the ball off a mis-hit header from Ben White, but the Arsenal goalkeeper put in an incredible save to keep the lead.

Despite that scare, Arsenal entered half-time firmly in control and looking more likely than ever to score again.

Arsenal carried on where they left off, asserting control of the ball, and looked to add a second goal to make it safe.

A moment of concern arose when Gabriel took a clumsy tumble to the ground and quickly flagged to the ref. Fortunately for Arteta, the Brazilian had jarred his right knee on the floor but was well enough to continue playing.

His afternoon took a much happier turn in the 69th minute.

White provided a superb cross from the right which found the run of Gabriel, who headed the ball into the net from the opposite end of the box to give Arsenal a two-goal lead. He scored to the delight of the Emirates fans.

Gabriel’s 200th Premier League appearance for Arsenal was a thing to behold as he scored the vital second goal to help his team keep a clean sheet.

Everton struggled to get back into the game in the final stages, and they were restricted by Arsenal’s solid backline.

The closest they came to changing the scoreline was Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, who headed just off target. Hayden Hackney had a long-range shot but was comfortably dealt with by Raya.

They held on for the remainder of the game to give a professional display that put them in a strong position in the title race.

Arteta’s team took the chance to level up after City’s early setback.

The Gunners will now look ahead to their League Cup clash with Fleetwood Town before facing Liverpool at Anfield next weekend. With momentum building, the Gunners will hope this result provides another foundation for their title challenge.

#2182. Arsenal vs Fleetwood Town: Match preview, team news and confirmed line-ups

Lucie is a sports writer and lifelong fan with a true passion for rugby, snooker, darts, Formula 1 and, of course, football. A devoted Arsenal supporter for many years and a self-confessed Gooner, she is never far from the Emirates action, whether she’s dissecting a tactical shift or celebrating a late winner. Her work covers match previews, results, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces, bringing a fan’s passion and a journalist’s eye for detail to every story.

Arsenal travel to Fleetwood Town tonight for their Carabao Cup fourth-round tie, with Mikel Arteta making nine changes to his starting XI. The Gunners will aim to reach the quarter-finals for the third consecutive year when they face the League Two side at Highbury Stadium.

The match kicks off at 8pm, with Arsenal looking to continue their cup run against lower-league opposition.

Fleetwood have reached the fourth round after beating Chesterfield, Shrewsbury Town and Championship side Sheffield United. An own goal from Rhys Norrington-Davies helped them secure their place in the last 16.

However, Fleetwood have won just three matches this season and only one of their last eight. They have kept clean sheets throughout their Carabao Cup run, though, and will hope to make life difficult for the visitors.

Arsenal have a good record against fourth tier opposition. They have won eight of nine previous games against such teams. The only time they have failed to move forward was against Bradford City in 2012, where they were defeated on penalties after a 1-1 draw.

Arteta has placed great emphasis on showing respect for Fleetwood but also ensuring the Gunners play to their usual high standards. Matt Lawlor has been encouraging his players to enjoy the occasion and not be overwhelmed by a bigger opposition team.

Arteta has made nine changes for the trip to Fleetwood, with goalkeeper Illan Meslier and 18-year-old Ceadach O’Neill making their Arsenal debuts.

Meslier, who joined the club in the summer, starts in goal. Jurrien Timber plays at right-back, with Marli Salmon, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie completing the defence.

Martin Zubimendi partners Myles Lewis-Skelly in midfield. Max Dowman starts on one wing, with debutant O’Neill on the opposite flank. Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyokeres complete the starting XI.

Dowman comes into the game having netted twice against Ipswich Town in the last round and will be hoping to put in another man of the match display to help Arsenal through to the quarter-finals.

Arsenal confirmed the starting XI: Meslier, Timber, Salmon, Mosquera, Hincapie, Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly, Dowman, O’Neill, Havertz, and Gyokeres.

Substitutes: Arrizabalaga, White, Odegaard, Eze, Konsa, Guimaraes, Harriman-Annous, Washington, Hashi.

Andy Cannon is back in training and will be available for selection for Fleetwood. However, Lawlor will look to manage his minutes. Finley Potter is also available, but Kane Thompson-Sommers and Will Johnson are both injured and unavailable.

Eberechi Eze is one of Arsenal’s impact subs, having played a part in seven goals in his last four appearances in the League Cup against non-Premier League opposition. He has scored twice and created five goals.

Dowman is another one to look out for after his performance against Ipswich. The 16-year-old scored twice in the last round and will be looking to build on that.

Fleetwood could be a threat with their high press and set pieces. Mark Helm has created the most chances with 23, but their attacking trio of Ronan Coughlan and Ched Evans could cause problems.

The game will be played at Highbury Stadium and kick off at 8pm UK time. It’ll be broadcast live on Sky Sports Main Event.

If the scores are tied after 90 minutes, the game will go straight to penalties. The Carabao Cup Quarter Final draw will take place on Wednesday evening.

We’ll have a full match report for you once the game has finished.

Morgan Rogers struggled to establish himself at Bournemouth because the role envisaged for him did not fit the team’s usual setup, according to former Cherries scout Des Taylor.

#2180. Arsenal vs Fleetwood Town Match Report: Arsenal crash out of Carabao Cup after Fleetwood Town win on penalties

Lucie is a sports writer and lifelong fan with a true passion for rugby, snooker, darts, Formula 1 and, of course, football. A devoted Arsenal supporter for many years and a self-confessed Gooner, she is never far from the Emirates action, whether she’s dissecting a tactical shift or celebrating a late winner. Her work covers match previews, results, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces, bringing a fan’s passion and a journalist’s eye for detail to every story.

Arsenal vs Fleetwood Town: Arsenal suffered a stunning Carabao Cup exit as League Two Fleetwood Town secured a memorable 5-3 penalty shootout victory after a 1-1 draw at Highbury Stadium.

Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave the hosts a shock first-half lead before Viktor Gyökeres equalised after the break. However, Max Dowman’s late red card added to Arsenal’s problems before Bruno Guimarães missed from the spot to send Fleetwood into the quarter-finals.

The result marks a remarkable achievement for Fleetwood, who sit several divisions below their Premier League opponents.

The match got off to an unusual start when an unauthorised drone flew over the stadium, forcing referee Michael Salisbury to stop play. Both teams left the pitch during an interruption of around eight minutes before the match resumed.

Fleetwood capitalised on the occasion and took the lead in the 21st minute. Aaron Loupalo-Bi got past young Arsenal defender Marli Salmon before sending a low finish across debutant goalkeeper Illan Meslier and into the net.

Arsenal had a tough time trying to break down the Fleetwood backline. Max Dowman looked to get Arsenal onto the front foot, but the hosts were solid and kept the lead.

The League Two side was ahead at the break, and Arsenal had to work hard to avoid embarrassment.

Mikel Arteta brought on Martin Ødegaard at the break, and the visitors began to push Arsenal on the counter. They scored an equaliser five minutes into the second half.

Gyökeres scored with a tap in to make it 1-1 to give some momentum to Arsenal, but Fleetwood defended well.

In the second half the Gunners looked like they would win the game, however Jay Lynch made a crucial save to stop Ben White scoring.

Despite Arsenal’s attempts to find a breakthrough, neither side managed to score again during normal time.

Arsenal were made to work harder in the 85th minute when Dowman was shown a straight red card after kicking out at an opponent. The dismissal of the 16-year-old meant Arteta’s side had to play the final stages of the game down a man.

With the score still level, the tie went straight to a penalty shootout. Ødegaard, Havertz and Gyökeres converted their efforts for Arsenal, but Fleetwood goalkeeper Lynch saved Guimarães’ penalty.

Fleetwood showed no signs of pressure as they scored all five of their penalties. Conor Haughey scored the winning penalty to give Fleetwood a 5-3 win, and celebrations broke out among the home fans.

Fleetwood will be playing in the Carabao Cup quarter-final after one of the greatest upsets of the competition, while it means an end to Arsenal’s hopes of making it through to the last eight for the third year running.

A vastly changed Arteta side will look to recover from a frustrating night in Lancashire, while Fleetwood can revel in their historic win over a premiership side.

#2178. West Ham v West Bromwich Albion | Nuno goes all-in to avoid terrible ten

Match-day morning in the championship. West Ham host play-off challengers West Bromwich Albion in a battle of two sides with dreadful records for going behind in matches. The Hammers with nine games already this season have one of the worst records in the league for gifting their opponents a head start, and today’s visitors find themselves on a run of six consecutive games of going behind.

The return of ‘clean sheet Mads’? If only.

Nuno has already made it clear that he’s trying to address the trend, as per his insistence back on 9th October:

“When you look back, you say we have to fix it urgently; we have to start the games better. We have to start games and sustain the level of performance”… was met with two clean sheets, but then a relapse last weekend and three first half goals conceded.

“Of the 20 goals the Irons have conceded in all competitions, 15 of them have come in the first half of games, and they only remain in the mix at the top because they have scored 20 of the club record-equalling 32 league goals after half-time.

They are consistently having to chase the game, and the trend shows no signs of letting up.”

Stop giving opponents a head start and, in effect, Nuno can fix West Ham’s promotion challenge.

It won’t get any easier than today against the other ‘worst side in the league’ for going behind. London Stadium’s sixty thousand will be only too aware of the Irons’ nasty little habit and will respond in traditional style – as they did last weekend –  if a tenth first-half goal slips through the hapless Hammers defence.

How about playing the game in your opponents half, Nuno. It’s mighty tough for the opposition to score if the ball stays 50 yards away from Mads Hermansen’s goal.

Revolutionary thinking, I know. 3pm this afternoon and we’ll judge the manager’s renewed efforts to get our team playing on the front foot.

#2176. Fleetwood 1-1 Arsenal (5-3 penalties): Gunners knocked out of Carabao Cup as Max Dowman is sent off

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal suffered a stunning Carabao Cup exit. They lost on penalties to League Two side Fleetwood Town 5-3 in the fourth round at Highbury Stadium. A 1-1 draw meant Arsenal had to go to penalties. Teenager Max Dowman was sent off five minutes from the end of the game.

Fleetwood, in 18th place in League Two, took an early lead, but Viktor Gyokeres scored his first goal of the season to bring them level. However, neither team could find a winning goal. Fleetwood held their composure to win the penalty shootout after Bruno Guimaraes missed his spot-kick. The game was also paused for two minutes due to a drone flying around the ground.

Despite a heavy rotation by Mikel Arteta, Kai Havertz, Gyokeres, Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Jurrien Timber all started. Martin Odegaard and Ben White were brought on during the half-time break, followed by Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa and Eberechi Eze. But overall the Evening Standard said Arsenal put in an “incredibly bad performance” over the course of the 90 minutes.

Dowman, 16, had been among Arsenal’s better players, creating chances for Havertz and Timber with dangerous crosses. He was shown a straight red card after reacting angrily to a heavy challenge from Harrison Neal and kicking out at the defender, though the force was minimal. It was his second red card this month, after a dismissal for the England Under-19s.

As Dowman walked off, Arteta was seen leaning towards him and delivering furious words. Asked what he said, the Arsenal manager told BBC Radio 5 Live it was “something that we discussed already before the match”. Suggesting the teenager had been warned to expect rough treatment. Arteta said he had not seen the red card back and that the referee’s decision stood. Sky Sports pundit Paul Merson was critical of how the Arsenal boss reacted to Dowman.

Arteta congratulated Fleetwood Town on the atmosphere they created. He said he could not fault his players’ attitude and intensity, with 11 men or 10. “When we create the volume of shots and chances we did, you have to score three, four or five,” he said. He added that even with ten men Arsenal had three big chances.

He called the unpredictability of cup football part of English football’s history, saying Arsenal were “extremely sad” to be on the wrong side of it.

Several squad members were absent. Riccardo Calafiori was out, and Noni Madueke had an ankle problem. Declan Rice was substituted in the previous game because of a concern.

Arsenal’s Carabao Cup dream of a first League Cup win since 1993 is over. Attention now turns to a huge Premier League trip to Anfield to face Liverpool on Sunday. Fleetwood, meanwhile, can celebrate a famous giant-killing and wait for the quarter-final draw.

#2175. Mason Mount offering Michael Carrick a midfield solution which could have legs

It is not uncommon to hear football club executives talking about the importance of the “money being on the pitch”.

In other words, managers having their best players fit and available most if not all of the time. Quality at the top level is essential but so is robustness. They go hand in hand.

Unfortunately for Manchester United, the money has not been on the pitch down the years nearly as much as the club would want or expect.

Bruno Fernandes stands out for what he does with the ball primarily, but also because he plays almost every minute of every game and, while his sheer indefatigability is extreme, United know they need more of his ilk.

This is why the forthcoming season is such a big one for Mason Mount. His quality has seldom been in doubt. The problem is he has rarely been on the pitch long or consistently enough to show it.

Indeed, the one-time England midfielder has started just 25 Premier League matches since his £60m move from Chelsea three years ago and that perennial unavailability is one of the reasons doubts were being cast about his Old Trafford future going into this summer.

Yet Michael Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and intriguingly the 27-year-old could yet have an impact on what the club do during the remaining six weeks of the transfer window.

For the second time in the space of six days, Mount was deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside new £48m, signing Andrey Santos for Friday’s resounding 5-0 victory over Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim, just as he had done against Wrexham last weekend.

Mount has spent the majority of his career playing further forward, either off the right or as a No. 10 but Carrick likes him in a fluid No. 8 role, a position Erik ten Hag had identified for the player only for persistent injuries to detonate those plans.

The logic is simple: Mount is mobile, can cover the ground, is adept under pressure, has line breaking passing, vision and a nose for goal. He is also a good presence in the dressing room and a leader in his own way. Watch him imparting advice to Shea Lacey as they walked back to the centre circle after the youngster’s goal opened the scoring against Rosenborg and you get a glimpse of that.

The question, of course, is whether he can stay fit long enough to impose those qualities that help to explain why Liverpool and Arsenal had also been so keen to sign him back in 2023 and Carrick’s predecessor Ruben Amorim was also such a fan.

With United’s summer budget only stretching so far, Carrick was always going to have to think on his feet in certain areas of the pitch.

What will be interesting to see over the coming weeks is whether the manager feels Mount is robust enough to complement Santos, fellow summer signing Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo.

MASON MOUNT SCORES FOR MAN UNITED!He takes the ball with a quality turn, and curls it into the corner of the goal 🤩📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/M9ErA2HKbo

Much of the chatter among United fans at present centres on who the third midfield signing will be after Santos and Tielemans.

Given Mount’s injury record, it would be a significant risk not to recruit again in that department in the hope he could stay fit over a full season. Four options in two positions behind the No 10 of Fernandes sounds fine in principle but what happens if Mount’s season was to follow a similar trajectory to the previous three?

If United are going to strengthen in other areas, there will need to be compromises or alternative solutions that help to free up cash along the way but gambling in midfield may not be the best way to go.

With Champions League football to factor in this season, it is still hard to believe United will not seek to strengthen again in midfield but the club seem ready to take their time on that front. And all the while an assortment of names continue to fly around.

After spending £85m on Santos and Tielemans, a massive outlay on a third midfielder at this stage would be a bit of a surprise.

Could that negate a move for Real Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni? Alex Scott is greatly admired by United but Bournemouth are determined to keep him and have put a prohibitive pricetag on him.

AS Roma’s Manu Kone is not thought to have universal backing internally. Tyler Adams’ name has been floated again but the Bournemouth and US midfielder’s injury record counts against him.

There has not yet been evidence of a serious appetite to go for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, whom they considered signing last summer. Sander Berge at Fulham and Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha are among a number of other midfielders who have been linked with United.

Another midfield signing could well emerge but United are keeping their cards close to their chest. Whatever materialises, though, it will still not change the fact this is a huge season for Mount.

⚽️ Shea Lacey⚽️ Jacob Devaney⚽️ Harry Amass⚽️ Ethan Williams Four #MUAcademy prospects were on the scoresheet in Trondheim 🧬💙 pic.twitter.com/fguQ36ANTM

“It was a good day. Clean sheet, scoring goals and everyone coming through injury-free hopefully is everything you want. Keeping the players fit and improving through pre-season is amongst the most important things. You want to build through the pre-season and you have to manage to players differently. It is never going to be perfect but we scored some great goals and we are moving forward nicely.

“I thought we defended well as a team for the most part. A clean sheet is a beautiful thing. I think we are in a good place with four weeks to go until the start, gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup. As it stands right now, we are in a pretty good place.”

This is what the official start of the season will look like for Michael Carrick’s side:

August 22- Hull vs Manchester UnitedAugust 30- Manchester United vs IpswichSeptember 6- Everton vs Manchester UnitedSeptember 13- Manchester United vs Manchester CitySeptember 20- Fulham vs Manchester United

They face two of the three promoted sides on the first two weekends and there is a very early Manchester derby.

August 1- Manchester United vs Atlético Madrid August 8- PSG vs Manchester United August 12- Manchester United vs Leeds August 15- AC Milan vs Manchester United

Having played Wrexham and Rosenborg in their first two games, the level of competition will rise significantly for Manchester United in the coming weeks.

There is the final whistle and Manchester United have cruised to a 5-0 win over Rosenborg in Norway. Goals from Lacey, Zirkzee, Devaney, Amass and Williams have seen Michael Carrick’s men ease to victory. A pretty one-sided game.

The first yellow card of the game is given very late on as Devaney is booked for a high boot.

A late change for Rosenborg as Hald-Hernes replaces Borgersen.

The visitors have dominated this game and they now have their fifth goal. It is created by great work from Kamason on the right side of the box before he squares it to Williams, who has the easiest of tap-ins at the far post.

Other than a few short periods in this game, Rosenborg have looked poor. They may be midway through their league season but you can see why they are down in 10th in the Norwegian top flight with just four wins from their opening 13 league games.

You would expect that Michael Carrick will be very keen to see his side keep a clean sheet.

Manchester United have their fourth of the evening. Kamason is found making an overlapping run on the right side of the box and his cross fired towards the back post is tapped in by Amass. That was a goal assisted by one full-back and scored by the other.

Good work from Soboczynski results in Rosenborg winning a corner out on the left. They take it short before a shot is hit from the edge of the box straight down the throat of Vitek.

Rosenborg hit the post. Manchester United should probably have been given a free-kick in the build-up as Soboczynski appeared to push Devaney over but play goes on. The ball comes to E Ceide at the far post but his effort strikes the outside of the post.

Just a few minutes after making a raft of changes, Manchester United have their third goal of the evening. Rosenborg fail to clear a corner from the right and the ball falls to Devaney on the six-yard box. He takes one touch before firing into the top of the net.

Bearing in mind Rosenborg are in the middle of their league season, this has been an encouraging showing so far from United. Joshua Zirkzee has been lively. He’s still more likely to leave than stay at Old Trafford this summer but performances like this won’t hamper his value. He set up Shea Lacey for his goal with a good pass after again dropping deep into space and he’s taken that goal to give United a 2-0 lead quite brilliantly. Patrick Dorgu has been a threat and Mason Mount has dovetailed well in central midfield with new signing Andrey Santos.

Both sides are going to make a raft of changes on the hour mark, with the rest of the Manchester United starting XI being changed other than Vitek in goal.

Santos brings down Borgersen not far outside the Manchester United penalty area to give Rosenborg a decent opportunity. It is a pretty decent effort from E Ceide that goes just wide of Vitek’s right post.

The visitors have not been great since the break but they have their second and it is a great solo goal from Zirkzee. Lacey, out on the left touchline, squares it for Zirkzee, who takes the ball towards the Rosenborg penalty area. He fakes a shot, which takes numerous Rosenborg defenders out of the equation as they slide past. He then sits down the Rosenborg keeper before slotting into an empty net. A fine goal from Zirkzee.

Soboczynski has his second chance since coming on at the break after good work from E Ceide down the left but the former’s effort goes wide.

That is a really poor decision from the linesman. Duris was played in behind the Manchester United defence and thought he was through for a one-on-one chance but the offside flag goes up. However, replays prove that Duris was clearly being played onside by Amass, who has looked shaky since coming on at the break.

Zirkzee receives a pass from Dorgu on the D and takes one touch before shooting. His effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner, which Wahlstedt slightly unconvincingly punches away.

That is a very good chance for Rosenborg to equalise early in this second half. Amass and Heaven makes a mess of things deep in their own half, presenting Rosenborg with a good opportunity inside the Manchester United penalty area. Two Rosenborg substitutes combine as Soboczynski squares it for Borgersen but the latter makes a mess of it and shoots well wide from 10 yards out.

Michael Carrick has decided to make just a few changes at the break with Amass and Kamason coming on. Shaw and Maguire have gone off, which has seen Yoro move inside from right-back to centre-back.

Our first goalscorer of pre-season = Shea Lacey! 💎 pic.twitter.com/AyFOWNh5Fi

With no delays, the first half is brought to an end and Manchester United take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Lacey’s goal. Expect a raft of chnages at the break.

As this half has worn on, Manchester United’s dominance has only increased.

Mbeumo appeared to be racing through one-on-one but Mortensen just about gets back to outmuscle Mbeumo and allow the ball to go back to his keeper. There were a few appeals for a foul by Mortensen but that challenge was just about fine.

Other than those early stages, Manchester United have dominated the rest of this first half and are pressing for a second. For the second time in the half, they strike the frame of the goal. Mbeumo clips in a cross from the right into the Rosenborg penalty area and it picks out the head of Yoro. However, from eight yards out, the Frenchman’s header comes back off the bar.

Moments after they hit the frame of the goal, Michael Carrick’s side take the lead. Zirkzee picks up the ball inside his own half and, from the halfway line, feeds a pass into the on-running Lacey. Dorgu wants Lacey to play the ball across to him at the back post but the latter opts against it. Instead, just inside the Rosenborg penalty area, he cuts onto his preferred left foot and curls one into the far corner. A good finish from Lacey.

Just as I was saying that both sides were lacking a cutting edge in the final third, Manchester United are inches away from taking the lead as they strike the post. Santos feeds a delicate pass into the path of Dorgu on the left side of the box. Dorgu strikes his effort powerfully but it comes off the outside of the far post.

Both sides have lacked a cutting edge when they get into the opposition final third, hence why there has not been a plethora of good chances.

Mbeumo beats his man down Manchester United’s right and cuts it back to Mount on the edge of the Rosenborg penalty area. Mount hits it first time but his shot is blocked and spins behind for a corner. It is Manchester United’s first of the game but it is headed away.

That was nearly the moment for Rosenborg to take the lead. Pereira’s cross from the left-hand side of the box takes a deflection and nearly ends up at the feet of Chiakha at the back post but it is just out of his reach.

Rosenborg looked the sharper in the early exchanges but Manchester United are growing into the game and starting to gain more control.

Manchester United create their first opening of the game. Rosenborg poorly five the ball away deep inside their half and immediately Zirkzee plays it into the path of Mbeumo, whose shot from the right side of the box is saved by Rosenborg keeper Wahlstedt, who initially spilt the shot but gathered at the second attempt.

Mount trips Sahsah just outside the Manchester United penalty area, which will give Rosenborg a good shot to take an early lead. Rosenborg look a little sharper unsurprisingly in these early stages.

The Rosenborg captain Selnaes takes but hits it straight into the wall.

With Rosenborg in the midst of their season and Manchester United just in their second pre-season game, you would expect the hosts to have more rhythm and flow in their game.

Manchester United to appear to be lining up with a back four, with Yoro starting at right-back rather than his more customary centre-back position.

We are under way in Norway. Rosenborg are playing in white, with Manchester United in blue.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Harry Maguire leading Manchester United out, and we are getting closer to kick-off in Norway.

Rosenborg: Wahlstedt, Mortensen, Singsdal Volden, Nemcik, Pereira; Bomholt, Selnaes, Fossum, Sunde, Chiakha, Sahsah.Substitutes: Sandberg, Amdam, M. Ceide, Rosten, Witry, Dahl, Hald-Hernes, Slordal, Hedman, Borgersen, Bakke, E. Ceide, Duris, Soboczynski.

Manchester United: Vitek; Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Lacey, Zirkzee, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Heaton, Mee, Amass, Armer, Kamason, Collyer, Devaney, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Gore, Thwaites, Gabriel, Obi, Williams.

It’s a good opportunity for Shea Lacey tonight. He’s expected to be deployed in the hole in behind Joshua Zirkzee. A talented, highly technical footballer with a good left foot, he’ll be wanting to make the most of the chance. Another opportunity for Mason Mount to stake a claim in one of the two deeper midfield positions next to new signing Andrey Santos. Big season ahead for Mount.

Manchester United’s preparations for the new season continue in Norway as they take on Rosenborg in their second pre-season game. These sides did meet in a pre-season friendly two years ago in July 2024, with Rosenborg winning that encounter 1-0.

Manchester United kicked off their pre-season against Wrexham nearly a week ago, which they lost 1-0 in Helsinki. Michael Carrick opted to deploy two different XIs for each half, meaning 22 players got a run-out. Manchester United kick off their Premier League campaign at newly promoted Hull City on August 22.

They have added two midfielders to their ranks over the last few weeks, both from the Premier League. Brazilian Andrey Santos has joined from Chelsea whilst Belgium’s Youri Tielemans has arrived from Aston Villa. Santos made his first Manchester United appearance in the loss to Wrexham whilst Tielemans is yet to feature having made the knockout stages with Belgium at the World Cup. A number of players are still yet to return from World Cup duty, including the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, although Rashford still faces an uncertain future.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived but he is currently recovering from a minor procedure. Benjamin Sesko is still trying to shake off a shin injury whilst Matthijs de Ligt is not yet available due to a back injury which plagued for most of last season. Manuel Ugarte faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines having picked up a serious injury whilst playing for Uruguay at the World Cup. After this game, the level of competition for Manchester United for the rest of pre-season ramps up a number of notches, with the likes of Atlético Madrid and back-to-back European champions PSG to come over the next couple of weeks as Carrick’s men prepare for a season in which they return to the Champions League.

Rosenborg are in the midst of their league campaign in Norway and are experiencing a tricky campaign. They are currently 10th in the Norwegian top flight, having won just four of their 13 league games thus far, but their form has picked up of late as they have won three of their last five games. They won their last match 3-0 against Start six days ago.

#2174. “Increased to 85,000 capacity” claim for London Stadium – Report | West Ham News

In a week during which the future of West Ham’s home hit the media again thanks to the owners desperately seeking a way out of their financial cut de sac, some pretty spectacular claims were made about the former Olympic Stadium’s ability to host huge events in the future.

West Ham fans, used to enormous queues and delays just to get inside will find the jaw-dropping suggestion that a further twenty thousand people could be crammed into the arena pretty implausible.

Yes, it coped -somehow- aided by a veritable army of volunteers and impeccably behaved ‘olympic-going’ families, with 80,000 in 2012. But they weren’t all trying to arrive at exactly the same time, were they.

Add the temporary nature of the upper tiers and the constant leaks, queues for everything and the long, post-event shuffle back to Stratford station, unlit and with the hated walking traffic lights halting progress as the rain falls whilst the misery becomes abject, and you have a sporting venue wholly unfit even for its current 62,500 capacity.

London Stadium queues: Try doing it at night, in the rain and the dark. along with another 25,000 fans. No thanks.

Yet 85,000 is the claim. According to sportscape magazine:

“…By making a formal request to the Newham Council to have boxing bouts categorised as “other leisure events” so as to facilitate the increase in the maximum capacity of the event from 60,000 to 85,000.”

You’d hope the licensing authority will see sense and deny the venue permission. Anyone who’s tried to get to, and from the stadium on a match day will understand why adding another 20,000 – presumably standing on the floor of the arena – but with the same access arrangements, the same shortage of toilets and concessions, will understand the unsuitability of the arena and it’s dreadful surrounds for further expansion.

It needs knocking down and rebuilding, West Ham fans will all tell you that. But with the Hammers’ 99 year lease, that is never going to happen. So further ‘ideas’ to try and turn a profit will surely keep failing thanks to the poor commercial design, the very temporary nature of the upper parts of the structure and the facility- free wasteland that surrounds the ground.

85,000? Well, I won’t be one of them. Not even if you paid me.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

The biggest frustration for me is having to go through security before the game. Having not been able to get away tickets for love nor money I haven’t been to any other Premier league ground for years. Can anyone tell me whether the same security is applied at other grounds and if the answer is no, why do they do it at West Ham? As for 85,000 capacity for boxing, you won’t get everyone in the stadium trying to buy a drink and go to the toilet in the same 15 minute window so that would help!

I was at Sam Fenders gig of 80k +. Getting out was no worse than normal.

Complaining about the access to the London Stadium? Agreed, it’s far from ideal, but 1000 times better than Upton Park, with less than 40,000.

Why does everyone suddenly forget how difficult it was to get on the station at Upton Park? I used to walk to Plaistow to come back past as it was easier than getting on the end of the que. That was also in the rain and dark. And that was one line so 35,000 people at Upton Park is probably the same ratio as the 62,000 at Stratford with all the different routes. Upton Park was falling down. I loved the place and had been going there for 35 years before we moved and season ticket holder there for quite a few of those but when you are taking your 5 year old to the loo’s at half time and ankle deep in pee it wasnt that great. Certain people were never going to accept the LS no matter what and moan about everything, even those things that were just the same at UP. I don’t think its perfect by any means but it’s not as bad as is made out and almost an additional 30,000 West Ham fans get to see the games now.

Full disclosure: I was one of those who couldn’t wait to go to the new stadium, for many of the reasons you outline above. So there’s no rose tinted specs. But if you’ve been to any other ‘new’ ground, be it Wembley, Twickenham or other state of the art stadium you’ll realise how shi*e our ‘home’ is by comparison.

The problem is not just the stadium. The whole area is wrong for West Ham. I remember years ago there was talk of building a stadium in East Ham at a disused bus depot.There must be sites West Ham can explore even if it means the maximum capacity is just 40,000. Still far better than the athletics bowl.

Why would we want to drop down to 40k? Talk about unambitious and being two bob.

We might as well go the full distance and ground-share with Leyton Orient.

Let’s be honest, as it is now Stratford is probably the best area in Newham for a football stadium, as per the 85,000 that is not going to applicable to football fixtures, and also i believe Sam Fender has already had 80,000+ at his live show earlier.

#2173. Arsenal Women vs Benfica: Champions League preview, team news and how to watch

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women face Benfica at Meadow Park tonight, and as they prepare to enter a tough clash in the UEFA Women’s Champions League, head coach Renée Slegers has called for ‘grit and fight’ from her players. The match kicks off at 8pm in Borehamwood and will be available to watch live on Disney+ for UK fans.

Arsenal come into the match on the back of a 2-1 north London derby win at Tottenham. The team sit fifth in the European league with four points, having won 1-0 at home against HB Koge and drawn 2-2 at Paris FC. Benfica are currently sitting in tenth place but will overtake them if they win.

Slegers said the main factor behind Arsenal’s derby win was intensity. “It was a really intense game. We had to fight for it. We scored first, and we came back, so that’s what makes me really proud. Now we have to make sure we follow that up,” she said at London Colney on Tuesday.

Kim Little returns to the squad. Slegers confirmed that Katie Reid and Michelle Agyemang will not be back in time, while Frida Maanum is progressing, but the game comes too soon.

Taylor Hinds was a player of the match contender at Tottenham, playing a full 90 minutes for only the second time this season. Alongside Steph Catley, she linked up well on the left. Slegers has not named the same starting XI in back-to-back games this season, though, and said Arsenal will need “sharpness, quality and injections” late on against Benfica.

The referee is Ivana Projkovska of North Macedonia, who was among the officials for the 2025 Champions League final, when Arsenal beat Barcelona 1-0 in Lisbon.

Benfica have won all four of their Campeonato Nacional Feminino games as they look to retain their title, conceding once, in Saturday’s 4-1 win over Sporting CP. In Europe, Ivan Baptista’s side won 2-1 at Juventus before losing 3-0 at home to Bayern Munich. They have made more interceptions than any other team in this season’s competition, with 33, while Arsenal have made only 13.

Slegers expects a physical, compact opponent, similar in some ways to the derby, though with some changes in personnel since last season, when Arsenal won 2-0 at the Estadio da Luz through Beth Mead and Alessia Russo. Baptista said being seen as favourites means little to him and that his team will cause Arsenal difficulties again.

The record favours the hosts. Arsenal have won 10 of their last 13 home league-phase games in the competition, including the last three, while Benfica have won only three of their last 15 away matches in the tournament.

Slegers admitted the domestic start has been tough but said it is too early to judge and that Arsenal are proud to be back on the Champions League stage. Last season they finished fifth in the league phase before reaching the semi-finals.

#2170. Arsenal injury news: Rice, Madueke and Calafiori concerns ahead of Liverpool clash

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal injury news has been in the headlines ahead of their visit to Anfield. Mikel Arteta confirmed Declan Rice, Noni Madueke and Riccardo Calafiori were all sidelined for their Carabao Cup clash against Fleetwood Town on Tuesday.

The Premier League champions lost 5-3 on penalties following their 1-1 draw at Highbury Stadium. Arsenal will face Liverpool at 4.30pm on Sunday. They have a number of injury concerns, plus a suspended teenager to deal with.

When questioned if the three players had just been rested, Arteta replied that Calafiori was unavailable. Madueke had issues with his ankle and Rice was “feeling something on the previous day”, making visible the reason why he has been substituted.

Martin Zubimendi replaced Rice in Saturday’s game when he substituted the player in the 80th minute of the game versus Everton due to Rice grabbing his hamstring. Madueke played till the end of the game. However, he was not spotted in training Monday, and Arteta did not provide any estimation for his return.

Calafiori appears to be in a better place. After being described as having a ‘slight issue’ by Arteta following the Everton game. DaveOCKOP reports that the defender is expected to be available against Anfield.

Winger Christos Tzolis has also been ruled out for five games with a hamstring injury. We’re likely to get an update on how all three are feeling going into the game from Arteta’s pre-match press conference.

Bukayo Saka is still sidelined with a quadriceps injury picked up against Bayern Munich in the Champions League. Arteta said the injury will take “weeks” to recover from, as he needs another scan due to fluid around the area. William Saliba has not played this season due to a back issue and is unlikely to return until December.

Arsenal’s problems were deepened at Highbury. Aaron Loupalo-Bi put Fleetwood ahead in the 21st minute. Viktor Gyokeres equalised five minutes after the restart, shortly after captain Martin Odegaard came on at half-time. Max Dowman was then sent off in the 85th minute for kicking out at Fleetwood’s Harrison Neal.

The 16-year-old will serve a three-match ban, reportedly covering the trip to Liverpool, the home game against Hull and the visit to Newcastle.

Fleetwood scored all five penalties. Odegaard, Kai Havertz and Gyokeres converted for Arsenal. Goalkeeper Jay Lynch saved Bruno Guimaraes’ effort, and 19-year-old defender Conor Haughey scored the winner. It was reportedly the first time the reigning top-flight champions have lost a League Cup tie to a fourth-tier side. There’s 84 places separating the clubs.

Arteta said the result was not down to attitude. “I’m sad, we’re all sad,” he said.

#2169. Arsenal Women vs Benfica: Alessia Russo Hat-Trick Fires Arsenal Women to 3-0 Champions League Win Over Benfica

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Arsenal Women vs Benfica: Arsenal Women continued their unbeaten start to the UEFA Women’s Champions League league phase with a convincing 3-0 victory over Benfica at Mangata Developments Stadium on Wednesday night.

Alessia Russo hit a hat trick to claim the spoils and become the top scorer in English Women’s Champions League history. The England international opened the scoring before the break and added two more after the interval.

Despite controlling much of the game Arsenal’s attacking play was stymied by the determined Benfica defence and the inspired Lena Pauels in goal. The German made some stunning saves before Russo finally found a way through.

Arsenal came out firing after their win in the North London derby. Olivia Smith put Pauels under pressure after just 65 seconds.

She made another save soon after as the hosts took control of the game and created a number of great chances.

Geraldine Reuteler made her first start for Arsenal and nearly picked out Smith with a dangerous delivery into the penalty area. Russo also saw an effort blocked following a well-worked set piece.

Georgia Stanway came closest to breaking the deadlock during the opening half-hour. The midfielder escaped her marker before sending a powerful shot towards the bottom corner, but Pauels reacted well to keep the score level.

The Benfica goalkeeper continued her impressive performance by denying Caitlin Foord from the resulting corner.

Benfica gradually grew into the contest and threatened through Froya Dorsin, who wasted an opportunity by firing over the crossbar. The visitors created further pressure before Arsenal regained control.

Russo sent an effort narrowly wide before Smith forced another save from Pauels.

However, Arsenal finally broke through five minutes before half-time. Foord supplied a clever pass into Russo, who placed a precise finish against the far post and into the net.

Arsenal kept their forward momentum going into the second half and nearly extended their lead.

Kyra Cooney-Cross found an excellent ball over the top for Foord but was thwarted by a vital challenge from Catarina Amado.

Foord continued to pose a threat and got on the end of a cross from Ona Batlle at the back post. She powered a header across the goal, but Benfica cleared it in time to stop Russo getting on the end of it.

Smith then tested Pauels again with a deflected effort, but the goalkeeper could not prevent Arsenal from scoring their second.

Russo rose to meet Steph Catley’s corner and headed home to extend the hosts’ lead. The goal was her 22nd in the competition, making her the leading English goalscorer in UEFA Women’s Champions League history.

Benfica responded with a dangerous effort from Andreia Norton, forcing Misa Rodriguez into a good save at her near post.

Arsenal quickly threatened on the counter-attack, with Reuteler rounding Pauels before Diana Gomes cleared her effort off the line.

Pauels kept the game alive for Benfica but made a fantastic save to keep out Smith’s powerful strike in the 15th minute.

But Arsenal finally won the game after Amado brought down Foord inside the penalty box.

Russo stepped up and confidently converted from 12 yards to complete her hat-trick and take her Champions League tally to 23 goals.

Foord thought she had added a fourth during stoppage time, but the officials ruled out her effort for offside.

The result means Arsenal remain undefeated in the league phase of the tournament and also highlights the importance of Russo to the club’s European campaign.

They return to Women’s Super League action on Sunday, November 1, when they play Aston Villa at Emirates Stadium before facing Liverpool. On November 12 they head to Spain to face defending European champions Barcelona.

#2164. Derek McInnes' ‘inexperience’ Rangers admission despite Hampden triumph

Derek McInnes admits Rangers’ big-money young attack still needs to develop a ruthless streak after booking a place in the Premier Sports Cup final.

The Ibrox boss was delighted to reach his first final as Rangers manager after Ryan Naderi struck the decisive goal against Aberdeen at Hampden.

But McInnes reckons the 25 shots Rangers produced, with just five on target, highlighted the inexperience that remains in a youthful forward line. He said: “Substantial investment has gone into an attacking unit consisting largely of players aged 20 to 22.

“While that profile offers immense potential and athleticism, younger forwards can occasionally lack the veteran savvy required to avoid snatched finishes or rushed deliveries.

"Statistical output frequently highlights opportunities left unfinished in the final third. In cup semi-finals, however, securing the result is paramount.

“Earning a place in the final gives this group an invaluable opportunity to build belief by competing for the first piece of silverware of the season.”

McInnes felt Rangers were too ponderous during the opening 45 minutes before stepping things up after the break and eventually finding the breakthrough through Naderi. He said: “It is a great feeling.

"Semi-finals are never straightforward, and historically, even highly talented Rangers sides have found them difficult hurdles.

Derek McInnes gives his verdict after reaching his first final as @RangersFC manager 🔵 "It's actually embarrassing we've had 25 shots and only 5 on target!" 🗣️ #PremierSportsCup https://t.co/RzdbeCB70x

— Premier Sports (@PremSportsTV) October 31, 2026

“When you fail to score early and the play is ponderous in the first half, lacking bite and failing to move the ball quickly across the turf, it becomes challenging.

“Producing 25 shots with only five hitting the target reflects inexperience in the forward areas; the team needed an extra pass and better composure in the final third.”

McInnes was also impressed by Kevin Kelsy’s role in the move which eventually led to the winner.

The striker had been on the verge of being replaced by Bojan Miovski before powering Rangers up the pitch. McInnes said: “Bojan Miovski was preparing to replace him right before that move.

“Kelsy demonstrated tremendous power and physical presence to carry the ball up the pitch and had the composure to execute the pass rather than rushing the play.”

And after securing a return to Hampden, McInnes insists competition for places will intensify ahead of the final.

He added: “Places in the starting lineup for mid-December are on the line, which should sharpen individual focus across the upcoming fixtures as the team prepares to challenge for the trophy.”

#2163. Arsenal Max Dowman Red Card Appeal Faces Rejection, Says Dermot Gallagher

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Former Premier League official Dermot Gallagher has said he thinks Arsenal won’t be successful in their appeal against Max Dowman’s red card in their Carabao Cup loss to Fleetwood Town.

The 16-year-old Arsenal winger was shown a red card for violent conduct after lashing out at Harrison Neal after a strong challenge from the Fleetwood defender. The Gunners then lost the fourth-round tie on penalties.

Arsenal are appealing the sending off of Max Dowman. They need to have their paperwork in by 1pm today (Thursday). They will be hoping to get a decision before their Premier League game against Liverpool on Sunday.

But Gallagher does not think they will be successful in their appeal as he believes there was clear intent from Dowman.

“I think it was a red card for the actions of the teenager,” Gallagher said.

He also thinks the referee should have given Arsenal a free kick as well as booking Neal for his challenge on Dowman.

Gallagher told Sky Sports News that the attitude of Dowman could be an issue for Arsenal in their red card appeal.

“I think he went out of his way to kick his leg up. It makes it difficult to overturn the decision,” Gallagher said.

“He’s got more of an aggressive reaction than what Cole Palmer had recently with Mateus Fernandes.”

But Gallagher was critical of the challenge made by Neal on the Arsenal youngster. He said that while Fleetwood’s defender did win the ball back, he didn’t think the challenge was made with enough consideration for Dowman’s safety.

“I think he should have got a free-kick and a yellow card,” he added.

The debate leaves Arsenal facing a difficult decision ahead of their Premier League fixture against Liverpool. If the appeal fails, Dowman’s dismissal will stand.

Sky Sports pundit Paul Merson said he disagreed with Gallagher’s comments, saying it was a harsh red card.

“It was a classic old fashioned tackle. He (Neal) wins the ball and then follows through. I think the reaction from the players might have had something to do with the referee giving Dowman a red card.”

Merson also warned the young Gunner that he will always be a target for opposition players.

Dowman has had disciplinary problems in the past, being sent off whilst playing for England against the USA. Merson feels the youngster needs to learn to control his emotions and not get caught up in the taunts of opposition players.

The incident has also raised more questions over how Arsenal are developing one of their most promising young talents.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta also attracted criticism for his reaction to Dowman after the Carabao Cup defeat to Fleetwood Town.

As the teenager walked towards the tunnel, Arteta leaned towards him and spoke to him. Merson questioned the approach, arguing that the Arsenal manager should have offered reassurance to the 16-year-old instead.

Arteta declined to reveal exactly what he told Dowman, explaining only that they had discussed the matter before the match.

The Arsenal boss also said the team had prepared for the emotional challenges they expected to face during the tie.

Jobi McAnuff similarly questioned Arteta’s response, arguing that Dowman remains young and will inevitably make mistakes as he develops.

Arsenal must now wait for the outcome of their red card appeal. With Liverpool next on the fixture list, the decision could have important implications for Arteta’s selection plans.
