#2120. Tottenham new boys score in shoot-out win over Sydney FC

Tottenham Hotspur fans enjoyed their first glimpse of summer signings Andy Robertson and Sandro Tonali in the shirt, with both players scoring penalties in the shoot-out that followed a 1-1 draw with Sydney FC.

Spurs took the lead through a first-half Mathys Tel free-kick, before Roberto De Zerbi’s youthful defence was undone by Takahiro Sekine, who tucked away one of the Australian side’s only chances of the game.

Magic from Mathys Tel 🪄A brilliant free kick from the Frenchman gets @spursofficial off to a flyer, as the striker puts it top bins to take a 1-0 lead in SydneyWatch #TOTvSYD live and exclusive on Paramount+ 📺 pic.twitter.com/ntqTgleasJ

Tonali was brought on as a half-time substitute, before Robertson took the captain’s armband from Archie Gray after he was introduced in the 65th minute.

The former Liverpool left-back delivered three dangerous crosses which went unconverted, something of a theme for a Spurs team who failed to make the most of long spells of dominance.

James Maddison and Mateus Fernandes were not in the match-day squad, while Pedro Porro, Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero, Micky van de Ven and Jean Paul van Hecke have yet to join the group after the World Cup.

There was another impressive showing from 17-year-old prospect Luca Williams-Barnett, who is pushing for first-team opportunities this upcoming season.

Penalties followed the final whistle, with Spurs scoring all four of their spot kicks. Goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, signed on a free transfer this summer, saved one and Sydney FC’s Josh Lacey hit the post to give Spurs the spoils 4-2.

Spurs win the shoot-out 4-2. That will be that.

Hoefsloot dives to his right and pushes Donley’s penalty around the post.

But then Dubravka saves from Popovic, and Spurs remain 3-2 up. Score the next one and they win the shoot-out.

Very similar placing to Tonali’s penalty. Does Dubravka have a save in him?

He doesn’t need to have one because Josh Lacey has hit the post. 3-2 to Spurs after three pens each.

Plenty of power and right into the side netting. No mistake from Spurs’s big money summer signing.

Dubravka then guesses the right way, but Toure finds the bottom left corner. 2-2.

The 17-year-old takes the mickey a little bit, dinking the ball straight down the middle. Spurs score their first penalty.

Then Popovic steps up and sends Dubravka the wrong way. 1-1.

Spurs were the game’s dominant force, but they did not convert that control into enough goals. No cause for alarm though, and no injuries from what we can tell. There will be some penalties on the way.

Williams-Barnett with a superb piece of control and turn forward, but the danger was snuffed out as he dribbled the ball into the penalty area. Then the youngster shoots from outside the box, deflected behind for a corner.

Andy Robertson has been impressive, and the goalkeeper makes a fingertip save to flick his low cross away from danger. Almost third time lucky for Yang who was waiting at the back post for a tap-in.

Andy Robertson's first outing as a Spurs player 🫡 pic.twitter.com/q5bdzQknJ2

Spurs controlling possession, pushing for the goal that would spare them having to take some penalties. As happens with this friendlies, the game has become more bitty since all the changes.

If the game finishes as a draw, there will be a penalty shoot-out. Donley has fizzed some crisp forward passes since coming on in midfield. Then Donley underlaps, picked out by Williams-Barnett but his low cross is straight at the goalkeeper.

Andy Robertson getting forward to good effect once again, standing up a cross for Yang in the middle but the substitute heads wide from seven or eight yards out.

Referee waves play on as Spurs pour forward and Robertson flashes a ball across the box, and the slight deflection was enough to put off Yang at the back post and he missed the target. Should have been a tap in.

Spurs close to a second, but Tonali’s shot from the edge of the box is pushed around the post. There was more good approach play from Williams-Barnett to tee up the Italian.

More Spurs changes: Andy Robertson is on, and takes the armband, he replaces Kyerematen. Up front, Richarlison and Solomon are off, replaced by Min-Hyeok and Dane Scarlett. Donley and Melia replace Gray and Gallagher in midfield.

A couple of appeals for a Spurs penalty after Kyerematen burst beyond the Sydney defence from left-back. He could have crossed sooner, but was tackled, and then there was a challenge on Richarlison. Referee waves it away.

Very youthful Spurs back four on the pitch now, which played a part in the nature of the equaliser they conceded. No Romero, Van de Ven, Van Hecke or Senesi available for selection today, but Andy Robertson is warming up on the touchline.

Spurs straight back into another long spell of possession, with Tonali winning a foul in midfield after a smooth turn forward.

A touch of ill fortunate for Spurs, the half-time substitute Takai inadvertently poked the ball through to Sekine who lifted the ball over Dubravka to equalise. Delicate finish, and Spurs are breached.

Conor Gallagher still closing down tirelessly, but he has been a little untidy with the ball at his feet. I suspect he was the bleep test winner in training. Sydney do well to play through the pressure and keep possession for a while.

Good industry from Tonali in midfield to regain possession, and Williams-Barnett shows real poise on the ball again. Easy to see why Spurs are excited about him.

Kyerematen defends well at the back post when it looked like Macallister was about to head at goal.

Then Spurs are away on the break, and Williams-Barnett skims the crossbar with a left-footed shot from a tight angle.

Three half-time Spurs changes: Tel, Bergvall and Davies off, Takai, Tonali and Williams-Barnett are on. Takai goes to centre-back with 17-year-old Williams-Barnett in an attacking midfield position.

A decent half’s work from Spurs, they look in a good place physically and their high pressing has caught the eye. Not quite clinical enough in the penalty area so far though, they have butchered some good chances.

Sydney have come to life as an attacking force, Spurs’s defence undone by a ball over the top. Dubravka caught in no-man’s-land, and Mac Allister poked the ball beyond him but did not generate enough power to score.

Cracking effort from the Sydney forward Macallister, trying to chip Dubravka from some 45 yards out. The goalkeeper was worried and scrambling, the effort misses the target.

Sydney looking ragged now, and Gallagher cracks a shot off the foot of the post from the edge of the box. Then Youlley takes on a shot from long range which is high, wide and handsome. Richarlison is then fouled by Popovic, dragging down the forward to stop a counter. Yellow card.

Conor Gallagher is charging forward at every opportunity, applying pressure on Sydney’s defenders whenever they have the ball. With no European football, Spurs can really lean into a high-octane approach this season.

Great take, right footed to the the goalkeeper’s side, and the strike was too powerful for Hoefsloot. A clean hit, and Spurs now lead. A well-deserved goal on the balance of play.

The game has slipped into a lull now, after a bright Spurs start. De Zerbi’s team do now have a free-kick at the edge of the D after Manor Solomon is fouled.

Tel amnd Gallagher threaten down the left for Spurs, with the midfielder finding the winger with a reverse pass. Tel’s cross is cleared.

Then Sydney muster their first shot of the game, Youlley with a strike from 25 yards out which Dubravka pushes away from danger.

Sydney FC starting to get their foot on the ball a little more now, but still no sign that they have capability to hurts Spurs going forward. Kyerematen is then fouled in the Sydney half.

Sydney are yet to have a touch in the Spurs penalty area, it has been one-way traffic so far. De Zerbi will be pleased with what he has watched so far, but no killer touch in the box as yet.

Conor Gallagher with a nice touch to win a free-kick near the left touchline. Sydney just about hanging on. The goalkeeper claims Tel’s cross from the free-kick.

Spurs’s closing down is choking Sydney’s build up play, and Gallagher wastes a good chance when free in the box. Shot blocked when there was time and space to pick his spot.

Lucas Bervall’s low cross is turned behind for a corner and Spurs remain in the ascendancy. Another threatening delivery, and Ben Davies may well have had a shout for a penalty, dragged to the turf by Grant. If this was a Premier League game, I’m sure VAR would have taken a close look at that.

Hoefsloot with a really poor pass from his six-yard box, straight into the path of Tel 25 yards out, but his side-footed effort was saved by the goalkeeper. Pitches like this make technical errors an inevitability.

Sydney’s goalkeeper Hoefsloot punches a corner clear under some pressure, attacking set-pieces were a rare positive for Spurs last season. The Premier League team are dominating possession in the early minutes.

Conor Gallagher and Richarlison leading an aggressive Tottenham press in the early exchanges. Tel enjoys plenty of touches down the left flank, but his inswinging cross from the left is headed clear. Rio Kyerematen is puhsing on from left-back.

After a rendition of Oh When The Saints Go Marching In on the trumpet, we are under way. A chance for Aussie Spurs fans to feel like they are in N17 for the evening.

The pitch looks slightly more lush than the surface Chelsea had to play on across town yesterday. The Allianz Stadium looks distinctly similar to the Etihad. Archie Gray captains Spurs.

No James Maddison in the squad for this game, perhaps still being managed physically after last year’s serious knee injury. Suspect we will see a more senior side picked for the friendly against Chelsea on Saturday.

The 21-year-old has a sweet left foot, on display when he scored this goal against Manchester City while on loan at Leyton Orient.

JAMIE DONLEY. THAT'S INCREDIBLE. 🤯The @SpursOfficial loanee with an incredible effort from distance that ends up in the net to give @leytonorientfc the opening goal against Manchester City 😱#EmiratesFACup pic.twitter.com/bHnKg92Q2y

Lucas Bergvall has been linked with a move away from Spurs, but he starts in midfield. No Fernandes in the squad at all. No summer signings in the starting line-up, but Tonali and Andy Robertson are on the bench.

Spurs starting XI: Dubravka; Kyerematen, Davies, Hardy, Tye Hall; Gray, Bergvall, Solomon, Gallagher, Tel; Richarlison

Subs: Kinsky, Robertson, Takai, Tingey, Byrne, Tyrese Hall, Russell-Denny, Donley, Tonali, Ajayi, Yang, Williams-Barnett, Scarlett

Spurs fans took their first look at summer signing Mateus Fernandes in a 2-0 victory over Auckland, and their pre-season tour continues today against Sydney FC.

Fernandes, an £85m purchase from West Ham United, also scored a stunning volley in a behind-closed-doors game against MK Dons.

Sandro Tonali is part of the travelling squad for these friendlies, as is new centre-back Jean Paul van Hecke. Marcos Senesi, Cristian Romero and Pedro Porro have been given extra time off after their respective nations reached the World Cup final, won by Porro and Spain.

Van Hecke and Senesi ranked very highly among defenders for progressive passing, which offers an insight into the qualities Roberto De Zerbi is prioritising this summer.

The Italian likes his teams to bait opponents into pressing them high up the pitch, before moving the ball through central areas using third-man combinations and wall passes. The addition of two ball-playing centre-backs and two new central midfielders should mean Spurs can play like a recognisable De Zerbi team.

While Dane Scarlett and Richarlison scored against Auckland, Spurs’s squad still lacks high-class options in forward areas, with a move for Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi mooted earlier in the summer.

Spurs fans will be excited to watch 17-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett, the midfielder who is one of the outstanding players in his age group in the country.

“He’s a talent,” Ledley King said. “There’s a lot of hard work ahead of him, but there’s no doubt that he’s someone with great ability.

“He’s seen players like Harry Kane come through the academy and, through sheer hard work and determination, put themselves in a position to kick on. He couldn’t have a better role model.

“There’s no doubt we’re excited by his talent and the next part will be up to him.”

#2119. Former West Ham Star ‘Wants’ Manager’s Job as Pressure Mounts on Nuno

After the third defeat of the season at the London stadium, there has been inevitable speculation that Nuno’s job is under threat. Supporters favourite would be Eddie Howe, yet it’s unlikely that the former Newcastle United manager would be interested in the job.

However there is a a former West Ham player reportedly interested in becoming the club’s next head coach should the Hammers decide to part ways with Nuno Espírito Santo in the near future. And it’s not Scott Parker!

Increasing pressure after three home defeats – and six goals conceded in eight days

Current Wales manager Craig Bellamy has privately indicated that he would welcome the opportunity to manage West Ham if the position became available. Bellamy’s former team-mate James Collins recently endorsed the idea during an appearance on TalkSport.

Bellamy has implemented an attractive brand of football with Wales, built around possession, high intensity and an aggressive pressing style. Yet, since taking on the job in 2024, results have been mixed with a 37.5% win ratio during that time. This has not stopped speculation over whether he could one day return to east London in a managerial capacity.

Following Saturday’s 3-1 defeat to West Bromwich Albion, Nuno Espírito Santo acknowledged the scrutiny surrounding his position.

“I am always under pressure, every day,” he said.

Supporters at the London Stadium made their feelings known after the final whistle, with chants of “You’re getting sacked in the morning” directed at the Portuguese Head Coach.

Yet despite the clubs current position in eighth place, Nuno Espírito Santo is expected to be given more time. Daniel Kretinsky continues to support the Portuguese coach, although both parties understand the pressure that comes with football management.

For now, Bellamy’s interest appears to be one for the future rather than the present. Nuno still retains the backing of the club’s hierarchy, but football can change quickly and results will ultimately determine his fate.

Should a managerial vacancy arise down the line, Bellamy’s connection to West Ham and his exciting coaching philosophy could make him a name worth watching.

#2118. The curious tale of Virgil van Dijk and Dan Burn

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Exactly two weeks ago I wrote an article about Dan Burn and Virgil vak Dijk.

Newcastle United had lost 1-0 at home to Aston Villa on the Saturday.

That article I did on Monday 19 October 2026 was sparked by seeing another piece on The Mag that morning, ‘Newcastle United striker problem’ by Oden Hudson: ‘Let’s start with the most obvious sign that the club has an issue in forward areas – we ended the [Aston Villa] game with Dan Burn at striker. A comical decision that not even the most rogue Football Manager player would dare consider, this is an abhorrently dreadful and comical sign that we have truly failed to address our issues up top over the summer.’

This has become a huge topic of conversation for many fans and indeed those in the media. Dan Burn playing up front for Newcastle United against Aston Villa.

This used by numerous people after the Villa match as final ‘proof’ of how bad things are at NUFC. Along the lines of  ‘proof’ of how clueless Matthias Jaissle, how rubbish the Newcastle United team is, how terrible the transfer policy is, and so on.

The way that writer and others were going on, you would have though Matthias Jaissle had played Dan Burn as a striker from the start of that Aston Villa match.

The reality was that Dan Burn came on in the 90th minute for Joelinton, who was knackered after starting his first competitive game in more than five months. Having trailed at the break, Newcastle United were the better team in the second half but struggled to break down an Aston Villa defence that was now set. Defending deep, Villa were very difficult to play through, whilst crosses into the box were getting zero joy as Villa’s tall defenders headed them all away, or Suzuki dealt with them,  we could all see United were getting nowhere as added time approached.

So Matthias Jaissle throwing Dan Burn on for the added time minutes in the hope he might cause a bit of chaos in the Villa penalty area, win the odd header that the rest of the United players had failed to do. It almost worked as well a couple of promising situations and one moment in particular, where if the ball had fallen more kindly then a Newcastle player (can’t remember who) would have had a huge clear chance from only seven or eight yards or so.

I couldn’t see anything wrong with doing that, chucking Dan Burn up front for the last few minutes. I didn’t have a problem with it. What I really did have a problem with was those Newcastle United fans and some in the media making out that this was the most ridiculous thing in the world and no other manager or team had ever done such a thing in the history of the game.

The fact is that countless other managers had done the same AND continue to do the same.

I quoted the example of Harry Maguire at Manchester United, he has been similarly used in the past as a last chance resort up front when Man U have been desperate for a goal. Indeed, ahead of the World Cup finals, a big debate was whether Thomas Tuchel should take Dan Burn or Harry Maguire. Neither were seen as going to be starting the England games but the key thing the media all agreed on was they could be brought on late in matches to help defend a lead, or to be thrown up front if they were desperate for a goal late on and struggling to create chances. Not playing as a striker for a long time but in the very final stages hanging around up front and a chance to try something different, win a key header maybe, cause some chaos.

My main quoted example two weeks ago though was Virgil van Dijk, I had seen him sent up front late on in countless Liverpool matches. With absolutely zero ridicule aimed at Jurgen Klopp or Arne Slot for doing so.

Surprise surprise, yesterday I saw relatively long before the final whistle at Anfield, Virgil van Dijk sent up front to try and salvage something as they trailed Arsenal. In the Sky Sports commentary this was seen as perfectly valid and an obvious thing to do to try something different, a tall central defender playing up front to try and get on the end of some crosses and long balls. Liverpool still didn’t manage an effort on target all match and lost the game BUT nothing negative has been said at all by anybody in the media or elsewhere, regarding this tactic of employing Virgil van Dijk as an emergency striker late on.

I think it is all a bit pathetic the way that certain journalists went on about Dan Burn playing those few minutes up front in the Villa defeat, a cowardly and not valid reason for having a go at Matthias Jaissle and Newcastle United generally.

Even worse the clueless Newcastle United fans doing the same, desperate to have a go at the new NUFC Head Coach by any means possible.

There are valid questions to be asked and debated on both Matthias Jaissle and Newcastle United generally. However, using that Dan Burn ‘striker’ thing as a stick to beat him and the club with was beyond embarrassing.

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

It has now been revealed that Régis Le Bris has been told by Sunderland he has their full support and will continue in the job.

It looked like the writing was on the wall when rock bottom Sunderland were outplayed and outclassed by second bottom Coventry City on Saturday, lucky to only lose 3-1. The Sky Blues now four points clear of hapless Sunderland.

However, Sky Sports report that they have had official confirmation that Régis Le Bris has been informed his job is safe.

Keith Downie covers Sunderland and Newcastle United for Sky Sports and he states: “Régis Le Bris’ position as Sunderland Head Coach is safe and he continues to have the full support and confidence of Sunderland’s hierarchy. The Frenchman remains central to Sunderland plans and ambitions, despite the club sitting bottom of the Premier League table. The belief within the club is the 50-year-old will turn things around.”

Sunderland have lost five and drawn one of their last six Premier League matches and their late (no) consolation goal on Saturday came after more than six hours of league football without scoring.

Sunderland have now picked up only two points from their last possible 21 and their only Premier League victory over the season was back in August, a lucky late 1-0 home win over Fulham.

The man from Sky Sports adding about what they have heard from inside Sunderland AFC: “There is an internal recognition that recent Premier League results have been disappointing and the club understand current frustrations felt by supporters. The club believe stability, collective responsibility and a united approach is the way forward for Sunderland as they look to achieve their ambitions….”

Yes, Régis Le Bris is doing a great job at Sunderland and hopefully they will keep faith with him as they continue to lose many more matches.

After losing so convincingly to the club that was second bottom, in the Premier League Sunderland now face Chelsea (home), Aston Villa (away), Spurs (home) and Liverpool (away). #2116. “Who else is standing up?” – Report claims players no longer fighting for Nuno | West Ham News

As the third goal went in yesterday, shoulders visibly sank around the players on the pitch as the home fans booed their efforts and the apparent ease in which second division sides are able to give West Ham the run around.

This, supposedly the strongest team in the Championship being humbled by a hard working West Brom after Southampton made the Irons look very ordinary seven days before.

It might not yet have reached the full-on crisis of a manager having irrevocably lost his dressing room, but West Ham fan and journalist Roshane Thomas has pinpointed what he sees as a squad rapidly losing investment in their manager’s success.

A precursor to disaster if Nuno’s squad no longer buy in to his ability to turn around their dismal record of conceding goals.

Report claims Bowen alone is invested in fighting for his manager

Writing in the NYTimes, Thomas pulls no punches with his article title:

“Nuno’s side remain horribly reliant upon Jarrod Bowen. He scored the equaliser against West Brom, but struggled to inspire another comeback once the visitors had restored their lead.

The winger had levelled matters up in the recent 1-1 draw against Queens Park Rangers, prompting the stadium announcer to boom: “Who else?” in recognition of his importance.

Konstantinos Mavropanos is sidelined with a knee injury, while Mohamadou Kante, Divine Mukasa and Tomas Soucek have helped ease the offensive burden on Bowen. But Engels, Manor Solomon, Taty Castellanos and Pablo have not followed suit. Joel Piroe, a proven goalscorer in the Championship, has been limited to substitute appearances.”

Many have highlighted the dizzying array of combinations Nuno has used for his starting eleven – not once has he fielded the same eleven names on the team sheet in consecutive fixtures, unlike 17 of his Championship competitors – yet his intransigence over failing goal keeper Mads Hermansen’s place in the side, along with a refusal to bring back outcasts Alvarez and Magassa reeks of favouritism over pragmatism.

Which tells me what West Ham are getting from Nuno is not what is needed: Sticking to favourites, ignoring outcasts and endless fiddling around with starting players out of position is one easy way to test the patience of players in the dressing room.

As Thomas clearly points out. Once that happens, the exit door cannot be far away. The next two games ahead of the break are crucial for Nuno – and for the club.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

Why can’t Nuno simply go back to basics. He needs to play with a number 6. A defensive midfielder to protect the defence. The goalkeeper isn’t good enough so replace him with Areola. If you play Bowen and Austibo on either flank , play Taty in the middle and keep him there where all strikers earn their bread and butter. Pablo can’t score a goal to save his life and the man on loan from Leeds might be a good finisher but he’s a bit slow and needs a run in the side to build confidence and understand his teammates better. If Nuno does these things results will improve

Can’t say I blame them I wouldn’t want to work for someone that ignores me or doesn’t speak to me because he doesn’t like what i said or did when it upset him AHH Bless shame if the truth hurts he is a bald head whether he likes it or not OR he has snow white magic mirror

For me there is no doubt about it. Players do know and see the weaknesses in a team put out by a manager and I doubt they have any faith in his ever changing tactics nor trust in his ability.

Too many players out of position as well as wasted talent in the squad.

When you see Kante at no. 10 (a brilliant box-to-box midfielder) there are 2 problems. First you are depriving the team of a very good midfield defender who can also break forwards with the ball. Second, at the same time you weaken the team in attack because he is not fast nor very skillful. He simply is not built to be a no 10. It’s a double whammy!

Bowen is head down playing for his teammates and the club, but when a manager repeats the same mistakes as if in a loop going back to last season, it must be disheartening and demoralising for the majority of players. He does not stand up for them and on a pitch they are in straitjackets.

Looking at this Newcastle United team v Everton.

Matthias Jaissle and his players looking to build on last weekend’s Premier League victory at Selhurst Park.

Whilst at the same time bounce back from the Carabao Cup defeat at the Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday.

Everton going through to the quarter-finals and a trip to League Two Fleetwood Town.

Tonight though a chance for Newcastle United to get back on track and for the Premier League table to look far better by the close of play on Monday.

A win against Everton would take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to seventh in the table with 14 points, the same number as Brentford in sixth and only a point behind Liverpool in fifth.

As a reminder, this was the Newcastle United team v Everton on Thursday night:

Hornicek, Dedic, Schar, Burn, Hall, Gonzalez, Willock, Ramsey, Barnes, Murphy, Osula

Hornicek, Dedic, Thiaw, Burn, Hall, Gonzalez, Willock, Joelinton, Fernandez-Pardo, Elanga, Wissa

Thiaw, Joelinton, Fernandez-Pardo, Elanga, Wissa

Obviously much depends on who is available tonight but I am predicting a completely different front three.

Anthony Elanga will hopefully now be able to start after his sub appearances and a no-brainer for him to replace Jacob Murphy.

I’m sure Matthias Jaissle would love to see United pressure Everton from the first whistle to try and get at them. If available I think Matias Fernandez-Pardo will replace Barnes and join Elanga in the team tonight to help do a high press. Playing MFP through the middle hasn’t been a success so far and therefore I see the Belgian on the left and Yoane Wissa returning to play through the middle if Osula is unavailable.

#2114. Newcastle United v Everton preview ahead of tonight’s St James’ Park match

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Welcome to the Newcastle United v Everton preview.

Newcastle look for revenge against the Toffees on Monday night as the two clubs face-off for the second time in just five days.

The blues got the better of United first time around when dumping the 2025 champions out of the League Cup and the Toon will be desperate to get their season back on track following such disappointment.

Three points for either side would have them in the top seven of the Premier League. The match will once again take place on live TV and a global audience will be waiting to see if the Toon can build on their win over Crystal Palace last weekend, as we look to put together a run of form ahead of the busy Christmas period that can make or break a season.

Newcastle have won two, drawn one and lost three of their last six league matches. Wins have come against Hull City and Crystal Palace whilst we’ve drawn with Bournemouth despite going 2-0 down. Defeats away to Leeds and Coventry saw the Toon get battered 4-1 on both occasions whereas Villa also took three points from St James Park in our last home match. The Toon have scored eight goals in these six matches but conceded a whopping twelve. The seven points gained has us twelfth in the league but a win would see us in seventh place.

Everton have only won one of their last six matches and have lost their last two in a row, drawing the other three. They beat Ipswich 1-0, drew with Tottenham, Man United and Hull and lost to both Chelsea and Arsenal. They’ve scored five goals in these six matches and conceded eight. A win on Monday would see them leapfrog the Toon and rocket seven places up the league. The Toffees were unbeaten in all competitions before the last two league matches so will be determined to alleviate this slump before it sees them slide towards a relegation scrap.

A quirk of the fixture list saw the two sides play each other in their last match having been drawn together at the Hill Dickinson stadium in the League Cup. Despite a promising start for United, this was ultimately a night to forget. Everton survived some early pressure before taking a two-goal lead into halftime. A number of substitutions saw the Toon attempt to wrest some momentum back from the Toffees. Any romantic notion of a famous comeback however was dispelled in the sixty-ninth visit when Everton scored again to take a three-goal advantage. There was still time for Dan Burn to net a late consolation but it was too little, too late as Everton dashed out Wembley dreams.

Newcastle haven’t beaten Everton in their last three visits to St James’ Park.

The Toon have lost only once in five home matches in all competitions this season.

NUFC have scored thirteen goals in their past eight home matches against Everton.

The 2007/08 season had very few highlights under Sam Allardyce who was thankfully shown the door in January. Big Sam had overseen only seven Premier League victories in twenty-one matches at the Toon. The Toffees visited St James’ Park in early October and the two sides played out a quite incredible five-goal thriller. Newcastle were the better team in the first half but were wasteful in front of goal as misses from Martins, N’Zogbia and Geremi looked to ensure that the teams were to go into the half-time break goalless. Thankfully Nicky Butt volleyed home at the Leazes End just before the interval to give the Toon the initiative. Anyone thinking this would mean NUFC would have things all their own way however were to have another thing coming when Johnson equalised just a few minutes into the second half to place the tie on a knife edge. An end-to-end second forty-five saw both sides push for a winner without really looking like they believed it possible until late substitutes were to make the difference. With just five minutes left, Emre picked up the ball outside of the area and unleashed an absolute rocket into the bottom corner from fully twenty-five yards out. A few minutes later, the Turkish midfielder turned provider when floating a freekick into the danger zone for Michael Owen to nod a header in off the bar and seal the destination of the points. There was still time for a wicked deflection to completely bamboozle Shay Given and end up in the back of the net but this was followed by the final whistle as United were able to celebrate three memorable points. Newcastle 3-2 Everton.

Antony Gordon came through the youth system at Everton having joined their academy at eleven years old. He made his debut in the Europa League aged just sixteen and spent six years at the Toffees. He played sixty-five league matches and scored seven goals over a six year period. He joined Newcastle in January 2023 under difficult circumstances following a well-publicised incident where he was harassed by supporters when leaving the stadium following a 0-0 draw with Southampton. He’d go on to enjoy an eventful three and half years at St James Park as NUFC qualified twice for the Champions League and he helped United to Wembley for the 2025 League Cup final, finally breaking a long-standing trophy duck in 2025. The 2025 League Cup would show both the good and bad of Anthony Gordon, scoring crucial goals in both legs of a semi-final success but being suspended for the final for a needless sending off just a few weeks later, meaning he missed out on playing in the greatest game of our recent history. He signed for Barcelona for over sixty-nine million pounds a few months back having scored twenty-four league goals in one-hundred-and-eleven appearances.

Paul Gascoigne was arguably one of the most naturally talented players to have ever come out of our country. Born in Gateshead, he made his debut for the Toon in 1985 and scored twenty-five goals in one-hundred appearances before signing for Tottenham in 1988. A million words could be written about ‘Gazza’ both on and off the pitch, books can and have been written about such an enigmatic figure. His story is eventful, intriguing, funny and tragic in equal measure. He played for Everton from 2000-2002 and scored a single goal in thirty-two league matches.

David Ginola was perhaps one of the most exciting players ever to represent NUFC in the Premier League era. Highlights of his two years on Tyneside include superb goals against Sheffield Wednesday, Man United and Ferencvaros, whilst equally memorable was his ability to whip the ball into the box loading the bullets for Sir Les and then Shearer to fire home. Tragically sold to Spurs by Kenny Dalglish in the same summer that Ferdinand also went to White Hart Lane, Ginola became something of a pantomime villain when playing against NUFC for the remainder of his career. Thankfully his retirement has seen a thawing in relations and he’s rightly remembered by Toon fans as a modern day legend. He played for Everton in 2002 but made only five league appearances for the Toffees.

Matthias Jaissle after a 3-1 defeat away at Everton in the League Cup: “Shocking and frustrating but if you just see the bigger picture, we did well in many aspects of the game. We of course are disappointed with the result, it’s also a bit shocking at the moment because overall the game was not that bad, but it’s the story of the season so far, that in situations where it really counts we lack the clinical approach to solve the situations. Just thinking about the first goal, it’s no risk zone, we clear the ball and nothing happens, and a couple of seconds later we concede a goal out of nothing. The second one is also frustrating in my point of view, we deserved to have a penalty then we miss in a transition to defend our own box which again is difficult to accept. We have clear rules then how to behave. We need to learn quickly. For me it’s about being mature in the situations, more clinical to solve the situations and not allowing almost a gift for the opposition to score. It feels like the opposition is not giving us these gifts at the moment so we need to avoid that.”

David Moyes after a 3-1 win against Newcastle United: “I thought it was a tough game. Newcastle had moments in the game but I think the Premier League is a bit like this at the moment. I think the games are quite close. You could be defending for twenty minutes and then you might be better for another twenty minutes. I think the games are very tight. Obviously we got the goals at good times, certainly the third goal sort of killed the game off at that time when Newcastle were probably better at the start of the second half.”

Newcastle United fans food bank will once again be collecting opposite the Gallowgate end and gratefully receiving food, money and toiletries for those in need. Of particular interest are non-perishable food and drink items (such as noodles, pasta, rice, canned food, soup, cereal, cordial, long life milk etc) as well as toiletries such as shower gel, shampoo, toothpaste and sanitary products. Please give whatever you can, any donation is very much appreciated.

For further info and/or to donate online go to Newcastle Foodbank

Thursday night was hugely disappointing for everyone concerned with NUFC for a number of reasons. The carrot of a match against League Two Fleetwood Town for a place in the cup semi-final was carelessly tossed away. That’s gone now and it’s important we build up a head of steam in the Premier League having got things back on track last weekend with a win over Crystal Palace. Newcastle need revenge against Everton and I fancy us to get it with two early goals putting the match to bed in the first half. Newcastle 2-0 Everton.

#2113. Martin O'Neill admits it's 'remarkable' Celtic still top after Falkirk loss

Martin O'Neill acknowledges that it is "remarkable" that Celtic remain top of the Scottish Premiership after dropping more points against Falkirk.

The Hoops were well beaten by the Bairns, 2-0, as they lost their second game of the season.

Their defeat followed a 2-2 draw with Dundee United last midweek and added to a gloomy recent spate of poor performances and results in all competitions which sits at just three wins from 10 matches in all competitions.

For O'Neill he insists he saw enough from his side this afternoon to suggest they should have beaten their opponents.

🗣️ “Remarkably, we’re still top of the league.” 🗣️ “We came from a mile behind last season to win the league.” 🗣️ “I keep out the noise.” Martin O’Neill says Celtic will “get a reaction” after their 2-0 loss to Falkirk ⤵️ https://t.co/DN1V5FRHbE

— Sky Sports Scotland (@ScotlandSky) November 1, 2026

But he admits they missed too many chances, as has happened too often this campaign already with Celts missing the chance to go seven clear at the summit.

"Is there any worry? Remarkably we're still top of the league," O'Neill said when asked the question by Sky Sports' Luke Shanley.

"We came from a mile behind last year to win the league. On two or three occasions as well. We're still in a decent position at this minute and we've played a lot of football as well."

Pushed by the reporter as to whether he feels Celtic could still be better, O'Neill added: "Of course we could. I'm not sure about your point here, I've just tried to explain to you, we missed goal after goal today.

"Their goalkeeper was magnificent, man of the match, so if we take even half our chances we would've won today."

#2112. Benfica vs Alverca - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 31 Oct 2026 16:22

Benfica will be looking to secure a sixth consecutive victory across all competitions when they welcome Alverca to Estadio da Luz on Monday evening for the final fixture of round 10 in the 2026-27 Liga Portugal season.

Marco Silva's side sit second in the Primeira Liga table with 22 points from nine matches, five behind leaders Porto, while the visitors are eighth after collecting 11 points from an available 27.

Benfica head into Monday's contest in confident mood after winning each of their last five matches across all competitions, scoring 16 goals and conceding just four during that run.

The Eagles' latest success came on Thursday, when they beat Gil Vicente 4-1 in the Taca da Liga quarter-finals, while their most recent league outing saw them claim a 2-1 victory away to Santa Clara.

Silva's side have also been difficult to stop at Estadio da Luz, where they are unbeaten in four league matches this season, winning three and drawing one, while their tally of 26 goals after nine rounds is the highest in the division.

With Porto facing bottom-placed Estoril Praia two days earlier, the five-point gap at the top could widen before Benfica take to the pitch, meaning the Eagles cannot afford another slip-up after dropping points at home against newly promoted Academico de Viseu on matchday one.

The hosts can, however, draw confidence from having won each of their last six meetings with Alverca, scoring at least twice in every encounter, including 2-1 victories in both meetings last season.

Alverca, meanwhile, travel to Lisbon after losing their last two matches without scoring, having been eliminated from the Taca de Portugal by Tondela before suffering a 1-0 home defeat to Arouca in the league.

Sergio Ferreira's side had enjoyed a more productive spell before those setbacks, recording successive league victories over Nacional, Rio Ave and Famalicao, but the current run leaves the Ribatejo club at risk of losing three consecutive matches for the first time this season.

Six points adrift of the continental places, Alverca are just one point and four positions better off than at the same stage last term, when they returned to the top flight after a 22-year absence, and a positive result on Monday could provide a timely boost to their hopes of a European push.

Ferreira's team can take some encouragement from their recent away form, having won their last two league matches on the road, though both of the visitors' Primeira Liga defeats outside their Ribatejo ground this season came against Porto and Sporting Lisbon, with another daunting test against one of the traditional big three awaiting them on Monday.

Benfica remain without Enzo Barrenechea, who is recovering from knee surgery, while Leandro Barreiro is also expected to miss out as he continues his recovery from injury.

Daniel Banjaqui is a doubt after missing recent matches with a muscle problem, although Jakub Kaminski is back to full fitness, having been named as an unused substitute in the midweek victory over Gil Vicente.

Jhon Duran was sent off after the final whistle of Benfica's victory over Santa Clara but has since featured in the Taca da Liga, with any disciplinary sanction relating to that dismissal still pending, meaning he should be available for Monday's encounter.

Alverca, meanwhile, are expected to be without Steven Baseya and Andre Filipe Cunha Vidigal, both of whom were shown red cards in their previous outing and will serve suspensions here.

The visitors are also expected to remain without Sabit Abdulai, Noah Raveyre, Bastien Meupiyou and Julian Martinez, with all four continuing their respective recoveries from injury.

Benfica have been in excellent form over the last few weeks and should have enough attacking quality to take advantage of an Alverca side missing two players through suspension.

The visitors have scored eight goals in four away league matches this season, suggesting they could cause problems at the other end, but the Eagles' strong home record points towards a comfortable victory for the hosts.

#2111. Nuno Has Had Long Enough – West Ham Need a Change

I’ve seen enough. For me, Nuno Espírito Santo’s time as West Ham manager should be up.

I’ve had nearly 24 hours to reflect on the dreadful 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion, and without the immediate anger and frustration of the final whistle, my opinion hasn’t changed. If anything, I’m even more convinced that Nuno isn’t the man to take West Ham forward.

This isn’t simply a reaction to one bad result or even two consecutive defeats. It’s the culmination of more than a year of watching a manager who still doesn’t appear to know his best team, his preferred formation or how to get the best out of the attacking players at his disposal.

The football has become stale, the players look unmotivated and, perhaps most worrying of all, I’m struggling to see any genuine improvement.

Jarrod Bowen says words are no longer enough, and I completely agree. But when I look back at our performances throughout the season, I’m not convinced these last two defeats represent some sudden collapse in standards. I think the problems have been there for quite some time.

In my latest video, I explain why I’ve finally lost faith in Nuno, why I don’t believe this is an overreaction and why West Ham need to act before our promotion ambitions suffer any further damage.

I’m also concerned about the empty seats, the growing apathy amongst supporters and the fact that watching West Ham has become such a chore.

I know plenty of supporters will disagree with me, and that’s absolutely fine. We all want West Ham to succeed.

But for me, the time has come for a change.

Nuno has had long enough. West Ham need to move on.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

#2110. Nuno gets a huge slice of positive news ahead of must-win Cardiff City encounter | West Ham News

Under fire Nuno Espírito Santo has a couple of games coming up that are in, in effect, must-win if West Ham are to get back on track with their promotion push and keep up with league leaders Middlesborough.

Names are already being thrown around was possible successors should Nuno falter in the last two games heading into the two week international break.

Walker Peters is unlikely to make Wednesday night’s game but opponents Cardiff face much greater challenges

Cardiff City’s injury crisis has deepened ahead of West Ham’s visit, with Brian Barry-Murphy facing mounting selection headaches and fresh concerns”

#2109. Defender lifts the lid on West Ham dressing room chaos | West Ham News

West Ham United’s dressing room must have felt as if it has been under siege for most of the last three years, with a string of managerial misfires and sackings, disruptive and outright ‘want  – away’ stars and two relegation battles fought in succession.

On top, of course the ‘BS out’ fan protests further contributed to the controversy surrounding the club, which peaked with relegation being confirmed last May  – and then the historic allegations forcing Chairman David Sullivan to quit just weeks after Vice Chair Karren Brady’s resignation.

Former Hammers defender Emerson has described the way in which the bombshell that was the  Lucas Paquetá inquiry catapulted the whole club into chaos, not long after the idyllic summer of ‘2023 – where it has seemingly remained ever since.

According to sportwitness.co.uk, Paquetá’s fellow countryman Emerson reckoned the whole Hammers dressing room was taken by surprise and plunged into controversy:

“The midfielder openly admitted that the case had taken a severe strain on his mental health. Palmieri now admits that it was not easy for everyone else at West Ham either…

Fellow countrymen Emerson Palmieri and Lucas Paqueta back in happier times before the storms broke in the Irons’ dressing room and beyond

“It was very tough because it caught us all by surprise..

I was taken aback when these kinds of allegations started to surface. And then we saw the scale it reached. He was facing the possibility of a suspension—or even a lifetime ban from football. He was deeply saddened by everything that was being linked to his name.”

Few fans perhaps appreciate the upset on the whole West Ham team and the dressing room created by the two-year long FA inquiry.

Certainly Lucas Paquetá never reached the heights of his first season as a Hammer after living with the spectre of a lifetime ban hanging over his head for years.

The player lost his dream move to Manchester City – and perhaps more importantly West Ham United were forced to try and maintain their Premier League standing whilst the allegations and the FA inquiry rolled over their heads like some impending thunderstorm.

In hindsight, it is little wonder that relegation resulted last May after the litany of crises involving the players, the club and its owners pretty much ever since that idyllic June day in 2023.

David Sullivan denies all of the historic allegations made against him

#2107. Championship striker pinpoints Hammers’ problem and offers hope for week ahead | West Ham News

Amongst the many voices raised over Nuno’s travails at West Ham following two consecutive home defeats, some opinions  deserve more consideration than others.

One former Championship player who knows only too well the challenges faced by teams struggling to compete in this, the toughest of the English leagues, has added to the growing suggestion that West Ham’s home form is suspect due to the weight of home expectation.

Important to remember that all three of the Irons’ defeats this season have come in front of an increasingly vocal, critical home fan base at London Stadium, and former Hull city and Peterborough striker Aaron McLean is certain it’s all down to the pressures of playing at home.

Writing for the bbc.co.uk after witnessing the Hammers’ second capitulation in two consecutive home games, McLean suggests:

“West Ham just don’t seem to be handling the pressure.

The fanbase is very split in terms of whether they want Nuno Espirito Santo in charge but the thing you have to do when playing for West Ham in front of 60,000 fans is put in a performance and if you’re in the Championship, you have to win.

BBC pundit McLean believes the Hammers squad aren’t coping with the pressure of playing in front of their own, demanding fan base at home.

“When you have a lovely stadium and playing surface, teams want to go there and enjoy it.

If you make your home ground a fortress, that can work for you but at the moment, the London Stadium is not a fortress and teams are going there and enjoying the experience, which is the total opposite of what West Ham need.”

As we wrote last week, the very weight of expectation appears to be hanging heavily around the players’ necks at present. If that is the case then the up and coming away fixtures at Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers this week will carry no such difficulties – merely unending vocal support from a travelling support that simply sings its heart out – whatever the match situation.

Just what Nuno’s men need right now. A couple of away days before the international break with the chance to get back to winning ways, without the weight of the world on their shoulders. Dealing with the pressure at home is another problem altogether.

#2106. Wouter Vrancken reveals Hearts star in hospital after Hibs defeat

Wouter Vrancken has revealed Tomas Magnusson was taken to hospital after being forced off for Heart of Midlothian in their Premier Sports Cup semi-final defeat to Hibernian.

The manager was left deflated at full-time as his side fell 2-1 to their rivals with a return to Hampden Park next month within touching distance.

The Jambos had led the action within the first four minutes when Claudio Braga found the net but their opponents turned the game on its head before half-time thanks to goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath.

Vrancken was concerned with more crocked stars with both Magnusson and Calvin Miller having to go off injured.

And the Belgian head coach has now explained the extent of those issues. "I didn't see Tomas because Tomas is to the hospital," said Vrancken. "Calvin was in a brace but it's always difficult to say directly after the game. So we have to wait for a scan tomorrow or the day after.

"The doctor and medical staff, they did their concussion test on the pitch, at that moment. (Magnusson) passed the concussion test and then he came to me to come in.

"Then he was going left and right, he couldn't stand on his legs anymore. When I saw it, there's no doubt in your head that you're going to let him on the pitch at that moment, because you cannot take the risk.

"Then he saw it himself also at the moment. He said, 'no, I can't do it. And then we had to change him, and now he's to the hospital, so I don't know."

#2105. Gil Vicente vs Vitoria de Guimaraes - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 31 Oct 2026 16:35

Gil Vicente will be looking to end their recent wait for a victory over Vitoria de Guimaraes when the two sides meet in a Minho derby at the Estadio Cidade de Barcelos on Monday evening.

The visitors arrive in better spirits after recording an emphatic victory over Maritimo in their previous league match, although their poor away form offers the hosts some encouragement ahead of the local encounter.

Monday's fixture carries an added personal dimension for Gil boss Luis Pinto, who will come up against the club that dismissed him in March after he guided Vitoria to Taca da Liga glory in January.

Pinto took charge of Gil after turning down an opportunity to return to Vitoria during the summer, and he will be keen to get one over his former employers as his current side look to build on a decent start to the campaign.

Currently seventh in the Primeira Liga table and three points away from the continental places, the Roosters saw their three-match unbeaten league run and four-game sequence without defeat across all competitions come to an end with a 1-0 loss to Porto last weekend.

Gil suffered a further setback in midweek, losing 4-1 to Benfica at Estadio da Luz in the Taca da Liga quarter-finals, and will be looking to respond in Monday's Minho derby.

Pinto will also want to see an improvement in his side's attacking output, with the Roosters managing just eight league goals this season, a tally higher than only those of bottom-side Casa Pia and Estoril Praia, who have both scored five.

However, Gil have been much more impressive defensively, conceding just seven times in the Primeira Liga campaign, with only leaders Porto (four) and Santa Clara (six) allowing fewer goals.

The hosts will also be looking to end a three-game winless run on home soil (D1, L2) after winning their opening two fixtures in front of their own supporters, a record that offers little encouragement given their recent struggles in this fixture.

Indeed, Vitoria are unbeaten in their last five meetings with Gil, winning four of those encounters and keeping clean sheets in each of their most recent four, which should give the visitors confidence ahead of Monday's clash.

The Conquerors head into the derby on the back of consecutive wins without conceding, following their Taca de Portugal victory over ACDR Lamelas with an emphatic 5-0 thrashing of newly promoted Maritimo last weekend.

That result marked Vitoria's second league victory in their opening nine matches of the campaign and ended a five-game winless run in the top flight, leaving Tiago Margarido's side 13th in the standings with 10 goals scored and as many conceded.

However, the visitors have a poor away record to address on Monday, having lost all four of their league matches on the road this season to remain one of only two teams yet to collect a point away from home.

Vitoria de Guimaraes form (all competitions):

Gil will be without defender Antonio Espigares, who received a late red card in the Taca da Liga defeat to Benfica, although Marvin Elimbi is available after serving a one-match suspension following his dismissal against Porto.

The hosts are also expected to remain without Arthur Tchaptchet due to a fitness issue, while Mohamed Bamba continues his recovery from the serious knee injury that has kept him out since January.

Francesco Dias is unavailable for Vitoria through injury, while goalkeeper Gui is still recovering from a serious knee problem and Thiago Balieiro is also a doubt after missing the last three matches.

Arnel Jakupovic scored twice in the emphatic victory over Maritimo last time out, opening his account for the club since his summer move from Osijek, and is expected to retain his place in attack ahead of Alioune Ndoye.

Lucao; Esgaio, Elimbi, Buatu, Moreira; Lausen, Prioste; Murilo, S Garcia, Martins; Kaba

Vitoria de Guimaraes possible starting lineup:

Zych; Strata, Borevcovic, Sidibe, Mendes; Nogueira, Doucet; Gustavo Silva, Samu, Camara; Jakupovic

Vitoria have the stronger recent record in this fixture and will take confidence from their emphatic victory over Maritimo, but their struggles away from home make it difficult to back them to collect all three points, so a draw looks feasible.

#2103. Richarlison grabs last-gasp winner for 10-man Spurs in fiery Chelsea friendly

Tottenham concluded their tour Down Under with a 2-1 victory over London rivals Chelsea at Accor Stadium in Sydney.

Sandro Tonali put Tottenham in front with a deflected effort before Estêvão equalised for Chelsea minutes later. Tottenham’s cause was not helped by a red card for Austrian defender Kevin Danso, who lasted just three minutes after coming on at half-time.

After making a mistake, Danso brought João Pedro down and was given his marching orders for denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Chelsea came close to taking the lead with their one-man advantage only for Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky to make some crucial saves.Just as the game appeared to be heading to penalties, Richarlison scored on the follow-up after Jamie Donley hit the post in the final few seconds of added time.

Richarlison. 90+2. pic.twitter.com/VIOS4Jh7P2

Tottenham will take on Getafe and Hoffenheim back on home soil before taking on Brentford on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

Chelsea have four more pre-season games, including fixtures against Juventus and AC Milan, before travelling to Fulham in the opening Premier League game of the Xabi Alonso era.

There is the final whistle and the 10 men of Tottenham snatch victory at the death with Richarlison scoring with seconds remaining.

In the final few seconds of the game, 10-man Tottenham win it. Donley’s shot from just outside the box hits the post and Richarlison follows up to score. It would have been a close call on offside if VAR was in use but it is not and Tottenham will take victory in Sydney.

Tottenham are being forced into a late change as Kyerematen, who come on for Robertson and nearly scored that wonder solo goal, is being forced off injured and is replaced by Tingey.

Delap is found in the centre of the Tottenham box with a cross from the right but the striker’s header from around the penalty spot goes wide and does not really trouble the target.

Initially, after Danso’s red card, Chelsea were in the ascendancy with a man advantage but Tottenham have dealt pretty well down a man.

Kyerematen nearly scores a quite sensational solo goal from inside his own half before driving forward. As he approaches the Chelsea penalty area, he tries to pick out the top corner and his effort comes off the top of the bar.

Xabi Alonso is making seven changes, yes seven, at once! That includes the likes of Delap and Tosin, who takes the captain’s armband.

The changes keep coming as Williams-Barnett replaces Tel for Tottenham.

A reminder that if the game is level after 90 minutes there will be a penalty shoot-out.

Roberto de Zerbi is making a double substitution as Tye Hall and Kyerematen replace Bergvall and Robertson.

17-year-old Satpaev, who hails from Kazakhstan, is replacing Estevao for Chelsea. Satpaev, who was at Kairat and turns 18 in 11 day’s time, scored the other day for Chelsea against Western Sydney.

Moore, who was on loan at Rangers last season, is replacing Solomon for Tottenham.

Robertson is so, so lucky. He is under no pressure as a cross comes over from the left and he should clear it with ease. However, he tries to be too clever and chests it back looking for his goalkeeper. There is not enough on it, allowing Pedro to nip in but his effort from inside the six-yard box is saved. Pedro probably should have scored and Robertson is a relieved man. Kinsky at the moment is the reason why Tottenham are not a couple of goals behind.

Tottenham have found it tough to get forward a lot since Danso’s red card but they do counter now and it ends with Tonali having a shot from just outside the box but his effort is easily saved by Sharman-Lowe.

Chelsea make a change as Anselmino comes on for Hato.

Palmer plays a ball down the right channel to pick out the run in behind of Palestra, who then returns it back to Palmer inside the Tottenham penalty area. Palmer’s first-time effort from the edge of the box is blocked.

Kinsky makes another big save to deny Chelsea. Tonali, who thought he had been fouled, loses the ball deep inside his own half, before Estevao has a great chance to put Chelsea in front from inside the Tottenham penalty area but Kinsky makes the save. It would have been a touch soft to give a free-kick to Tottenham but in the Premier League you suspect Tonali would have been awarded a free-kick there.

Tottenham are going to make a change at the back in light of Danso’s red card. Hardy is going to come on for Gallagher, who is booed by some of the Chelsea fans inside Accor Stadium. The England Under-18 international Hardy has come on at right centre-back in place of Danso.

Chelsea hit the frame of the goal. Pedro cuts it back from the byline to the penalty spot. Estevao gets to it first and his shot takes a deflection off Robertson. Kinsky makes a brilliant reflex save to push it onto the bar before Colwill blazes over.

Roberto de Zerbi is slumped in his seat distinctly unimpressed, shaking his head in frustration and perhaps disgust.

Palmer takes the free-kick but his effort is always curling wide of the far post.

The Austrian defender came on at half-time but has lasted just three minutes before being given his marching orders. Danso makes an absolute mess of a pass back to him from Gray and lets the ball run past him. Pedro gets around him and looks destined to drive towards the Tottenham penalty area but is brought down. Danso is shown a red card as Davies was probably not going to get across in time and it was the denial of a goal-scoring opportunity. Why do that in a pre-season friendly? Stupid.

Tottenham are making two changes at the break as Richarlison and Danso come on for Solanke and Van Hecke. Chelsea have also made a substitution as 16-year-old Nicoll-Jazuli comes on.

It appears the more times you see the incident involving Wesley Fofana and Conor Gallagher right at the end of the first half the more it looks like a penalty. Fofana did not appear to get the ball and instead catches Gallagher so Tottenham can probably feel a little aggrieved not to be given a penalty.

What have you made of that first half? Remember you can share your thoughts and opinions in the comments section at the bottom of the blog.

Possession: Chelsea 31%-69% TottenhamShots: 3-3Shots on target: 1-2Corners: 0-1

The first half is brought to an end and it is level at 1-1 at the break in Sydney.

Should Tottenham have been awarded a penalty? Robertson whips the ball in from the left to pick out the run of Gallagher into the box. Gallagher appeared to get to the ball ahead of Fofana, who seemingly then took Gallagher out but the referee does not point to the spot. That was a risky challenge to say the least from Fofana and on first viewing probably should have result in a penalty.

Palmer plays the ball forward to pick out the run in behind of Pedro, who has a two-on-one with Kinsky but the offside flag quickly goes up. Pedro was miles offside.

That was a decent opportunity for Tottenham. Tel finds the underlapping Davies with a pass towards the byline and the latter plays it across the six-yard box but Solanke was not there to meet it. Had Solanke read that, it would have been a simple tap-in.

Tel comes close to putting Tottenham back in front. It would have been a great solo goal as he drives inside from the left wing and moves into the Chelsea penalty area. He gets the better of Essugo on the corner of the six-yard box but is denied by a decent save from Sharman-Lowe.

Pedro has a chance to put Chelsea in front but his effort goes wide. Chelsea steal possession inside the Tottenham half after a poor pass from Robertson and the ball is then played forward to Pedro, who shoots from just inside the Tottenham box but his effort goes wide of the far post. Davies did just enough to put Pedro off.

Tottenham have two penalty appeals in quick succession turned down. First was for a potential handball by Essugo and then a push by Palestra on Tel. The handball would have been very harsh and the second incident was never a foul on Tel, who was losing his balance anyway.

Chelsea gift possession away deep inside their own half and Tel’s eyes light up. The ball rolls across to the Frenchman in a central position just outside the box and he opens up his body, trying to curl one into the top corner, but gets his first-time effort all wrong and his shot misses the target by a mile.

Like London buses, two goals come in quick succession and Chelsea are back on level terms. Chelsea counter from deep inside their own half and the ball ends up with Gittens on the left. From the corner of the box, he crosses towards the far post. It takes a touch off a Tottenham defender and ends up at the back post where Estevao, one of the smallest men on the pitch, beats Robertson and heads into the opposite corner.

Tottenham take the lead in Sydney courtesy of £100m signing Tonali. Solomon lays it back to Tonali who, from just outside the box, hits it first time and his shot takes a big deflection off Colwill, taking it into the far corner and giving Sharman-Lowe in the Chelsea goal no chance. That was probably Tottenham’s first proper foray forward in the game.

It has been a pretty stop-start game as play continues to be halted by fouls. The two managers might enjoy seeing the passion of their teams but they will also want to see their sides actually play, which is quite difficult when fouls are being committed left, right and centre.

Van Hecke has already fouled his former teammate Pedro once and he bundles into him again. Van Hecke has a wry smile as he walks away and Pedro tells the referee that is now twice he has been fouled by Van Hecke. I think it is a fairly safe assumption that Van Hecke and Pedro do not like each other that much!

We are not even 10 minutes into this friendly but there is absolutely no love lost between these two sides and the challenges are flying in. Former Chelsea man Gallagher slides in on Essugo, which infuriates the Chelsea players. The referee takes his time to make his decision as both sides come to blows before giving out the first booking of the game to Gallagher.

Pedro is caught by Van Hecke out on Chelsea left and the latter is absolutely furious with that decision, believing he got the ball. However, replays show that he did not get the ball and a free-kick was the right decision. Those two were teammates at Brighton and supposedly were involved in a training ground altercation just over a year ago!

The free-kick is whipped in towards the back post and the last touch is deemed to have come off Chelsea, much to their chagrin.

Lavia catches Tonali late and eventually the referee blows his whistle to bring play back for the free-kick. In a Premier League game, that may well have been a booking for Lavia. It might be a pre-season game but there will be no love lost between these bitter rivals.

The pitch in Sydney is on the bobbly side, which will make slick passing more challenging, dare I say it probably not really possible or realistic.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Tottenham led out by Archie Gray and Chelsea by Levi Colwill. There is a lights show inside Accor Stadium as the teams making their way onto the pitch.

#2102. The Strange Pattern Behind Every Major West Ham Managerial Appointment

A social media post doing the rounds over the weekend has sparked an interesting debate among West Ham supporters, highlighting what some see as a recurring theme in the club’s managerial appointments under David Sullivan and the late David Gold.

The post lists a succession of West Ham managers and jokingly categorises them by their playing positions:

The less charitable description attached to Avram Grant is perhaps best left where it belongs, on social media. He actually never played professional football!

While the observation is obviously tongue-in-cheek, it does raise an intriguing point. Since Sullivan and Gold took control of West Ham in 2010, the club has overwhelmingly turned to former defenders and goalkeepers when appointing managers.

Defenders and goalkeepers are often associated with organisation, structure and caution. Many of the managers West Ham have appointed during the ownership era have certainly prioritised defensive solidity first and attacking football second.

Bilic – one in a long line of defenders or ‘keepers appointed as West Ham Manager

That said, West Ham have hardly looked defensively secure under Nuno this season, and many teams have taken full advantage of those weaknesses.

Allardyce built his reputation on pragmatism. Moyes delivered the most successful period of the modern era through discipline, shape and resilience. Even Pellegrini, despite his reputation for attacking football at Manchester City, spent much of his West Ham spell battling to find defensive balance.

The goalkeeper connection is perhaps even more interesting. Both Lopetegui and Nuno Espírito Santo were former keepers, with each enjoying success elsewhere before taking on the challenge in east London.

Of course, there is no evidence that Sullivan sat down with a shortlist and immediately crossed off every former midfielder or striker. Football management success rarely comes down to the position someone played during their career.

After all, some of the Premier League’s most successful modern managers have come from every area of the pitch.

Yet supporters often look for patterns when results are poor, and West Ham’s recent struggles have inevitably led to fresh examination of decision-making at boardroom level.

Whether the theory is meaningful or merely an amusing statistical quirk, one thing is certain, Hammers fans would probably care far less about a manager’s former position if the current team was climbing the Championship table.

Sometimes football’s strangest observations turn out to be nothing more than coincidence. This may well be one of them. But it is the sort of coincidence that will get supporters talking.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

What do you expect when you have unambitious, dullard, embarrassing, two bob, cheapo, gobby owners; you get tinpot appointments.

Loser managers that are unemployed and no-one else wants.

Even the reappointment of Moyes was an embarrassing and two bob appointment at the time as he’d been jobless since his first stint with us.

It was pure chance and an absolute fluke that he did well for us.

Pellegrini was the only ambitious appointment, and even that was only forced due to rioting from our supporters due to the owners lies and lack of ambition.

The sooner David Sullivan and his sons have no involvement in the club, the better.

He doesn’t look in the best of health, and he won’t be here forever.

I can think of something else which all those former and present West Ham managers might have in common. They were all unemployed and probably had all been sacked!

the other thing that they have in common, with the exception of Moyes is they’re all absolute rubbish. ( being nice).

#2101. If West Ham Cannot Sack Nuno – Then He Must Make These Immediate Changes

Calls for West Ham United manager Nuno Espírito Santo to be sacked are growing louder following consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion. The Hammers have dropped to eighth in the Championship, and supporters are understandably questioning whether the Portuguese coach is capable of leading the club back to the Premier League.

I certainly fall squarely into the camp of people who don’t believe Nuno can either motivate his players or outsmart many of his rival Championship managers. The football has become stale, the team looks disjointed and there is precious little evidence of a manager getting the best out of what should be a very competitive squad.

But if we’re absolutely honest with ourselves, I suspect most West Ham supporters would acknowledge that Nuno is nowhere near being sacked. So rather than simply demanding his removal, perhaps the more useful question is what he can actually change to get this team playing better.

There are several reasons why I suspect Espírito Santo will remain in charge for the foreseeable future.

Firstly, West Ham are still in a state of flux regarding the club’s ownership structure. Until the proposed changes involving Vanessa Gold’s shareholding are completed and the i’s are dotted and t’s crossed, there remains uncertainty about precisely who will be making the biggest decisions.

Secondly, despite bringing in the best part of £200million through summer player sales, there are questions about how much money the club actually has available. Whether West Ham would be willing or able to fund another managerial dismissal and appointment is unclear.

And thirdly, if Daniel Křetínský is indeed calling the shots, Nuno is very much the manager he backed to lead the club through this Championship campaign.

Which leaves us with a rather uncomfortable situation. A manager whose football is becoming increasingly difficult to defend, but who may nevertheless be extremely secure in his job.

The first thing I’d change is the defence.

Nuno needs to abandon the experiment of playing Morato at left-back and select a proper full-back in that position.

I appreciate that Morato has performed reasonably well at times, and his versatility has been useful. But ultimately he’s a central defender, and I don’t believe the arrangement is helping West Ham develop a balanced team.

Whether Nuno selects Adama Boiro or Ollie Scarles doesn’t particularly matter to me at this stage.

We need better balance, more natural movement down the left and defenders playing in positions they understand.

As I’ve said previously, Arne Engels appears to be guaranteed a game irrespective of how he performs. Meanwhile, Nuno seems to believe he can win the Championship without consistently selecting a recognised defensive midfielder.

West Ham have a wealth of options in central midfield, yet we repeatedly find ourselves overrun, unable to retain possession and exposed whenever opponents break forward.

For that reason, I think it’s probably time to change the midfield completely.

I’d be tempted to give Lewis Orford another opportunity alongside either Edson Álvarez or Soungoutou Magassa.

Both Álvarez and Magassa offer the possibility of greater defensive protection, something West Ham have been desperately lacking.

And with a more secure base behind him, Divine Mukasa could finally be deployed in his best position as a number ten.

He’s a wonderfully gifted young footballer, but we’re wasting too much of his ability by asking him to drop deep and collect possession from the centre-backs.

Get him further up the pitch, give him some protection behind him and let him start opening up opposition defences.

Between the sticks, Mads Hermansen hasn’t exactly covered himself in glory.

I’m not suggesting every goal West Ham concede is his fault, because the defending in front of him has frequently been dreadful.

But when a team is struggling this badly, nobody should be guaranteed their place simply because they’ve been selected regularly.

Nuno has an ex PCG goalkeeper in Alphonse Areola at his disposal… surely it’s worth a try?

Which brings us to the striking department.

Leading up to the Southampton game, plenty of people were keen to repeat the fallacy that West Ham couldn’t win football matches without Pablo.

It’s worth remembering that Pablo didn’t start the Hammers’ 6-0 victory against Wrexham, which I consider our most convincing performance of the season.

And following back-to-back defeats in which the £23million striker started both matches, I suspect that particular myth has been exposed to all but his most vociferous supporters.

I don’t question Pablo’s effort. He works hard, puts himself about and certainly isn’t afraid of making a tackle.

Unfortunately, those qualities alone don’t make somebody an effective Championship striker.

For that reason, I’d be inclined to give Joël Piroe, our only proven Championship goalscorer among the recognised centre-forwards, a proper opportunity to establish himself.

He hasn’t been given anything resembling a consistent run in the side, and I struggle to understand how Nuno can properly assess his options without giving him one.

I’m not suggesting Piroe is guaranteed to solve our problems.

Of course, all these changes will count for very little unless Nuno can find a way to motivate his players.

I have little doubt that West Ham possess a number of talented footballers, many of whom I suspect would look considerably better under different coaches.

Once the players cross that white line, tactics, organisation and selection become equally important.

And that is where Nuno continues to let himself down.

Whether any of my suggestions would make a significant difference, I genuinely don’t know.

But I do know that repeating the same errors time and again isn’t going to get West Ham back into contention for automatic promotion.

The players who have consistently underperformed need to be dropped, and those who haven’t had much of an opportunity deserve a chance.

We have enough players in this squad to try something different.

And frankly, that’s probably the best we can hope for at the moment.

Because as much as some West Ham supporters might wish for Nuno Espírito Santo’s removal, I suspect he’s currently extremely secure in his job.
