#2099. Man City 0-1 Brighton: Highlights, man of the match, stats as superb Seagulls haunt Enzo Maresca’s men on Halloween

By Oliver Thomas | 31 Oct 2026 16:59, Last updated: 31 Oct 2026 19:20

Premier League leaders Manchester City have suffered back-to-back top-flight defeats after losing 1-0 to third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

The Seagulls entered this contest seeking revenge after going out on penalties in the EFL Cup fourth round to Enzo Maresca’s side on Wednesday.

Having twice led in that cup tie, Brighton struck first yet again; this time through Yasin Ayari who took full advantage of a lapse in concentration from Matheus Nunes to sweep home from close range.

Man City had chances of their own through Iliman Ndiaye, Elliot Anderson and Nunes, but they struggled to keep the ball under the intensity of Brighton's press, while they continued to look shaky at the back.

As expected, the hosts dominated much of the second half, but Bart Verbruggen was in inspired form for the Seagulls between the sticks, and City’s 24-game top-flight scoring streak at the Etihad has now come to an end following an underwhelming attacking display.

Defeat for Man City, who also lost at Aston Villa last weekend, means that champions Arsenal will have the opportunity to climb above them to the top of the table if they avoid defeat against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

Victory for Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton, meanwhile, has seen them consolidate third position in the table, moving to within two points of Man City at the summit and climbing three points ahead of Chelsea in fourth spot.

Oliver Thomas live from the Etihad Stadium

After failing to win any of their previous four Premier League games against Brighton (D2 L2), Man City were aware of the threat posed by an equally free-scoring Brighton outfit who also caused multiple problems in the midweek EFL Cup tie.

A game between the Premier League’s top-two scoring teams, seemingly destined for a goal fest, turned out to be a tight affair as Brighton produced a disciplined, resolute display to claim their first-ever away win over Man City at the 19th time of asking (D4 L14).

Hurzeler’s side have admirably responded to recent setbacks, and for a club that has never finished higher than sixth in English football's top division, their performances this season – including statement wins over Arsenal and now Man City – have showcased why they are more than capable of challenging for Champions League qualification.

As for Man City, a surprisingly toothless display was met with frustrated groans from the Etihad faithful, and this rare blemish on their home record – just their second league defeat in 23 home matches– serves as a stark reminder that their defensive vulnerabilities must also be addressed.

The Sky Blues have conceded 12 goals across their last six fixtures in all competitions, shipping at least two goals in three of those games, while they have now gone six games in a row without a clean sheet for the first time since January/February 2025.

Avoiding a third straight league game without a win away against Nottingham Forest next weekend will be high on the agenda for Maresca, before his City side take on Fulham and then rivals Arsenal after the international break at the end of November.

Diego Gomez’s dangerous delivery from the right flank towards the far post is not dealt with by Matheus Nunes and the ball invertedly pings off Maxim De Cuyper’s shin, perfectly teeing up Yasin Ayari to sweep home from close range.

22th min: Iliman Ndiaye chance for Man City

Ndiaye glances a header agonisingly wide from inside the penalty area after great work from Elliot Anderson to deliver a cross from the right.

48th min: Maxim De Cuyper chance for Brighton

With Josko Gvardiol off the pitch for Man City, Gomez bursts down the right and picks out De Cuyper, who was in acres of space but slams his effort well over the crossbar.

52nd min: Iliman Ndiaye chance for Man City

Ndiaye's shot from a fairly tight angle on the right side of the penalty area is palmed onto the crossbar by Bart Verbruggen at his near post.

62nd min: Matheus Nunes chance for Man City

Substitute Rayan Cherki slips a perfectly-weighted through-ball to Nunes on the right. The Portuguese cuts inside but his shot is saved by Verbruggen’s strong right hand.

Every Brighton player deserve credit for contributing to a strong collective display at the Etihad, but Bart Verbruggen’s presence between the sticks made a huge difference for the Seagulls.

The Dutchman made seven saves in total across the 90 minutes and has now kept his sixth clean sheet in nine Premier League games this season, more than any other goalkeeper.

#2097. Morton may be struggling but charity is bringing hope to the community

Christmas is an important time of the year for Morton in the Community. Since 2019 the social impact arm of the struggling Championship club has taken part in Festive Friends, the programme run by the SPFL Trust to provide turkey and trimmings for those who need them most.

For the first time families from the east end of Greenock will also be invited to Cappielow for a separate dinner this year while a Boots and Pieces pop up shop in the town centre provides sports kit and equipment for  a community ranked the most deprived in the country.

“Think of the pressure families come under at Christmas,” says charity Chief Executive Brian McLaughlin. “They come under pressure to put stuff on their credit cards and it’s such a difficult time for everyone. Even for businesses and football clubs….”

For the local football club in Greenock this Christmas threatens to be more difficult than usual. Morton face a financial short-fall of £320,000 after main sponsors Dalrada failed to make promised payments on time.

A recent financial update from Financial Director Kenneth Weldin refused to rule out administration by ‘early to mid December’ unless a solution arrives soon. A fans’ Fighting Fund has raised over £70,000 and might buy a little more time.

The best hope now lies with a consortium of local businessmen led by businessman Raj Samrai and featuring local billionaire Sandy Easdale.

A £150,000-a-year investment package is on offer in return for 60 per cent of the club and ownership of Cappielow.

While there appears to be no great enthusiasm for an offer amongst members of Morton Club Together - the fan ownership group - 427 of the 1200 members voted in favour of a period of due diligence in order to give both parties a chance to work through the structure and terms of a deal. Alternative options are thin on the ground.

Working from an office in Cappielow, the charitable arm of the football club can do nothing but continue to offer help and support for a community which now has one more financial hardship to fret over. Shipyards and heavy industry left Greenock decades ago and the loss of the football club which has played out of Cappielow since 1879 would feel like another savage blow.

“This club has been a big part of my life for 20 years,” says McLaughlin. “My grandad used to be a steward at Cappielow and my dad and his twin brother used to jump the turnstiles.

“Saturday at 5pm is either the best or the worst part of a supporter’s week. And these are difficult times.

“But we can’t control what happens on that side of things.

“What we can control is the work that we do to support the wider community during difficult times.”

A former player with Greenock Juniors, McLaughlin always had a plan to forge a career out of football in some capacity.

After completing a degree in Sport Development he worked as a community coach for Street League before joining his local club as a Development Officer in 2014. In 2018 he was appointed Chief Executive of Morton in The Community, an award winning operation running over 20 initiatives to engage locals aged from 18 months to 80.

Billed as ‘The Heartbeat of Inverclyde’ the ticker of the local club has faltered more than once over the years.

There was a previous brush with administration until the Rae family - local confectioners - stepped in to prop things up and absorb years of losses. A move to community ownership in 2021 saw Morton Club Together assume majority control of a debt free club.

Where other fan owned operations appointed a figurehead, a captain of industry, to run the show Morton rely on volunteers with little or no experience of running a football club. And placing all their eggs in one financial basket proved a calamitous mistake when the Dalrada money dried up.

An investment package by Dutch ownership group Estrella has since been turned down and MCT members now debate why the local consortium should gain a 60% stake in the club and control of Cappielow simply for handing over the same amount of money every month as they do.

Resigned to the fact that fan ownership at Morton in its current form has failed many now fear that rejection of the consortium’s offer would render Greenock Morton the ghost of Christmas past.

“I am optimistic about everything,” says McLaughlin. “What I say to our staff and volunteers is that we need to focus on controlling the controllables.

“We are here to support the club any way we can. Because the club is a key part of the community and we really hope that the future is positive.

“If we do our bit we will be okay and we will continue to support people and I think we will be alright.

“And, touch wood, I think the football club will be okay as well.

“If they can continue to provide the football we will continue to build and provide the projects that Inverclyde needs.”

The needs of Greenock and its surrounding areas are deep-rooted. In the Scottish Index of Multiple Deprivation of 2020 Inverclyde was found to be the most deprived data zone in Scotland, with extreme scores for income, employment, health (including drug related hospital admissions), education and crime.

Around half of the region’s population live in the three of the most deprived localities. Workless households are amongst the highest in the UK while premature mortality is in the top 10 across local authorities.

“Inverclyde is top of the league table in so many areas for the wrong reasons,” says McLaughlin.

“At one point we were the covid capital of Scotland.

“We are top in terms of health and poverty rates and child poverty is through the roof.

“As a father that really affects me because I look at my two year old son and wonder what kind of life I want to give him. And what can I do to help other people have a better life?”

While the national game is regarded as a curse on society by some politicians at Holyrood, Morton in the Community are just one of the club charity arms reaching into local areas to improve lives through the power of football. Their work is neither sexy or appreciated and goes largely unseen.

This week marked the 50th anniversary of Morton’s greatest ever player, Andy Ritchie, moving to Greenock from Celtic.

Signing in time for a Wednesday night game against Davie Cooper’s Clydebank in October 1976 his first impressions of Cappielow were unfavourable. An old fire in the home dressing room stunk of gas and he gained the impression that Vikings had just looted the main stand stand and moved to for the escape boats 20 minutes before his arrival.

Viewed as a slightly archaic, shambolic, old school 20th century football stadium, Cappielow hasn’t changed a great deal in the five decades since. And yet, where the old shutters only opened for games and training sessions in days gone by, Morton in the Community have spent the last seven years since 2019 quietly turning the old place into a multi-purpose hub for those who need someone to talk to.

“That time from three to five on a Saturday is so important to a lot of people. But it can’t be the only time a stadium is open,” McLaughlin observes.

“What I really love about this job is that it’s not just dealing with the people who live for the three to five on a Saturday.

“People come in here and say, ‘I’m not a football fan, I have never been in here.’

“And that doesn’t bother me one bit because what happens on the pitch will happen. We can’t control that.

“What we can control is the impact we have on peoples’ lives.

“We can offer them a bit of hope. We can give them a wee bit of direction. Or a bit of support.

“That’s probably the biggest source of satisfaction for me. When I look back and say, ‘you know what? We helped someone today.”

Grassroots football offers weekly sessions. Worried that football is becoming a middle class game, McLaughlin grew up kicking a ball around the streets of Braeside but sees the cost of participation rising to a level parents can no longer meet.

“Football is becoming very expensive now. When I grew up I was fortunate because we played football in the street with a plastic ball using lampposts or bottles for goalposts and a driveway as a pitch.”

For a number of reasons that doesn’t happen now. Inverclyde has some of the highest stats in Scotland for childhood obesity in the under-fives and McLaughlin wants to introduce the kids of the area to movement, physical activity, sport, football, gymnastics via the charity’s nursery programme. To play football any way they can.

“We have delivered free provision for football holiday camps. We have also trialled ‘pay what you can’ for parents to walk in and put a tenner in a bucket, a pound in a bucket or nothing at all.

“And what you find is that the numbers are double or triple what we would normally get.

“We did a background survey asking people if they could afford to pay the normal £12 a day and the overwhelming answer was ‘no. The cost of playing football is a real issue now.”

Football now accounts for just 60 per cent of the charity’s activities they roll out. On a Monday night Team Talk opens the stadium up for those who feel the need to have a cup of a tea, a biscuit and just talk. On a Friday morning they co-host a session with Moving On Inverclyde, a local drug and alcohol recovery charity.

“Last week we had 16 men in a room. Some were 18 some were 50 plus, some had high flying careers, some less so.”

He takes pride in the story of one man who refused to leave his own home for years. He is now one of the charity’s volunteer facilitators, delivering programmes for Scottish Action for Mental Health after completing a degree.

“And all that started with coming to a freezing cold Cappielow on a Monday night for a cup of tea...”

For Inverclyde finding the money to keep the lights on at Cappielow is not just a case saving one of Scotland’s oldest football clubs. For some of the area’s most vulnerable people it’s a lifeline.

#2096. Arsenal receive early team news boost for Hull clash as suspension confirmed

By Ben Knapton | 31 Oct 2026 17:20

Arsenal have received an early team news boost for their Premier League clash with Hull City next weekend, as Tigers midfielder Matt Crooks will be suspended for the trip to the Emirates.

Sergej Jakirovic's side played out a gripping 2-2 draw with Ipswich Town at the MKM Stadium on Saturday, as Oli McBurnie and Tim Iroegbunam cancelled out efforts from Florentino Luis and Julio Enciso.

Crooks started the top-flight encounter on the bench, but the 32-year-old was brought on for John Egan at half time, when Hull were chasing the game at 1-0 down.

However, Crooks was cautioned on the hour mark for a poor challenge on Ipswich's Luis, thereby collecting his fifth booking of the season after previous yellows against Manchester United, Chelsea, Newcastle United and Everton.

Having been yellow-carded five times before the 19-game cut-off point, Crooks will now serve a one-game suspension, ruling him out of Hull's visit to North London next Saturday.

The former Middlesbrough man was a regular fixture in the Hull XI in the early weeks of the season, starting five of their first seven games of the Premier League campaign, missing matches against Coventry City and Aston Villa due to a thigh injury.

Crooks was an unused substitute in last weekend's 1-1 draw with Brentford, though, and his absence from the Hull XI against Ipswich as well suggests that his ban will not have a seismic impact on Jakirovic's plans next weekend.

Instead, Iroegbunam and Regan Slater are expected to pair up in midfield at the home of the champions, although Crooks's ban will deprive the Tigers of an experienced, tough-tackling engine room option.

Hull are already working without three midfielders due to injury in Darko Gyabi, Lucas Gourna-Douath and Eliot Matazo, although the former two are anticipated to return at some point in November.

Jakirovic has avoided a double suspension blow for the trip to Arsenal, though, as McBurnie is also on four yellow cards but avoided picking up a fatal fifth in Saturday's game.

Hull have especially fond memories of the Emirates Stadium, having shocked Arsene Wenger's Arsenal 2-1 in September 2008 shortly after being promoted to the Premier League for the first time.

However, the Tigers have since failed to win any of their last 14 games against the Gunners, suffering 12 defeats in that time, including a chaotic 3-2 loss in the 2013-14 FA Cup final.

Arsenal did the double over Hull in the 2016-17 Premier League season by an aggregate score of 6-1, thumping the Tigers 4-1 away before a 2-0 Emirates triumph in their most recent head-to-head.

#2095. City fire blanks in shoot-out as Maresca’s opening game ends in defeat by Inter

Manchester City lost the Asahi Super Dry Trophy 3-1 on a penalty shoot-out against Inter Milan.

Enzo Maresca took charge of the Premier  League runners-up for the first time since his arrival as Pep Guardiola’s replacement, though he was without many of his stars who had yet to return from World Cup duty.

One of the players missing was Elliot Anderson, the £116m signing from Nottingham Forest, though Jeremy Monga, 16, was an unused substitute after being brought in from Leicester City in the summer transfer window.

City took the lead on 14 minutes through Divin Mubamba as he tapped in an Antoine Semenyo cross, but Inter’s experienced defender Benjamin Pavard levelled just six minutes later when City failed to clear a corner.

The Premier League side dominated possession in the second half after an even first 45 minutes but could not find a way through. Phil Foden, the captain, was again underwhelming after a difficult year last season, but with the season still to come he had plenty of time to show his best form once more after signing a new contract at the Etihad.

The game went to penalties after full-time with no extra time played, and only Claudio Echeverri held his nerve for City as Inter Milan scored three of theirs, Matteo Lavelli netting the winning spot-kick.

Both teams learnt little from the match as Inter made 11 changes and City eight, though Maresca will have been impressed by Ryan McAidoo’s performance as a second-half substitute, as he regularly threatened from the right wing. The 18-year-old forward will surely be in demand from other clubs looking to loan him, and City may yet be tempted to keep him around for the coming season.

Savinho slices a shot wildly high and wide. Changes are coming.

Reis claims to meet a corner at the back post, but it comes off an Inter player. The corner switches to the right, and this one is cleared, for now. City keep the ball and Ait-Nouri picks out Gonzalez’s run, and he strains to shin it over.

Lewis has the ball in the box after quick feet from Savinho with the assist, and he prods the ball at Provedel.

Foden and Semenyo off, Sangare and Echeverri on. Lewis is City’s new captain.

On the front foot 👊 pic.twitter.com/AZC7UXYXrj

Foden sends in a corner, and Reis hooks a volley against the bar as the ball drops. Gonzalez gets back up to his feet slowly after that phase of play, and then sits back down as he awaits treatment.

City are camped in Inter’s half now, which is an improvement on the last half where it was more even, territorially.

McAidoo is released down the inside left, he clears his marker and aims for Semenyo, but Bisseck clears for a corner.

Pavard goes down after he is caught late from Ait-Nouri, but he’s fine to continue.

More subs now  Topalovic replaces Stankovic. Provedel replaces Martinez in goal.

Savinho might be the most dangerous player for City today, a sentence that has rarely been true in the last couple of years. McAidoo whips in a cross, which Henrique clears under no pressure.

Reis and Alleyne are the central defenders. Ait-Nouri is on the left, and Khusanov the right.

Stankovic gets a yellow as Savinho sprints down the inside left away from Inter Milan players. McAidoo is then tripped by Augusto, who hurt himself doing so.

A decent enough corner from Foden who swings the ball close to the back post, but the goalkeeper Martinez is fouled as the ball comes in.

The full slate of City changes, as Lewis has a shot blocked when a corner is not properly cleared. Savinho stands a cross up, but it comes to nothing. Khusanov has a shot scrambled away.

Reis and Mcaidoo, Ait-Nouri, Alleyne, and Gonzalez are on for City, with Gviardiol one of the players going off, as is Reijnders.

Frattesi, Henrique, Mosconi, Zielinski and Bastoni are the five Inter introductions, but there are more. Mkhitrayan has gone off, with Diouf, Idrrissou, and Augusto some of the exits too.

We go again. A billion subs have been made. So far, Frattesi is on. Let’s see what we know about the rest. Ait-Nouri is on.

It’s been more or less what you expect from a pre-season friendly in the humidity.

The players are yet to shake off their summer ice creams and really get sharp again, but there are some flashes of ability here and there.

Reijnders releases Semenyo, the Dutchman plays the ball into Savinho, who dances to the byline, pulls it back, but it’s then cleared from Bisseck.

That’s it for the half, and the action restarts in 15 minutes.

Savinho wriggles into the box but just fails to find Semenyo.

Mkhitaryan concedes a foul on Lewis in midfeild, and the half appears to be drifting to a bloodless close.

Savinho, maybe in his last game for City, brings the ball high up the right but then City are forced all the way back to Donnarumma.

City are not panicked by keeping the ball, and they look for a fresh opening.

Foden commits his own foul in midfield, this time on Mkhitaryan. There are a few minutes left before half-time, at which point we may see a few changes from both sides given the early stage of pre-season.

Foden swings in a corner that Savinho briefly keeps alive before Diouf clears, and Dimarco cannot quite reach the ball before it’s played back to Donnarumma.

Barella fouls Reijnders in midfield, but it’s nothing vicious.

Semenyo clips in a dangerous-looking cross from the left wing, but it’s deflected behind for a corner on the right.

Foden is tugged down in midfield, with the City man still failing to show much of his talent in the new season.

Mkhitaryan continues to find space in pockets on the left. In general, Inter are finding it very easy to trundle to the edge of the City box.

Donnarumma flaps at a cross, and Savinho and Lewis work to clear it momentarily.

Do you think the players are coping without a hydration break?

Dimarco is fed by Diouf, with the right wing-back finding the left wing-back. He’s on the right side of the pitch too, oddly, but his left-footed shot is far from dreadful, but easily stopped by Donnarumma.

City have some pressure and Kovacic hits a group of defenders with a volley from outside the box. It’s meek stuff from Maresca’s men so far but obviously, too early to draw much from it.

City are looking to build from the back through the middle, but they are quickly crowded out. Inter come forward once more.

Diouf forces a corner on the right wing as Donnarumma clears a cross. It’s taken short, Inter switch the ball left, but Mkhitaryan overhits a pass to the byline.

Mkhitaryan receives the ball on the left, inside the box, in another dangerous position. Lewis had drifted  too far inside, but the danger passes when the forward is flagged offside.

Inter are keeping the ball calmly at the back, finding spaces between the pressing City attackers.

They break through and Donnarumma beats away a low shot from Stankovic.

Benjmain Pavard scores! Manchester City fail to clear their lines and Pavard, who started the move, is on hope to finish with the keeper stricken.

Divin Mubamba gets the opener! Semenyo beats his right-bacck and crosses to the six-yard box for Mubamba to tap in.

14. Wonderful work from Semenyo 👊He beats his man on the left to get to the byline, squares it across goal and Divin converts from close range 🎯🐝 1-0 ⚪️ https://t.co/pCDrkfriLY

Dimarco volleys wide but he too was offside, and then Martinez saves from Reijnders at the other end. It’s a free-flowing match so far.

Stankovic goes close with an early header after Inter win their first corner of the match. It’s an open game so far.

City win two early corners, but they are both cleared. A bright start for the Premier League side. Esposito then goes close at the other end, but he was offside anyway.

A recent on-pitch spat over the captain’s armband between Liverpool players demonstrated that these friendlies are not simply warm-ups.

The fans are out in force in Hong Kong, where the Premier League continues to dominate attention.

Here’s what the former striker told Manchester City: “I’m looking forward to it. I’m not sure Enzo is going to change that much but some tweaks here and there.

“People talking about it being similar to when [Alex] Ferguson left but I don’t think it’s the same, they didn’t have the same infrastructure. He’s a top manager. He will want to put his own stamp on it.”

The biggest story in football right now is increasingly hard to ignore.

Gianni Infantino’s ludicrous plan was sunk almost as soon as it was announced, then he defended himself with such verve as to make himself look completely isolated and apart from the organisation itself, and now UEFA has said it is calling time.

The governing body says it has lost faith in the Peace Prize inventor, a problem which had been in the post for a while now.

The two London sides are facing off in their own pre-season friendly.

You can follow that live here, and find out which player has been sent off.

In their little costumes ahead of kick-off.

The venue in Hong Kong is decent enough and has started filling out. It’s a jaunty 26 degrees, 92% humidity, and raining too. It’s just like being in London during your worst nightmares, basically.

We’ll see how this continues, and if it does continue, over the coming weeks, but Phil Foden has the nod as captain for Enzo Maresca tonight.

Foden signed a new contract recently but has been well off his consistent best for some time now. Another poor season would put him in the frame for the exit door next summer, so this is a chance.

Captaining the side in Enzo's first match as boss 👍©️ pic.twitter.com/bcvIhwXMas

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester City and Inter Milan.

The two sides meet  at Kai Tak Sports Park, Hong  Kong as their pre-season work kicks up a gear ahead of the new campaign.

City are still getting used to life without Pep Guardiola, the coach who left after a decade of high spending and high performance.

In his place is Enzo Maresca, who is not shy with the chequebook himself.

Ayyoub Bouaddi, the outstanding 18-year-old Moroccan international, should soon arrive from Lille when a fee is agreed, but Elliot Anderson and Jeremy Monga have already been signed.

City were runners-up last season, so Maresca is under pressure not just to keep things going without Guardiola, but to get the team back to the top of English football. That looks to be a tough prospect with Arsenal likely to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle in the coming days.

Inter, meanwhile, have swooped to pick up John Stones on a free transfer after his contract ended at the Etihad Stadium, and he is joined by Manuel Akanji, another former City centre-back whose loan turned permanent in the summer.

Inter won Serie A last season under head coach Cristian Chivu, and they are still one of the best sides in Europe.

While this friendly is likely to be played at a reduced pace, and will be disrupted by rustiness and substitutes, we could still learn a lot about both sides going into the new campaign, and there may be the odd surprise thrown up by a young player looking to stake a claim ahead of his senior colleagues this year.

#2094. Bournemouth transfer news: Cherries hold 'initial talks' over swoop for Colombia international

By Ben Sully | 31 Oct 2026 17:48, Last updated: 31 Oct 2026 17:50

Bournemouth are reportedly interested in signing Vasco da Gama attacker Andres Gomez.

The Cherries have recent experience of negotiating with Vasco after signing Rayan from the Brazilian club in the January transfer window.

Rayan has proven to be a real asset for the south coast side, having scored nine goals and provided two assists in 29 competitive appearances.

Having already seen success from Rayan's move, the Cherries appear open to the possibility of recruiting another Vasco attacker.

According to TEAMtalk, the Cherries are 'seriously interested' in signing Gomez from the Brazilian side.

The report claims Bournemouth have already held 'initial discussions' and are 'expected' to table an offer in the winter transfer window.

The Bournemouth recruitment team, led by, are said to view the Colombia international as a similar profile of attacker to Rayan.

There is also a belief that a deal can be done below the €35m (£29.3m) Bournemouth paid to sign Rayan earlier this year, despite the fact that Gomez is under contract until 2031.

The right-footed winger began his senior career with Colombian side Millonarios before he spent 18 months with Real Salt Lake in the MLS.

A return of 15 goals and 15 assists in 65 matches earned him a move to French side Rennes, where he scored three goals in 19 appearances.

After struggling for starting opportunities in France, Gomez joined Vasco on a season-long loan deal in August 2025 before the move was converted into a permanent transfer in January.

The attacker has a regular fixture for Vasco this season, having netted eight goals and contributed six assists in 49 competitive matches.

Meanwhile, he has scored two goals in 11 appearances for Colombia and featured twice in his country's three friendlies during the most recent international break.

The possibility may now arise for Gomez to test himself back in Europe after failing to show his true potential during his brief stint with Rennes.

#2093. James Penrice hit with former referee verdict on 'instant red card' vs Aberdeen

James Penrice should have been "instantly" sent off for Rangers in their Premier Sports Cup semi-final against Aberdeen on Saturday evening.

That's the view of former FIFA referee Keith Hackett after he watched the defender catch Dons' Afeez Aremu high in a clash at Hampden.

Gers saw off their foes to reach the showpiece finale next month after Ryan Naderi found the net in his side's narrow 1-0 victory. But it could have been different had Penrice been shown a red card by referee Ryan Lee.

Penrice clearly caught Aremu on the hip with his studs and the debate raged on whether or not the force was enough to see Penrice given his marching orders. But after the whistler did not even produce a yellow for the challenge, VAR official John Beaton refused to intervene and the player continued.

Then he helped tee up Naderi for the winner.

Hackett had his say on Football Insider and insisted the former Hearts ace was lucky to avoid punishment. In fact the retired official could hardly believe the outcome.

He said: "I have to ask how James Penrice was allowed to stay on the field of play, when his high boot was in contact with the chest of his opponent.

"That was clearly serious foul play, and should have seen a red card produced instantly. The fact that no action was taken comes as a surprise. Why was there no intervention by VAR?"

Rangers will now face the winner of the Edinburgh Derby in the first cup final of the campaign.

#2092. Tottenham: Shocking James Maddison 90-minute stat sparks "concern" from Gus Poyet

By Ben Knapton | 31 Oct 2026 17:50

James Maddison's repeated injuries and inability to complete a full 90 minutes in the Premier League are a "concern" for Tottenham Hotspur, Gus Poyet has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The 29-year-old was dropped from Tottenham's starting lineup to face Crystal Palace in Saturday's 5.30pm kickoff, having tweaked a groin muscle against Chelsea in last weekend's 2-0 win.

Maddison was declared fit by De Zerbi in his pre-game press conference, but the Italian decided to take no chances with the Englishman, instead bringing Dominic Solanke back into the XI.

Maddison's most recent injury was nowhere near as bad as first feared, though, as concerns over another knee issue were sparked when the midfielder sat down on the turf at Stamford Bridge.

However, following yet another all-too familiar setback for Maddison, ex-Spurs midfielder Poyet has admitted that the 29-year-old's repeated failure to play a full match is worrying.

"He has had a good career so far, but yes these injuries are a concern, because he can’t last the 90 minutes," Poyet said in an exclusive interview with Sports Mole.

"So he has to recover now and look to get back playing again to ensure he can last 90 minutes at the top level. He is a good creative player, so useful and we saw what he can do as he showed against Coventry."

De Zerbi was asked about Maddison's absence from the first XI by Sky Sports News ahead of kickoff vs. Palace, to which he replied: "Not just for the physical condition. To be clear James is very important for us when he feels good, when he plays."

Maddison has been limited to just two Premier League starts so far this season, featuring from the off against Coventry City and opening the scoring with a stunning curler from outside the box in that 3-1 win.

The ex-Leicester City man held his place in the XI for the trip to Chelsea last weekend and completed 86% of his passes while also drawing two fouls before his premature withdrawal.

Prior to Spurs' clash with Crystal Palace, Maddison averaged just 30 minutes per match in all competitions this season, having played for 210 minutes across seven games in the Premier League and EFL Cup.

Maddison made five successive substitute appearances against Brentford, Everton, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Manchester United - with a shoulder injury sandwiched in between - before lasting 69 minutes of the win over Coventry and 51 minutes against Chelsea.

The midfielder was also restricted to just 34 minutes in three substitute appearances in the 2025-26 Premier League, having spent the majority of the campaign recovering from a serious ACL injury.

Furthermore, Maddison only lasted 90 minutes three times in the 2024-25 season; vs. Rangers in the Europa League in December 2024, and against Tamworth in the FA Cup and Everton in the Premier League on January 12 and 19 respectively - almost two full years ago.

While an indispensable creative asset to Spurs when fully fit, Maddison only playing a full game three times since the start of the 2024-25 season is both shocking and concerning, both for himself and De Zerbi.

Gus Poyet was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill sports betting.

#2091. Martin O'Neill explains Jota omission before Falkirk clash

Martin O'Neill has explained his decision to leave Jota out of Celtic's matchday squad against Falkirk.

The Portuguese winger has only recently returned from long-term injury with an ACL problem and he has made four appearances since his comeback against Motherwell last month.

He was not named in the squad at all by the manager for this afternoon's test against the Bairns who are sitting sixth in the Scottish Premiership and in decent form of their own.

O'Neill, though, put all worries about a potential setback to bed as he revealed the playmaker has been left out due to the fact that Falkirk play their games on an astroturf pitch.

Asked on Sky Sports why the wide man is not involved and whether that may be something for punters to worry about, the Northern Irishman calmed those fears.

"No, he's just back from the injury and I think in terms of the pitch, we felt it's best with the type of injury he's recovering from, to leave him," he said.

Celtic found themselves a goal down to Ethan Ross' finish within the first three minutes of action. At the time of writing they remain 1-0 behind.

#2090. Exciting young talent JJ Gabriel makes debut as Man Utd beat Atletico Madrid

JJ Gabriel showed glimpses of his potential as he made his Manchester United debut in their 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid in Stockholm.

The 15-year-old may have been introduced with only eight minutes remaining, but, given how highly rated he is, it was a significant move by Michael Carrick to give him game time in the senior team.

There were hints of why Gabriel is so well regarded during those eight minutes, as he found space in the centre of the pitch and linked well with Leny Yoro. But he was also on the receiving end of some physical challenges – something he will have to grow accustomed to the more he plays at senior level.

Yoro, who himself made his senior debut as a 16-year-old for Lille, was impressed by Gabriel and said: “He’s a really good player. He is still really young and still has a lot to learn and a lot to improve on but he’s really humble and still working, so I’m happy for him to get his first minutes. I hope, for him, it’s going to continue like that.”

United fought back after conceding an early goal against Atletico to secure their second win of pre-season.

They fell behind in the sixth minute when Arnau Ortiz’s cross into the box evaded everyone, including United keeper Tom Heaton before hitting the back of the net.

United got the equaliser their performance deserved when the impressive Shea Lacey showed his skill in the box and was fouled. From the resulting penalty, Bryan Mbeumo sent the goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

In the 72nd minute, Mbeumo got his second of the afternoon after he bundled the ball home after the United press forced Atletico into a mistake.

The Spanish side hit the post twice in the closing stages but United held on to win.

“We had a clear plan before the game, everyone stuck to it and made the game enjoyable,” Mbeumo said. “We work really hard during training for these games, the main goal is to be ready for the season starting. I have done great things on the right but also as a striker.

“I think I am more experienced on the wing but I enjoy playing as a striker. For an offensive player, it is always good to score for the team.”

United dominating possession in the opening stages with Atletico happy to sit off and let the Premier League side have it. Even in pre-season, Diego Simeone has his side set up well to defend.

The visit to the Strawberry Arena means United are back at the stadium where they won the 2017 Europa League.

📸 Wayne Rooney, 2017 🏆#UEL | @ManUtd pic.twitter.com/HxZVn1mAEQ

Gianni Infantino is facing an ultimatum from Uefa: resign or face an emergency no-confidence vote.

It is understood all 55 of Uefa’s member nations would opt to oust Infantino in a vote of no-confidence if he refuses to step down. Uefa can trigger such a vote with just 43 member nations.

European football’s governing body announced a loss of confidence on Saturday morning and has demanded change after Infantino was forced to scrap his £15bn plan to sell a stake in the World Cup.

Uefa’s statement followed widespread opposition and a revolt within Fifa’s ranks that staff are calling “kill the monster”.

The Football Association backed Uefa’s stance, saying: “We fully support Uefa’s position. It is time for a full and robust review of Fifa’s leadership and governance to ensure that the global game is run transparently, for the benefit of all 211 member nations and with the long-term stewardship of football at its heart.”

Atletico: Oblak, Domínguez, Le Normand, Hancko, Ruggeri, Koke, Obed Vargas, Castillo, Arnau Ortiz, Carlos Martín, Lookman

United: Heaton; Yoro, Maguire (c), Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Amad, Lacey, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Bayindir, Mee, Vitek, Amass, Armer, Kamason, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Thwaites, Gabriel, Williams, Zirkzee.

Good afternoon and welcome to pre-season coverage of Manchester United against Atletico Madrid.

Michael Carrick’s squad continue their preparations for the new season with a trip to the Swedish capital, Stockholm, where they face Diego Simeone’s La Liga side.

Last week, United cruised to a 5-0 victory over Rosenborg but today will be their first real test. They are slowly starting to get players back but the likes of captain Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans will not be involved.

“I think we’re in a good place. I think there’s four weeks to go to the start and we’re gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup as we progress,” Carrick said.

“But I think a little bit of patience and time and trying to keep ahead and as I said, keeping everyone fit but moving forward is a really good direction to go in. And as it stands right now, I think we’re in a pretty good place. So, the boys will get better as we go.”

One player who will be looking to impress is Mason Mount. He has had an injury-hit spell at Old Trafford but is fit and ready to go for the season. He is also growing into a leadership role at the club.

Struggling for results in Serie A, Sassuolo and Fiorentina face off at Mapei Stadium on Monday in a meeting of two out-of-form sides.

Sassuolo's cavalier approach may have provided entertainment while they were securing encouraging results earlier in the campaign, but it always looked unsustainable.

The Neroverdi collected seven points from their opening four matches, including a 2-2 draw in their regional tussle with Bologna before beating Juventus 3-2 in front of their supporters.

The Emilia-Romagna outfit have continued to score, netting twice in defeats to Frosinone and Lazio, but Aquilani's men were undermined by defensive shortcomings in both games, losing 4-2 to the promoted side and suffering a 6-2 beatdown against the league-leading capital club.

Those results leave the Neroverdi three points clear of the relegation zone ahead of their 10th-round contest with the Viola, who sit two places below them in the Serie A table.

Paolo Vanoli has endured a strange few months, having been replaced by Fabio Grosso last month, around 90 days after the 2006 World Cup winner was appointed in his place for the season.

While Vanoli helped steer the Viola to safety in the 2025-26 campaign, results since his return have been mixed.

However, the pause has adversely affected the Tuscan outfit, who have lost three of their subsequent four matches, only ending their losing sequence by holding Atalanta BC to a draw on Thursday night.

Fiorentina will assess Luca Ranieri's leg injury before the penultimate fixture of the round, while Arthur Atta (strain), Fabiano Parisi (knee), Marin Pongracic (muscle) and Riccardo Sottil (back) are sidelined.

Franco Mastantuono, Alex Jimenez and Mateo Pellegrino have accounted for seven of the Viola's 11 goals this term, leaving much resting on Mastantuono and Pellegrino to deliver in the attacking third.

#2088. Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

Celtic could be forced into a fixture reshuffle after Rangers booked their place in the Premier Sports Cup Final with victory over Aberdeen.

There is already a precedent for such a move. Last season, Rangers had to switch an Ibrox clash with Hibernian after Celtic's Hampden showdown with St Mirren was scheduled for the same day. The match was pushed back to the Monday evening, with Emmanuel Fernandez scoring the winner for the Gers.

A similar scenario is now looming for Martin O'Neill's side, who are due to host Hibs at Parkhead on Sunday, December 13, the same day as this season's Hampden showpiece.

While Hibs could still reach the final themselves if they beat Edinburgh rivals Hearts in the second semi-final, their Premiership trip to Glasgow looks almost certain to be moved should they fall short.

The SPFL and Police Scotland are traditionally reluctant to have Celtic and Rangers playing separate matches in Glasgow on the same afternoon, making a change the most likely outcome.

Celtic are unable to simply bring the fixture forward by 24 hours. The champions are in Europa League action away to Omonia Nicosia on the Thursday night before the scheduled league encounter.

That leaves Monday evening as one potential solution, mirroring the arrangement made for Rangers and Hibs last season.

However, officials could also decide to move the match to an entirely different date depending on fixture congestion and broadcast requirements.

For now, Celtic's schedule remains unchanged, but Rangers' victory over Aberdeen has left a major question mark hanging over Hibs' planned visit to Parkhead.

#2087. Brighton sent Champions League warning by Gus Poyet after Man City win (exclusive)

By Ben Knapton | 31 Oct 2026 18:23

Brighton & Hove Albion are firm contenders for Champions League football but cannot afford to slip up in games they would be expected to win, Gus Poyet has exclusively told Sports Mole.

The Seagulls' latest notable scalp arrived on Saturday, as Fabian Hurzeler's men stunned leaders Manchester City 1-0 at the Etihad thanks to an early Yasin Ayari goal.

Brighton's triumph moved them onto 19 points from their opening nine games of the season, taking them to within just two points of Arsenal and Man City at the top of the Premier League table.

Fabian Hurzeler also masterminded a notable 3-0 win over Arsenal before the September/October international break, and his side's 24 goals is more than any other team in the English top flight.

Brighton's only two defeats in the Premier League this season have come away to Chelsea and Liverpool, although they did drop two points in a 1-1 draw with Leeds United at the Amex Stadium on September 5.

Therefore, Poyet - who managed Brighton between 2009 and 2013 - has warned the Seagulls that they could lose their Champions League contenders tab if they start dropping points against bottom-half teams.

"Games against the top sides are key of course, but it doesn’t determine Champions League contenders or not," Poyet said in an exclusive interview with Sports Mole.

"For me I would say Brighton are a contender. I see them pushing for a top-six position and being in Europe, so this is an improvement from last season.

"It’s great to perform well against the big sides, but if you drop points to the teams at the bottom, then you can’t be looking to be a contender. Up until now, Brighton are in the hunt for sure."

As well as getting the better of Arsenal and Man City, Brighton have also bested Aston Villa, Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Coventry City, keeping clean sheets against each of the latter four.

Palace, Coventry and Sunderland all find themselves in the lower echelons of the Premier League table, so Brighton cannot be accused of slipping up against teams in and around the relegation places so far.

An extremely kind run of fixtures now awaits the Seagulls, who meet Brentford, Hull City, Newcastle United, Bournemouth, Nottingham Forest, Everton and Ipswich Town in their next seven top-flight games.

If the Seagulls emerge from that run with at least five wins under their belt, their Champions League credentials will only be enhanced, but question marks will creep in with just a couple of dissatisfactory results.

Gus Poyet was speaking to Sports Mole on behalf of William Hill sports betting.

#2086. Ex-refs chief drops double penalty verdict as Man City vs Brighton footage re-analysed

Manchester City had two penalty appeals turned down against Brighton, but only one of them was worthy of a spot-kick.

That is according to former PGMOL chief and ex-FIFA referee, Keith Hackett, who exclusively told Football Insider that Man City deserved the chance to equalise from 12 yards.

Yasin Ayari's first-half goal made the difference at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday, 31 October, with Enzo Maresca's side unable to hit back.

That doesn't mean that the Citizens were without their chances, though. But the Seagulls' defence was just too strong for the home side.

Fabian Hurzeler's side also had some fortune go their way, with both Lewis Dunk and Luka Vuskovic escaping penalties during the 90 minutes.

The first incident occurred just before half-time, with Elliot Anderson's attempted pass deflecting off Vuskovic's outstretched arm inside the area.

There were then calls against Dunk, who clearly blocked Iliman Ndiaye's cross, but each of his arms were in a natural position and not outstretched.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Hackett reviewed the footage and agreed that Vuskovic should have been punished, but not Dunk.

"The reason this is not a penalty kick, in my opinion, is it looks as though it's hit the knee and come to the arm possibly," he said.

"In either case, let us assume that it's come off the naturally positioned arm. There's little he can do. And therefore, that's not a penalty kick for me.

"I'm nailed on. I think the other one, I actually think he goes for it. I think his arm's already way out, stretched out horizontally; it cannot be any wider.

"I'm looking, was it deflected? Was there sufficient distance for him to withdraw his arm? There was no indication that he was going to withdraw his arm or make a movement.

"There's sufficient distance coming in to actually withdraw or make a movement to withdraw it, but he's not. He's statuesque."

After an incredible start to the 2026-27 campaign, Man City have stalled in their bid for the Premier League title, losing two on the bounce now.

Having gone on a seven-game winning streak in the league, the Citizens have now lost to Aston Villa and Brighton, rather disappointingly.

And according to Opta, at this current rate, Man City will lose out on the Premier League title to Arsenal again, this time by two points.

In fact, their chances of lifting the trophy in May have dropped to just 18.86 per cent, while the Gunners have a 68.23 per cent chance of a title repeat.

#2085. Ex-Sunderland employee reveals how close Regis Le Bris is to the sack

Regis Le Bris may have just two games to save his job at Sunderland as pressure mounts ahead of the upcoming international break.

The Black Cats will face Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League next time out, before their Premier League clash against Chelsea, with both games at the Stadium of Light.

Two wins would undoubtably ease the pressure on the manager's position, but there is a growing feeling he could be let go if they fail to pick up points from either game.

Former Sunderland chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Le Bris' position is under threat as a result of what has been a nightmare start to the Premier League season.

Sunderland sit bottom of the table after nine games, and a 3-1 defeat against newly-promoted Coventry City at the weekend has raised signigicant concerns.

While there are mitigating circumstances, including major injuries which have limited Le Bris' side, there is a growing feeling that results must improve immediately.

Brown warned Football Insider on 12 October that Sunderland could be in "big trouble" after both Brian Brobbey and Dan Ballard suffered injuries on international duty.

The absence of his two star players has caused problems for Le Bris, and there is a feeling results could improve after their returns, but the boss may not have that long.

Brobbey returned to the starting XI against Coventry but had little impact, while Ballard is expected to be out until after the break, when Le Bris may already be gone.

"Sunderland have been keen to give Le Bris time to turn things around," Brown told Football Insider.

"He has a lot of credit in the bank from last season, but any manager who had his team bottom of the league after nine games is going to face serious threats over his job.

"The big problem he has is that he's been missing Brobbey and Ballard for a few games. If he can get them back fit and firing, then that will help him turn things around.

"Brobbey obviously came back in the last game, but having both players back would be a huge boost to Sunderland as a whole.

"The problem is, I'm not sure they'll be prepared to give him that long if things don't turn around before this next break, because I expect that's when decisions will be made.

"If they don't start winning games or at the very least picking up points they are going to be forced into a decision, rightly or wrongly.

"It's very difficult for Le Bris, or any manager, juggling European football and the Premier League with a squad which maybe isn't at the level you'd want to cope with that.

"But when you're not winning games in the Premier League, and you're sitting down the bottom of the table, it's always going to put pressure on."

Despite the growing pressure on Le Bris' position, there are a number of factors which could play in his favour as the board weigh up a decision over his future.

Brown told Football Insider on 20 October that Le Bris has the full support of his players at Sunderland who are still playing for him and hopeful of turning things around.

#2084. Dowman weaves his magic and new signing shines as Arsenal hit ground running

Teenage sensation Max Dowman was the star of Arsenal’s first pre-season match, as he scored one goal and assisted another in a 4-1 victory over Girona.

Dowman, 16, was joined on the scoresheet by new signing Christos Tzolis, who struck with a low effort in his first game since his £34m move from Belgian side Club Brugge.

Established attackers Kai Havertz and Gabriel Jesus also scored for the Premier League champions, who were largely comfortable against opposition from the Spanish second tier.

Here are four things Telegraph Sport learnt from the match:

It was this time last year that Dowman first announced his remarkable talent to the wider world. Then only 15, he sparkled in pre-season and made it clear to Mikel Arteta that he was ready to impact matches at the highest level.

A year on, Dowman is now an established first-team player. He is the youngest ever Premier League winner and the competition’s youngest ever scorer, and he looks set to make even more of a mark this season.

In this friendly against Girona, Dowman created Arsenal’s opening goal with a gorgeous defence-splitting pass for Havertz. He did so after receiving the ball under pressure and spinning into space. Dowman then scored Arsenal’s third with a powerful low drive from the edge of the box.

Dowman is in competition with Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke for a place on the right wing, which means this summer represents a huge opportunity for the teenager. After playing for England at the World Cup, Saka and Madueke will both miss most of pre-season.

Dowman, therefore, has a serious chance of going into the new campaign as the starting right-winger. The Community Shield on August 16 must be a target in his mind.

“We know what he’s capable of doing,” Arteta said. “We want to be more consistent in terms of the performances and the actions that he can deliver, but I think today he had a really good game.”

Arsenal are close to completing a deal for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimarães but, for now, their only outfield signing of the summer has been Tzolis. This was the Greek winger’s first match in front of supporters and he immediately demonstrated why Arsenal were willing to pay £34m to buy him from Club Brugge.

With Tzolis, it is all about the final product. Goals and assists. He struck 22 times for Club Brugge last season, and registered 29 assists.

How did he produce such impressive numbers? The answer could be seen in his first-half goal against Girona. Receiving the ball on the left wing, Tzolis quickly accelerated towards the penalty area and unleashed a low shot. It was perhaps a more direct approach than Arsenal would usually have seen from Leandro Trossard, the player Tzolis has replaced, and it caught Girona off-guard as the ball deflected into the net.

“I’m very pleased with him,” Arteta said. “First of all, the way he has adapted to the club, to the team. The connection he’s already generating with the boys. I think you’re going to love the player.

“A player who’s very direct. He’s got the goal between the eyes. He has a lot of similarities with Leo [Trossard] in a lot of the things that he can do and the spaces he can occupy. And then the work rate that he has... He’s a boy that comes with so much hunger. He wants to prove himself, it’s a dream for him. And we are here to help him.”

Havertz was one of the few Arsenal players who benefited from playing at the World Cup. His injury issues mean that, unlike most of his team-mates, he did not end the 2025-26 season in a state of exhaustion.

After returning to the pitch in the spring, Havertz enjoyed an impressive end to the campaign for Arsenal. He then performed well at the World Cup, scoring three goals for Germany.

He remains one of Arteta’s favourite players, not least because of his versatility. He started in attack in the crucial end-of-season games in May, but played in midfield against Girona. His low finish, from Dowman’s pass, represented his eighth goal in his last 12 matches for club and country.

Girona’s goal, scored by Arnau Martínez, was perhaps the only alarming moment of this comfortable pre-season victory. Martínez was unmarked from a left-wing corner when he powered a header into Arsenal’s net.

For a group of players who pride themselves on their set-piece prowess, this was a disappointing moment. It also perhaps showed Arsenal’s reliance on their two first-choice centre-backs, William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães, when they are defending crosses into their box.

Gabriel arrived at Arsenal’s pre-season training camp a few days ago, so he should be in good shape by the start of the new campaign. Saliba, though, will be missing for months with a back problem.

Without Saliba’s height and power, will Arsenal be as effective from set-pieces in the opening chunk of the campaign? Coventry City, Arsenal’s opponents on the first night of the season, will undoubtedly look to test the champions in these situations.

The reigning Premier League champions are handed the Costa Brava Trophy, which is half-heartedly lifted into the air by White. There will be far bigger trophies on offer to Arsenal in the upcoming campaign.

Arsenal have cruised to a routine 4-1 win over Girona, with Havertz, Tzolis, Dowman and Gabriel Jesus all finding the net. Arteta will be delighted with his side’s professionalism and ruthlessness.

Meslier takes too long on his goal kick, gifting a corner to Girona. However, the delivery from the hosts is so poor as it flies harmlessly out of play. That sums up Girona’s difficult evening.

There is another round of substitutions for both sides.

Arsenal’s makeshift line-up, which is full of Hale End graduates, is holding firm, with Girona evidently struggling for attacking inspiration. If Arsenal can see out this victory without any injuries, then it would have panned out exactly how Arteta would have wanted.

We are back under way for the second half.

That was a straightforward half for Arsenal. Arteta will be pleased with Havertz’s showing in his 33 minutes on the pitch. After missing so much of last season through injury, it has been a good summer for Havertz so far. He scored three goals in Arsenal’s final six games of 2025/26, and then netted four times for Germany in June.

The 2009-born playmaker was Arsenal’s standout player in that first half. Dowman’s confidence and class on the ball has been brilliant, with his expertly-crafted assist for Havertz’s opener an obvious highlight.

Tzolis registered 22 goals and 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He is an end-product machine, and that goal was a little indication of how he racks up such eye-watering numbers. After receiving possession on the left wing, he was so quick to shift the ball onto his right foot and fire the shot at goal. He describes himself as a “direct” player and that was evidence of it.

The new winger is one-on-one with Martinez and darts inside, before firing a low effort into the bottom corner. It took a slight deflection, leaving Gazzaniga with no chance. Tzolis has looked lively and slotted into Arsenal’s attack seamlessly so far.

After suffering an injury at the end of last season and missing the World Cup, White returns to action here this evening and wears the armband. He will look to support Dowman, who appears to be starting on the right wing.

It’s been a confident start from Arsenal, who are stroking the ball around in a very assured manner. Havertz looks to pull the strings by firing a low cross towards Gyokeres, but the delivery is scrambled clear by the Girona backline.

White leads Arsenal out onto the pitch to face Girona, who boast the likes of Van de Beek, Gil and Moreno in their starting XI.

Talking earlier this week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta sent out a determined message to other clubs by outlining their ambitious transfer plans.

“A lot is happening,” Arteta said. “We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director and myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

“That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way.”

Arteta also believes that last season’s Premier League title has served as added motivation for his squad to improve and hit new heights.

“This has to be the start and this has to be the standard,” he said. “Excellence has to be our standard and this has to drive to attack the future. The way we behave daily with more and more determination and ambition, because we’ve shown that we’ve got it. Now we have to show that we belong to this level and we want to increase and take this football club to a different dimension.”

It had been a relatively quiet transfer window for Arsenal, who have recruited just goalkeeper Illan Meslier and winger Christos Tzolis.

However, Arsenal are now moving very bullishly, closing on Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães, while also targeting Real Madrid’s Vinícius Júnior.

Sam Dean has the full breakdown of a potential deal for the Real Madrid star and how Arsenal are prepared to continue flexing their muscles in the transfer market in what would be one of the biggest moves in Premier League history.

It was January 2025, with Arsenal earning a hard-fought 2-1 comeback victory in the Champions League courtesy of first-half goals from Jorginho and Ethan Nwaneri.

Since this European encounter, Girona have been on a seriously downward trajectory, enduring lowly 16th and 19th finishes in La Liga, with the latter ensuring relegation to the Segunda Division, where they’ll play in the upcoming campaign.

August 5: Arsenal vs Real Betis (Dublin, Ireland)

August 9: Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (London, England)

August 12: Arsenal vs Como (London, England)

August 16: Arsenal vs Manchester City (Cardiff, Wales)

Mikel Arteta’s side will then begin their defence of the Premier League title on August 21 when they host newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21.

Arsenal are closing in on one of the statement signings of the summer, with Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimarães getting closer to joining the Premier League holders.

This deal means that Christian Norgaard is expected to leave and seal a move to Everton for around £7m.

We have our patterns, we know how to defend the box and we know what we have to do," Rose told BBC Sport.

"We were just working on details. We stick to our plan, stick together. We are a little more alert in a couple of situations.

Evanilson, meanwhile, has scored in four of his previous five competitive appearances for the Cherries, including in each of the club's last four Premier League matches.

#2075. Celtic fall to Falkirk defeat as Scott Bain shines for Bairns

Celtic paid the price for a sloppy start and a superb display from former goalkeeper Scott Bain as they fell to a 2-0 defeat at Falkirk.

Ethan Ross netted in the third minute after a mistake by Cameron Carter-Vickers and Scott Tanser put Falkirk two ahead in the 38th minute.

Bain made 10 saves as Martin O’Neill’s side endured an afternoon of frustration and suffered a sixth defeat in 10 matches.

The champions remain four points clear at the top of the William Hill Premiership but have now played a game more than second-placed Rangers.

Falkirk moved up to fourth in the table after their fourth consecutive victory and their first over Celtic since 2007.

Read more: Celtic face key fixture shunting thanks to Rangers as precedent set

Carter-Vickers returned to the starting line-up after injury, while Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain was handed his first start in two months. Winger Haissem Hassan was recalled.

Kasper Hogh might have fancied himself to end his barren run on Falkirk’s synthetic pitch given most of his career goals have come on artificial surfaces, but the former Bodo/Glimt striker was dropped as Camilo Duran led the line.

The Danish striker came on for the final 25 minutes but was barely involved as he went 14 games without a goal.

Falkirk got an early lift after the Celtic central defence failed to deal with a long ball.

The hosts worked the ball out to Ryan Strain, whose cross was knocked into the path of Ross by Carter-Vickers. The wide player lapped up the chance.

The goal came at a cost as Strain injured himself while crossing. Jack McMillan was a natural replacement at right-back.

Both sides made opportunities in the first half.

On-loan Derby winger Owen Eames was a hive of creativity on Falkirk’s left wing and helped set up two half chances for Jacob Murrell, who could not make the most of them.

The 19-year-old wide player set up the second goal as left-back Tanser ran on to his infield pass before slotting past Sam Johnstone.

Duran hit a post after getting in behind and Celtic were kept out by a string of excellent first-half stops from Bain, who denied the Colombian three times and also foiled Hassan with a diving save.

Falkirk were almost out of sight early in the second half when Murrell bundled the ball over the line after Celtic failed to deal with a long throw, but the ball had hit the American’s hand when it bounced off a post before going in off the striker’s waist and the goal was disallowed by VAR.

O’Neill had brought on James Forrest for Callum Osmand at half-time and the winger forced Bain’s first save of the half before Callum McGregor, Kieran Tierney and Hassan missed the target from inside the box.

O’Neill turned to Hogh and Benjamin Nygren as Duran and Oxlade-Chamberlain made way.

But Bain quickly pulled off a brilliant double save from Forrest and Nygren to spark chants of ‘Scotland’s number one’.

The former Celtic goalkeeper soon denied Forrest again before Nygren was thwarted by a diving block from Finn Yeats.

It grew increasingly clear that Celtic were never going to score as Liam Scales headed over and Bain saved long-range efforts from Nygren and Mika Baur.

They have failed to build on that 2-1 success over Daniele De Rossi's Genoa, suffering consecutive 3-0 defeats to Inter Milan and Torino before losing 2-1 to Lazio in gameweek eight.

While the Emilia-Romagna outfit came close to beating Udinese, they were thwarted by Maduka Okoye, who saved Adrian Bernabe's 69th-minute penalty as the match ended goalless at the Tardini.

That point was insufficient to lift Gilardino's men out of the bottom three, but a draw could suffice this time, provided Sassuolo beat Fiorentina in Monday's earlier fixture.

Even that appears a tall order at a ground that has brought considerable pain over the past decade: Parma have lost five of their last six trips to Bergamo, conceding 16 goals without reply across those defeats, although they claimed a rare 3-2 victory in May 2025.

Franck Kessie and Thomas Kristensen are touch-and-go for Atalanta, while Giacomo Raspadori, Gianluca Scamacca, Raoul Bellanova (thigh), Isak Hien, Sead Kolasinac, Odilon Kossounou and Gianluca Gaetano are all sidelined.

Those injuries leave La Dea without several match-winners, although leading scorer Nikola Krstovic will hope to add to his six league goals, which place him behind Gustavo Varela on nine and Donyell Malen and Antonio Raimondo on eight apiece.

Lautaro Valenti and Nesta Elphege both face late fitness tests to determine their availability for Parma on Monday.

The league's lowest scorers have netted just five times in nine matches, with David Romero and Simone Lontani contributing two goals apiece to underline their shortage of match-winning options.

Carnesecchi; Zappacosta, Scalvini, Obric, Bernasconi; Pasalic, Ederson; Elmas, De Ketelaere, Rowe; Krstovic

Atalanta's defensive frailties have prolonged their winless run, but facing a Parma side with just five goals from nine league matches offers an opportunity to restore some solidity.

With 10 of their 11 points earned at home and Krstovic providing a reliable scoring threat, La Dea have our backing to return to winning ways.

#2073. Nottingham Forest face meltdown with Evangelos Marinakis and Oliver Glasner at loggerheads - expert

Evangelos Marinakis and the Nottingham Forest leadership will be very unhappy at Oliver Glasner's public criticism.

The boss has won just one of his 10 games in the dugout at the City Ground since taking over from Vitor Pereira in the summer, raising doubts over his position.

However, following a 2-0 defeat against Brentford last time out, he took aim at the players and the club and insisted a change in manager would not resolve their issues.

Former Man United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider that Glasner's assessment of his situation is correct but is unlikely to go down well in the corridors of power.

Much will depend on the relationship the manager shares with owner Evangelos Marinakis, and whether these concerns have also been aired behind the scenes.

Glasner is no stranger to airing his frustrations in public, having done similar at Crystal Palace, but there is also a feeling that results must improve if he wants backing.

Former Tottenham scout Bryan King warned Football Insider on 28 October that Glasner must avoid Marinakis' wrath if he wants to remain in charge at Nottingham Forest.

His latest outburst has hardly seen him stay under the radar, however, as is likely to have sparked concerns behind the scenes alongside their poor on-pitch performances.

However, Glasner may receive backing for his claims as he bids to turn around what has been a difficult couple of years at Forest with the support of the board.

"Oliver Glasner is right, the issues at Nottingham Forest go far beyond the manager's control," Brown told Football Insider.

"That's the reason they've been through five managers in the last year and nobody has been able to turn things around, and Glasner is facing the same issues they all did.

"He's right to put the blame on the players, because they haven't changed, and ultimately they're the ones who have played a part in all of those managers failing.

"If Glasner fails, it will be the same players again who haven't stepped up, and the decision-makers behind the scenes failing to support him.

"But, the problem is, I can't imagine his decision to come out with these criticisms publicly is going to go down well with the owner or the board at Nottingham Forest.

"They don't often take kindly to public criticism, no owners do, so I think it will depend on what the relationship is like between Glasner and Marinakis.

"Has he gone to him already with these issues? Can he tell him what the problems are now? Or has he done it publicly to get his message across in that way?

"We'll see how they react, because Glasner was quite clear on how he feels, and it's certainly going to be one to watch in the next few days."

Should Glasner's recent outburst end in the result he is hoping for, then the club have work to do in the background to back the boss ahead of the January transfer window.

There are glaring weaknesses on the pitch at the City Ground which must be addressed, while the manager continues to oversee changes regarding his players and the dressing room.

Brown told Football Insider on 29 October that Nottingham Forest have alraedy begun working to identify attacking additions, with "top-class" strikers on their radar.

Glasner has identified the position as a major weakness in his squad and is pushing the recruitment team to strengthen up front after a slow start to the season.

The Tricky Trees have scored the joint-fewest goals in the Premier League, with just six after nine games, and have still yet to find the net at the City Ground.

#2071. Deportivo La Coruna vs Osasuna - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 31 Oct 2026 20:01, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 02:14

Deportivo La Coruna will look to end a six-game winless league run when they take on Osasuna at Riazor on Monday evening.

The hosts head into the contest in 12th spot in La Liga after taking 11 points from 10 matches, while Osasuna are just a couple of places behind on goal difference.

Deportivo made a positive start to their first top-flight campaign since 2017-18, which saw them take eight points from their opening four matches.

However, they have experienced something of a reality check in recent times, having gone six consecutive league games without a win, including defeats in three of their last four La Liga outings.

The most recent of those losses came via a 1-0 scoreline in last Saturday's away clash against Atletico Madrid, extending their winless run in head-to-head meetings to 14 matches.

Antonio Hidalgo's side at least managed to avoid a major upset in their midweek Copa del Rey clash against sixth-tier Auriense, with Jonathan Asp scoring a brace before Luismi Cruz found the net in a 3-0 victory.

After advancing to the second round, Depor will return to the familiar surroundings of Riazor, where they have lost just once in five matches this season, although three of those encounters have finished all square, including their last two home outings against Real Betis and Levante.

While they have not faced Osasuna in the top flight since the 2016-17 campaign, they may still be able to take confidence from the fact they have avoided defeat in each of their last five La Liga home meetings, keeping clean sheets in all of those contests (W2, D3).

Jagoba Arrasate, meanwhile, is still in the early stages of his second spell as Osasuna boss after being appointed as Luis Miguel Ramis's successor in the middle of October.

Arrasate marked his return with a 2-0 win over Racing de Santander at El Sadar, but his side were unable to back up that result in Monday's away clash against Sevilla.

Goals from Isaac Romero and Felix Correia condemned Osasuna to a 2-0 loss, representing a fourth consecutive away league loss since beating Celta Vigo 2-1 in the first road trip of the season at the end of August.

While they have struggled on their travels in the league, Osasuna made light work of their midweek away clash against sixth-tier Atletico Calatayud in the Copa del Rey, with Raul Garcia netting a hat-trick in a comfortable 6-0 success for the two-time finalists.

If they are to enjoy away success in the league, Osasuna need to become a much tougher team to break down after shipping 17 goals across their opening five road trips in La Liga.

A strong defensive display would boost their chances of claiming their first top-flight win over Deportivo at Riazor since recording a 2-1 victory in December 2007.

Deportivo La Coruna form (all competitions):

Deportivo are expected to be without defender Bright Ede, midfielder Marc Casado and forward Zakaria Eddachouri.

Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has returned to training after undergoing meniscus surgery in September, but Monday’s fixture is likely to come too soon for Depor’s top scorer.

Bil Nsongo will continue to lead the line in Aubameyang’s expected absence, with the striker looking to score in a second straight home game after netting in the 1-1 draw against Levante.

As for the visitors, Jorge Herrando and Romain Del Castillo remain sidelined with adductor injuries, while Aimar Oroz is out with a hamstring problem.

Arrasate could make at least one change to the team that started Osasuna's most recent league outing against Atletico, with Iker Munoz pushing to get the nod over Lucas Torro in the middle of the mark.

Ante Budimir will continue to lead the line for the visitors, with the Croatian looking to add to the seven goals he has scored in La Liga this season.

Deportivo La Coruna possible starting lineup:

Roman; Altimira, Loureiro, Gimenez, Quagliata; Villares, Amatucci; Luismi, Soriano, Yeremay; Nsongo

Fernandez; Rosier, Catena, Boyomo, Bretones; Munoz, Moncayola; Ru. Garcia, Gomez, Dubasin; Budimir

Given Osasuna's struggles on the road, we think they will find it difficult to claim the spoils from this contest, but we think they will do enough to take at least a point off a Deportivo side that has drawn three of their five home games this season.

Leeds United came from 2-0 down at half-time to beat Liverpool 4-2 at Soldier Field in Chicago as Andoni Iraola’s side were undone by sloppy defending in the second period.

Liverpool’s dominant first-half display was underlined by goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz. However, Daniel Farke’s men replied with four strikes in 25 second-half minutes through Sean Longstaff, Brenden Aaronson and two alarmingly similar goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

Jeremie Frimpong, serviced by a wonderfully flighted cross-field ball by Trey Nyoni, then set up Wirtz to make it 2-0 five minutes before the break, but on the hour Leeds began their recovery when Aaronson scored following a mistake by Kerkez – who gave up possession to Ethan Ampadu in his own half.

Liverpool return to Anfield for friendlies against Monaco and Como before they begin their Premier League season away at Newcastle United later this month.

Leeds have matches against RB Leipzig, Manchester United and Augsburg before their league campaign gets under way at Nottingham Forest.
