Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

#2069. Bruno Fernandes, Lisandro Martinez: Are Manchester United senior players letting Michael Carrick down?

By Nsidibe Akpan | 31 Oct 2026 22:47

Manchester United's capitulation at Stamford Bridge on Saturday was the clearest picture yet of a club eating itself from within.

A 2-0 defeat to Chelsea, sealed after Lisandro Martinez was sent off for a rash challenge on Wesley Fofana, leaves Michael Carrick's side 17th in the table and winless in nine matches across all competitions.

It also lands three weeks into a period in which two of United's senior players have publicly questioned the manager and the club's hierarchy from inside the dressing room.

The question now being asked around Old Trafford is not whether United have a results problem - that much is obvious - but whether the players themselves have become part of it.

The unrest did not begin at Stamford Bridge. It started on 13 October, when United lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League and Martinez used his post-match interview to criticise the club's recruitment, singling out director of football Jason Wilcox and saying he expected more investment in the squad.

He stopped short of an apology at first, but after meeting Carrick and senior club officials two days later he apologised publicly; the club is understood to have fined him.

A week later, it was Bruno Fernandes' turn. After a chastening 4-1 Champions League defeat to Como on 21 October, the captain told TNT Sports that United had not pressed Como's defenders with enough intensity, adding that whether that amounted to criticism of Carrick's tactics was "on the manager and staff to see, not me."

Carrick responded by dropping Fernandes for the following Premier League match, a 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October that extended United's winless run to eight games and left them 16th in the table on seven points from eight games, one point above the relegation zone - their lowest points total at this stage of a season since 1986-87.

Carrick and Fernandes held direct talks before the Chelsea trip in an attempt to draw a line under the Como fallout, and the captain was restored to the starting lineup.

For an hour, the reconciliation looked to be working: United were the better side for long periods of the first half, with Fernandes, Amad and Matheus Cunha all missing presentable chances to take the lead.

The game turned early in the second half. Morgan Rogers split United's defence and lifted a finish over Senne Lammens to make it 1-0, and minutes later Martinez caught Fofana with his arm from a Chelsea corner, earning a straight red card and conceding a penalty that Cole Palmer converted.

Reduced to ten men, United's resistance collapsed, and Chelsea spent the rest of the match squandering chances to extend the lead further.

To United's critics, the word "sabotage" is not too strong.

Two senior players airing grievances about the manager and the hierarchy inside a three-week span, in a season already defined by results, is read by some as a dressing room no longer pulling in one direction.

Jamie Carragher said on CBS Sports that Martinez had been "bang out of order" for calling out the hierarchy, and took a similar view of Fernandes after Como.

Wayne Rooney went further, labelling the current squad "selfish" and accusing them of behaving like children rather than owning their performances.

Rooney, while defending Carrick personally, argued Fernandes' public criticism was a way of deflecting from his own drop in form this season, and said the pattern of players speaking out risked fracturing the dressing room at the worst possible moment.

On this reading, Martinez's red card - an undisciplined, arm-raised challenge with United already on top - fits a wider theme of senior players failing to show the control and restraint a manager under pressure needs from them.

There is a difference, though, between frustration and sabotage.

Martinez's grievance was about recruitment, not team selection: he wanted greater investment in a squad he felt had been left short, a view plenty of independent observers of United's thin depth would recognise, and he named no team-mate in making it.

Fernandes' critique of United's pressing against Como was echoed, not dismissed, by independent tactical analysis of the match, which found Fernandes himself was often the only United player applying sustained pressure on Como's defenders.

Neither player has questioned Carrick's suitability for the job directly, and both episodes were followed by conciliatory gestures rather than escalation: Martinez's apology and fine, Fernandes' private talks with Carrick and restoration to the starting eleven for Chelsea, and Carrick's own description of the decision to drop his captain as a football one rather than a disciplinary one.

The club's hierarchy reviewed Carrick's position after the Como and Bournemouth defeats and chose to back him rather than make a change - hardly the behaviour of a board being pushed toward the manager's exit by player unrest.

And for all the talk of a fractured dressing room, United were comfortably the better side for an hour at Stamford Bridge; what undid them in the end was a moment of individual indiscipline from Martinez, not a collective capitulation.

What is harder to dispute is that United's results, not any single comment, are what is driving the crisis.

Nine games without a win, a defensive crisis compounded by suspensions and injuries, and now a 17th-place standing leave little room for Carrick regardless of how united his dressing room is.

Sabotage implies intent; what Stamford Bridge showed was closer to a team low on confidence, short on senior defensive options, and unable to see out a match it had controlled for an hour.

The more pressing question for United is whether public unrest and poor results start to reinforce each other - whether another bad week invites another outspoken interview, and another outspoken interview makes the next bad week more likely.

The hierarchy has given Carrick more time. His players, for now, say they support him too. Saturday suggested that support alone will not be enough to turn results around.

#2064. Liverpool star Alexis Mac Allister should be 'banned' as latest footage analysed - expert

Alexis Mac Allister should have been sent off and serve a suspension for his part in the scuffle that came in the final stages of Liverpool's 1-0 loss to Arsenal on Sunday.

That is according to experienced former Everton, Tottenham and Aston Villa scout, Bryan King, speaking exclusively to Football Insider.

The Gunners clinched the three points courtesy of Kai Havertz's early goal, which would decide a game packed with controversy.

Liverpool felt that they should have had a penalty for a shirt grab on Alexander Isak in the first half, and anger spread around Anfield as Arsenal attempted to slow down the game.

Mac Allister's snap came after he had been adjudged to have fouled Martin Odegaard, relieving the pressure on Mikel Arteta's team.

The ensuing scuffle saw the Liverpool midfielder, 27, throw himself to the ground and claim to have been headbutted by Noni Madueke, though replays revealed minimal contact.

The most aggressive action in the sequence at the end of Sunday's game likely came from Mac Allister, who ultimately went down holding his face.

The midfielder fouled Odegaard and had words for the Arsenal captain, ending his point by slapping the back of his head.

Jurrien Timber and Madueke took exception and after a slight touch between their heads, Mac Allister threw himself to the ground.

The Argentine would get a yellow card for his troubles while the Arsenal winger, who had already been on a yellow, was ignored by referee Andy Madley.

"I feel certain players and the way teams are playing, there's a certain dishonesty about it," King told Football Insider.

"Personally, I'm getting fed up of seeing players get knocked down and get pushed over, or get touched and fall over, through absolutely nothing.

"With one intent - either to get a penalty, a free kick or an opponent sent off. Mac Allister should have had a red card yesterday and be serving a ban, for his actions. It was the way he went for Odegaard. It was the way he reacted afterwards.

"It takes the pace of the game out. At that moment in time, Liverpool were in the ascendancy and then all of a sudden, you've got five minutes of messing around.

"If he was injured and it was a head injury, why wasn't the trainer on the pitch? Because that's one of the stipulations - if there's a head injury, the trainer's got to come on the pitch.

"There was no sign of the trainer, was there? I think everybody realised how embarrassing it must have been."

Mac Allister has faced huge criticism in the wake of Sunday's game, including from Liverpool legend Jamie Carragher.

"I’m delighted he [Madueke] didn’t get sent off there," the former Reds centre-back said.

"We have really got to be calling people out and just say ‘This is embarrassing’. I think Gary [Neville] said it on commentary. It’s got to stop. It’s ridiculous.

"I can’t stand it. If someone pulls their head back and butts, of course [that’s a] red card. But if people are head to head and one touches the other one and they go down, and the player gets sent off, people in the game and supporters [should] call your own people out for it.

"I’m a Liverpool fan and that’s a joke. People are trying to gain an advantage from this because they know they can."

The Saudi Pro League side are sitting in ninth spot in the league phase (West), while Pakhtakor are a point behind in 12th position.

Pakhtakor entered the AFC Champions League in the preliminary round after finishing in second spot in the Uzbekistan Super League last term.

The Uzbek side cruised to a 3-0 victory over Al-Hussein to reach the league phase, where they have mustered just two points from their opening three matches.

They started the league phase with back-to-back games against Saudi Pro League opposition, playing out 1-1 draws against Al-Ahli and Al Qadiash.

However, they were unable to take anything from last week's away clash against Iraqi outfit Al-Quwa Al-Jawiya, with Saad Abdulameer's effort proving the difference in a 1-0 defeat, making it four consecutive matches without a win for Kamoliddin Tajiev's side.

That result extended their winless run to four matches, which they ended with a much-needed 1-0 victory over Xorazm Urganch in Friday's league encounter, leaving them in second spot and two points adrift of leaders Neftchi Fargona, who have played a game more.

As they turn their focus to Monday's Champions League fixture, Pakhtakor can take some confidence from the fact they have lost just one of their last 13 competitive home games, although that solitary defeat took place against Neftchi Fargona in their most recent outing at the Pakhtakor Central Stadium.

Al-Nassr are competing in the AFC Champions League main draw after winning the Saudi Pro League title under Jorge Jesus's watch last season.

Jesus left at the end of the title-winning campaign, paving the way for ex-Tottenham Hotspur boss Ange Postecoglou to take over the reins.

The 61-year-old has overseen 11 wins, one draw and two defeats in his 14 matches in charge, with one of those losses coming via a 4-0 scoreline in their Champions League opener against Al-Ain.

Al-Nassr have responded to that defeat with a five-game winning run, including a 3-1 victory over reigning Uzbek champions Neftchi Fergana on matchday two of the league phase, leaving them a point adrift of the top eight.

Cristiano Ronaldo starred in Al-Nassr's most recent outing against Al-Kholood in the Saudi Pro League, netting a second-half hat-trick in a 5-3 win to move within 15 of his 1,000-goal target.

Having scored at least three goals in four of their last five games, Al-Nassr will be looking to continue their fine form when they make the trip to Uzbekistan, although their hopes of victory may be tempered by the fact they won just one of their previous four away competitive matches (D1, L2).

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#2058. Sunday's Ligue 1 prediction, including Paris FC vs Monaco and Marseille vs Toulouse

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 01 Nov 2026 00:00, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's Ligue 1 predictions focus on key clashes involving sides in the early European push, as Lyon host Angers, Paris FC welcome Monaco to the capital and Marseille take on Toulouse at the Stade Velodrome.

Strasbourg will hope to climb out of the Ligue 1 relegation playoff zone with a victory on Sunday at Stade de la Meinau against Auxerre.

The Alsatian club dropped to 16th after a 3-0 defeat at Rennes on matchday eight, while Auxerre sit three points above them in 12th after drawing Le Mans 1-1.

As improved as Auxerre have been lately, they have looked out of sorts defensively away from home all season which is why we believe Strasbourg will return to winning ways.

Lyon will hope to remain unbeaten at home in Ligue 1 this season as they return to Groupama Stadium on Sunday to face Angers.

A 2-0 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on Monday dropped Les Gones down to fifth, while Angers sit 14th, having drawn Lorient 0-0 last time out.

While Angers can keep matches close, doing so against a team with Lyon's depth we doubt they can fend them off for 90 minutes.

Paris FC will put their undefeated home record on the line Sunday as they host Monaco at Stade Jean-Bouin in a bid to reach the top five in Ligue 1.

Last Saturday, Paris dropped to sixth after Lens beat them 2-1, while Les Monegasques sit fourth after drawing Lille 1-1 last week.

Paris FC seem to have lost much of that early-season momentum and look much more vulnerable at the back, something we believe a resilient Monaco side can take advantage of.

Sunday’s Ligue 1 action concludes with Marseille welcoming Toulouse to Stade Velodrome on matchday nine.

A 4-3 win versus Le Havre put Les Olympians up to eighth in the table, while Toulouse sit 11th, drawing Troyes 0-0 the last time around.

These are two aggressive teams that leave a lot of gaps in behind and in the end we believe the attacking power of Marseille will carry them through.

#2057. How Hibernian made Hampden history against Hearts and booked final date with Rangers

Hibernian made a little piece of Hampden history this afternoon when they came from behind to beat Hearts in the second Premier Sports Cup semi-final.

The Easter Road club had lost all four of their previous meetings with their age-old Edinburgh adversaries at the Mount Florida venue before today.

When Claudio Braga put the Tynecastle men ahead in just the fourth minute it looked like they might be heading for another defeat.

But first-half goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath gave Hibs a deserved lead and they held on to book a place in the final against Rangers next month.

Marink Reedijk, who had failed to win any of his first four games as manager, savoured the victory as much as any supporter.

Here are five talking points from the last four meeting.

Stragglers were still taking their seats inside the packed stadium when Hearts broke the deadlock.

Braga got in between Jason Kerr and Marko Ivezic and on the end of a Calvin Miller cross in the Hibs six yard box and headed beyond Raphael Sallinger from a few yards out.

The Portuguese forward was mobbed by his team-mates on the touchline as the maroon half of the stadium celebrated wildly.

But there was not much more for them to shout about after they had edged ahead.

Hibs recovered superbly from the early setback. Felix Passlack, their captain, was unfortunate not to restore parity just a few minutes later after being sent through on goal by Joe Newell. Beau Reus just managed to keep his deflected attempt out.

Owen Elding also should have done better after being supplied by Adam Mayor. The striker shelled over when he only had the keeper to beat. But he atoned for his miss soon afterwards by teeing up the leveller.

He controlled a pass from Newell and then scooped a chip over the heads of the opposition defence to Boyle who turned a shot in off of Reus and the inside of the left post.

The Hearts players and fans appealed for offside but linesman Douglas Ross kept his flag down.

VAR officials Andrew Dallas and Nick Walsh had a long look back at the replay over at Clydesdale House and found that there colleague had made the correct call. Jordi Altena had played the winger on.

Jamie McGrath put his side in front with an opportunistic strike at a Boyle corner three minutes before half-time.

The ball broke to Newell, who had just skimmed the top of the crossbar from distance, and he burst forward and then unleashed a powerful shot which was blocked by Malachi Fagan-Walcott. McGrath was perfectly positioned to net the rebound.

Hibs fans had high hopes of seeing their struggling heroes produce some Total Football when Dutchman Reedijk replaced David Gray as manager at Easter Road last month.

There has, though, been little evidence of that in the former Ajax youth coach’s opening games.

His charges produced some nice passages of play after falling behind at Hampden and deserved to go in front. They dominated long spells of the encounter with their capital rivals. But they did so by winning their battles and bullying their opponents.

Josh Mulligan and Kerr were booked by referee David Dickinson for fouls on Stephen Kinglsey and Dhanda respectively. The players in green and white shirts were hungrier and far more physical.

Miller going off injured – he was replaced by Sabri Guendouz shortly after the half hour mark and was later seen hobbling about on crutches – did nothing to help Hearts’ cause. He had set up the opener and posed a threat whenever he got on the ball.

Still, they could have no complaints about the scoreline when they returned to their dressing room. Braga had headed a Josh McPake cross well wide after his side had fallen behind. But if he had found the target and levelled it would have flattered them.

Hearts, doubtless after a few choice words from their manager Vrancken, played with far greater purpose when the action resumed in the second half. Sallinger had to produce fine saves from both Braga and Guendouz to keep the Leith men in front.

McPake, who should be named in the Scotland squad for the Nations League games against North Macedonia and Switzerland on Tuesday, was a real handful throughout.

However, Hibs looked dangerous on the counter too. Reus had to deny Boyle and Ivezic and Kingsley slid in a denied Passlack on two occasions as well. It was, to use an old football cliché, real end-to-end stuff.

The meeting between Aberdeen and Rangers on Saturday evening had been a tense affair that was devoid of chances as well as a difficult watch for the neutral observer. This was the perfect antidote. Everyone in the 41,673-strong crowd was royally entertained.

This has been another wretched season for Hibs fans and they travelled along the M8 in hope rather than expectation.

The Leith men last won a William Hill Premiership game back in August and are in bottom spot in the top flight table.

But Passlack and his team-mates buried the memory of the Scottish Cup defeats that Hibs they had suffered against Hearts at Hampden in 2006, 2012 and 2022 and the League Cup loss they were on the receiving end of on the South Side of Glasgow in 1955.

There were tears in the eyes of their longsuffering followers during the rendition of Sunshine on Leith which they belted out following the final whistle.

If Hibernian perform as well in the final against Rangers next month then their fans may have more reason to party.

#2056. ‘Honestly…’ – Andoni Iraola gives candid reaction to drawing Bournemouth in Carabao Cup quarters

Andoni Iraola has admitted that he’d rather not have seen Liverpool drawn against Bournemouth in the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup.

Both teams came through their fourth-round ties on Wednesday night, with the Reds defeating Chelsea on penalties and the Cherries seeing off Aston Villa, and they were paired together in the draw for the last eight.

It means that the Basque will come up against his former club at least twice more this season, having already returned to the Vitality Stadium in September when the Merseysiders triumphed 1-0.

With the quarter-final draw being made shortly after the match at Anfield ended last night, Iraola was asked for his reaction at Liverpool being paired with Bournemouth.

The 44-year-old replied (via liverpoolfc.com): “Honestly, I was talking before the draw and I said, ‘The only team I don’t want is Bournemouth…’ For me, it’s special. They know me very well, they are playing very well lately, in a good moment, but it is what it is.

“We haven’t been very lucky with the draws – we have played Spurs and Chelsea already and now Bournemouth. That is going to be obviously special for me, but we have to earn the right to be in the semi-finals and I hope we can do it here at home again.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Although Iraola has been spared another trip to the Vitality Stadium as Liverpool were drawn at home, another clash against his former club is sure to see him dominating the narrative ahead of the Carabao Cup quarter-final, which’ll likely take place on Wednesday 16 December.

When the Reds won away to Bournemouth last month, the Cherries had yet to win a game under Marco Rose. The south coast side could be a much more fearsome proposition this time around if they continue their recent resurgence, with AC Milan, Manchester United and Aston Villa all vanquished 3-0 over the past week.

For both teams, the quarter-final in mid-December will represent an inviting opportunity to take a giant stride towards winning a trophy this season. With Arsenal, Chelsea, Tottenham and Man United all out of the Carabao Cup, the route to a Wembley final is very much opening up.

Iraola has already voiced his intentions to take the competition seriously, viewing it as a genuine opportunity to lift silverware in his first campaign in charge of Liverpool.

That’ll mean having to get through a tie that he’d rather not have had to negotiate, but we’re sure he’d prefer it to having a week off in December from his team already being knocked out of the competition.

#2053. Sunday's Serie A predictions including Juventus vs. Napoli, Lazio vs. Cagliari

By Seye Omidiora | 01 Nov 2026 00:30

Today's Serie A predictions include Luciano Spalletti and Max Allegri taking on their former clubs, with Juventus facing Napoli in the standout match, as well as title-contending Lazio welcoming Cagliari to the capital.

Arriving at Stadio Sinigaglia in starkly contrasting form, high-flying Como and rock-bottom Venezia will meet for Serie A's Sunday lunchtime kickoff.

While the hosts won again in midweek, and stayed in touch with Italy's top three, their Venetian visitors lost for the eighth time this term.

While Venezia have generally offered some resistance at Stadio Penzo, they are yet to pick up a point on the road - and that drought will go on.

Como may be feeling the strain of a packed fixture list - and several fringe players are injured - but their sheer weight of individual skill usually shines through.

After racking up 13 goals in three games, free-scoring Frosinone will aim to extend their strong start in Serie A when they welcome Torino to Stadio Stirpe on Sunday.   Sitting four points above their visitors, the newly promoted side are surpassing all expectations, but Toro's own winning run was abruptly halted in midweek.

Generally tipped for relegation in August, Frosinone have quickly become a team to fear, smashing goals past several opponents.

Yet, after a grim 2025-26 campaign, Torino are showing signs of improvement under new boss Abate - and they have had two extra days to recover.

Lazio will look to prolong an incredible start to the Serie A season on Sunday, when they welcome Cagliari to Stadio Olimpico.

For the first time since they last lifted the Scudetto, the Biancocelesti are unbeaten through their first nine league games; meanwhile, the visitors remain in Rome after suffering another defeat in midweek.

While Lazio cannot stop scoring, Cagliari have begun to leak goals at an alarming rate, and that is not a good combination for the Sardinian side.

So, the hosts' success streak will go on, while the visitors are set for their second loss in Rome within the space of five days.

Fresh from securing consecutive Serie A victories for the first time this season, Genoa travel to Lecce on Sunday aiming to claim a third straight league win on matchday 10.

Daniele De Rossi's men will certainly be in higher spirits than the Salentini, who have suffered back-to-back defeats after falling 5-1 to early-season high-flyers Frosinone on Thursday.

Thursday's heavy defeat was alarming, but Lecce have repeatedly demonstrated an ability to recover from successive setbacks and should produce a more disciplined home performance.

Genoa's six-match winless away run and five blanks during that sequence suggest that their recent revival may stall at Stadio Via del Mare.

Headlining Serie A's ninth round, Italian giants Juventus and Napoli will convene in Turin for a heavyweight contest on Sunday.

Both coaches have a glorious past with the other club, but that must be forgotten when three points are at stake - particularly with the pair trailing Italy's top six.

Traditionally, the home side prevails when this pair clash, but Juventus are currently low in confidence and could be facing another defeat.

Napoli have unlocked more firepower since returning from the last international break, and that should help them outscore their ailing hosts.

#2052. Giorgi Mamardashvili says Liverpool staff got one thing ‘wrong’ before penalty shootout

Giorgi Mamardashvili has said that the information given to him about Chelsea’s penalty takers prior to Liverpool’s Carabao Cup shootout win over the Blues was erroneous.

With the teams level at 1-1 at the end of normal time, the tie would be settled on spot kicks, and the Reds prevailed 6-5 after sudden death to advance to a home quarter-final against Bournemouth.

At the end of the shootout, the home players flocked to the Georgian goalkeeper, whose save from Emmanuel Emegha proved the turning point as the Dutchman had the opportunity to win it for the visitors with his kick.

It was the only one of Chelsea’s eight penalties that Mamardashvili actually saved (Valentin Barco struck the post and Wesley Fofana skied his into the Kop), and the 26-year-old joked afterwards that his notes on the Blues’ penalty takers weren’t of much use to him.

Speaking to ITV after the match, Liverpool’s number 25 said: “I had this paper as well, but everything was wrong!”, adding that the information provided to him by club staff wasn’t helpful during the shootout.

On the save from Emegha, the goalkeeper explained: “Before the shot I was looking at his [standing] leg, where he puts it down. I decided to go to my right side. I wanted to save more but sometimes one is enough.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Perhaps Mamardashvili was disappointed with his save ratio from the eight Chelsea penalties – excluding shootouts, he’s saved 10 out of 29 faced in his career – but he came good for Liverpool in the one moment that they needed him most (the save from Emegha).

The Georgian guessed the right direction on five of the Blues’ spot kicks, and while he was given no chance with Levi Colwill’s powerful strike, he won’t be happy to have let Morgan Rogers’ spot kick squirm under his dive.

The 26-year-old also did his bit to ensure that his team made it to the penalty shootout, pulling off smart reaction saves from Rogers and Marco Palestra in the second half, and he’ll be satisfied with his overall performance whilst standing in for Alisson Becker.

Mamardashvili will probably have to wait until the quarter-final against Bournemouth in mid-December to make his next Liverpool appearancve, unless his Brazilian counterpart is rendered unavailable in the meantime.

However, the towering Georgia international showed last night that he’s capable of stepping up and delivering when the Reds need him. If he’s involved in another penalty shootout later in the season, hopefully the notes given to him will be more accurate this time!

#2051. Jamie McGrath insists Hibs' win over Hearts 'reward' for fans after slow start

Jamie McGrath believes Hibernian's win over Hearts in the semi-final of the Premier Sports Cup was "reward" for fans who have supported through thick and thin this season.

The Easter Road outfit saw off their Edinburgh rivals in the derby clash at Hampden on Sunday to seal their spot in the cup final against Rangers to be played on December 13.

Their form in the Scottish Premiership has been poor by comparison and Marink Reedijk's side are languishing at the foot of the Premiership table. But for McGrath that is somewhat of a false position.

Hibs have been unfortunate not to take more points this season and secure more victories, the midfielder says, as they have struggled to turn performances into results.

Jamie McGrath reacts after firing @HibernianFC into the #PremierSportsCup Final with his Edinburgh Derby winner 🥬 "Today, I think we got our reward" 🗣️ #PremierSportsCup https://t.co/0xRwKJwDdU

— Premier Sports (@PremSportsTV) November 1, 2026

So he hopes the derby victory can catapult his side back to form and help push them up the division and give their fans more to shout about.

"Yeah it's been a frustrating start to the season obviously, we knew we had to just keep working," he said. "Today I think we got our reward.

"We've been unlucky in the past few weeks not to get a few wins, but better saving it for today, I suppose.

"We've had that belief (we could change the narrative) but for whatever reason the last few weeks we haven't got the results we wanted or that perhaps performances merited.

"I think first-half today we showed bits and pieces how good we can be on and off the ball so it's something we can work towards, keep building towards and working hard and now we can reward the travelling fans with a final."

Asked to talk reporter Connie McLaughlin through his winning goal after Martin Boyle had levelled in the aftermath of Claudio Braga's early Hearts opener, McGrath instead took time to applaud man of the match Joe Newell.

"Set-piece, Joe does brilliantly and I think he was outstanding today. He kept the ball alive and was unlucky not to score himself. I saw the ball coming to me so it was a nice one," he concluded.

#2050. MN: Why the shortcomings of Milan’s squad have been exposed by pendulum-like form

AC Milan fell to their first defeat of the Serie A season on Wednesday night, losing to Bologna, and it exposed some obvious shortcomings.

MilanNews have chosen to focus above all on the squad available to the head coach Ruben Amorim. With matches every three days due to the two competitions to be played (hopefully) throughout the season, the pendulum-swing nature is becoming harder to digest.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The reason is quite clear: the squad is too small to be competitive every three days in both the league and the Europa League. It is objectively limited in quantity and poor in quality, especially in the reserve options. Amorim even said he could sense the fatigue from minute one.

It’s no coincidence, therefore, that Milan struggles to maintain a steady course for more than two consecutive matches. With fixtures so close together, when the opponent’s level rises (Bournemouth and Bologna are significantly stronger and more organised than Salzburg and Udinese), the squad’s limitations and the quality of its players come to the fore.

This is clearly exacerbated by the numerous injuries and the need to deploy players out of position to cover for absences. It will take at least a couple of transfer windows to more or less sort out the squad situation, giving Amorim the right players for his ideas and for all the matches he faces.

However, it’s equally true that more should have been done this summer, starting by supporting Amorim with a proper Head of Football/technical director, someone with experience to oversee the necessary overhaul.

The key for now though is to face reality. While trying to recover the injured players, we must wait until January, when – according to Cardinale’s promise  – some more reinforcements will arrive. Amorim deserves time and trust, but he can help himself with some selections too.

#2049. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

🌴 @RealBetis_en's Hector Bellerin reacts to a 3-1 preseason win over his former club Arsenal"I spent 10 years over there always trying to help and see Arsenal where it belongs, and it's nice to finally face them with them being in that position" 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/er3YtAysQb

“It is another opportunity for fitness. Coming into games against teams of good quality, it is important we get good fitness. It is a chance to build momentum for the season ahead. We are taking steps in the right direction. Of course, we want more from the performance and the results, but we take learnings and move on.

Antony was booed when he came on and is also being booed whenever he touches the ball.

Martinelli is played in down the left channel and gets onto the end of the ball inside the Betis box. He checks back and finds his compatriot Jesus on the edge of the box. Jesus tries to pick out the bottom corner but his shot goes just wide.

Isco should put Betis 4-1 up but tries to be too cute and clever. Former Arsenal man Bellerin delivers a cross from the right side of the box and picks out a free Isco in the six-yard box. Arsenal have changed nearly their entire starting XI whereas Betis have made just the one substitution thus far. Betis have played more games so far in pre-season, which probably explains the difference in the number of changes.

Salmon is deceived by a dummy by Riquelme and then brings the Betis man down, earning him a yellow card.

On the hour mark, Mikel Arteta is going to make a triple change, which feels like it was a plan going into the game. That includes Meslier coming on in goal in place of Kepa.

Copley is helped off by the two Arsenal medics, shaking his head and not putting any weight on his left leg, and is replaced by Julienne.

You have to hope that the knee injury to Louie Copley is not serious but judging by the way he went down largely unchallenged, his reaction and the way he was being helped down the tunnel it didn’t look too good. A tough moment for the youngster who had only been on the pitch nine minutes.

Play is halted as Copley has been down for a little while clutching at his left knee. He got his studs stuck in the ground and went down in some pain. The medics come on to check that left knee. He only came on at half-time but his night is over not even 10 minutes into the second half.

Nwaneri catches Bernal and if this was a competitive fixture than I think Nwaneri would perhaps have been booked for that challenge.

Those raft of changes from Mikel Arteta at half-time have seen just four of their starting XI remain on the pitch; Kepa, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly and Nwaneri.

Arsenal have a corner early on in this second half as Vieira’s shot from distance deflects behind. The delivery from the left has too much on it, going over the heads of all the Arsenal players in the box, and Betis are able to clear.

Mikel Arteta has made a whole host of changes, which includes the likes of Jesus, Martinelli, Gabriel and Vieira coming on. Betis have brought the former Real Madrid man Isco on at the break.

Arsenal’s title triumph was built on that stout defence and conceding so few but there have been so many self-inflicted wounds here. The first half is brought to an end and Real Betis take a 3-1 lead into the break.

Manuel Pellegrini’s side have their third goal of the night and restore their two-goal advantage. Havertz gives the ball away poorly deep inside his own half and the ball is played into Fornals. Riquelme shoots from just outside the box and forces Kepa into a save down to his right.

Betis have one goal from a corner and now Arsenal do. Betis keeper Valles complains that he is being fouled by Havertz after Tzolis swung in the corner from the left and the ball comes through to Hincapie, who has the simplest of headers from inside the six-yard box.

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Spanish side Real Betis at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin, with this being the first-ever meeting between the two sides. This is the first time Arsenal have played a pre-season game in Dublin since August 2018, when they drew 1-1 with London rivals Chelsea, with Arsenal winning on penalties.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 in their opening game of pre-season, with new signing Christos Tzolis on the scoresheet in his first appearance for the club. After today, Arsenal have three more games, including the Community Shield, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry on opening night of the new season. They are closing in on a deal for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes, who is set to become one of Arsenal’s most expensive signings. Mikel Arteta’s side have been dealt a blow ahead of the season with the news that France centre-back William Saliba will miss an extended period due to a back injury. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Real Betis, under the management of former Manchester City boss Manuel Pellegrini, finished fifth in La Liga last season and have therefore qualified for this coming season’s Champions League after a 20-year absence from the competition. Pellegrini has led Betis into European competitions for five consecutive seasons, which includes losing the 2025 Europa Conference League final to Chelsea. They have been busy in pre-season action already having played five games up to this point. They have won four of the five, including a 4-0 victory over Lyon, with just one defeat coming against Granada.

They have a number of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Antony, Giovani Lo Celso, Pablo Fornals and former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin. Real Betis have already played a number of friendlies as they build up to the start of their season, which begins on August 21 when they take on Real Sociedad.

#2048. Journalist takes brutal dig at Chelsea player after one incident which highly amused Van Dijk

One journalist was far from impressed with the antics of Chelsea defender Malo Gusto in his team’s Carabao Cup clash against Liverpool at Anfield on Wednesday night.

Early in the second half, the 23-year-old received the merest of contact from Virgil van Dijk and threw himself to the ground in apparent agony, clutching his leg in melodramatic fashion while the Reds captain simply looked at him with a face of bemusement.

A couple of minutes later, the Blues left-back was gently nudged by Bradley Barcola in front of the Kenny Dalglish Stand and again fell to the turf dramatically, even removing his boot and waving it at the assistant referee to try and dupe him into thinking that he’d been grievously harmed.

After the first of those rather amusing incidents, Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle took to X with a rather sardonic verdict on the coming together between the Chelsea defender and the LFC skipper.

The journalist posted with tongue firmly in cheek: ‘Gusto is down after an altercation with Van Dijk and may now have to retire from the sport’.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

We just hope that the Chelsea left-back watches those two incidents and is shamed into cleaning up his act, with his amateur theatrics not painting him in a positive light whatsoever.

The way in which he threw himself to the ground after the mildest of contact from Van Dijk and Barcola was embarrassing, as was his waving of his boot towards the assistant referee.

That’s not the kind of behaviour that we want to see from any player on a football pitch, no matter what team’s colours they’re wearing, and Xabi Alonso should pull him aside and reprimand him over it.

We can only imagine how melodramatic Gusto would’ve been if a Liverpool player had shoved him in the same way that Emmanuel Emegha did to Van Dijk later in the second half.

For his own sake, we’d implore the 23-year-old to refrain from such needless play-acting in the future.

#2047. Alvaro Arbeloa makes bold "we can beat anyone" claim after Fulham end Villa Park losing run

By Ben Sully | 01 Nov 2026 00:39, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 02:17

Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has expressed his belief that his team "can beat anyone" after they held Aston Villa to a 1-1 draw on Saturday.

The Cottagers were fortunate not to fall behind in the early stages at Villa Park as John McGinn crashed his 16th-minute penalty against the frame of the goal.

Villa eventually opened the scoring through Nicolas Jackson in the closing stages of the first period, before Fulham responded with a lengthy spell of consistent pressure after the restart.

The Cottagers deservedly levelled the scoreline just after the hour mark, although the goal arrived in fortuitous circumstances as Zion Suzuki dropped the ball over the line as he attempted to gather from a corner.

While they were unable to find a winner, the draw ended Fulham's seven-game losing run at Villa Park since they last won at the ground in 2014.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! ? https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk

Fulham finished the game with 55% possession, five shots on target to Villa's three and an xG of 2.21 compared to the opposition's 1.71.

The encouraging performance represented another building block in Alvaro Arbeloa's tenure as his side made it three consecutive Premier League games without a win.

Speaking after the game, the Fulham boss declared that his players have proven they are capable of competing with any team put in front of them.

"I am so happy with our performance in the second half," Arbeloa said. "This is what I want to see from my team, that character, that ambition.

"We needed to be aggressive against a team like Villa. It was a Champions League team in front of us.

"Technically, I thought we were very good but this is the Premier League, and you have to be aggressive, and physically, you have to be at your best level.

"I think maybe we deserved a little bit more, but the performance was really great. I think we are a very difficult team to beat, and I think we can beat anyone."

Having picked up seven points from their last three games, Fulham sit outside the Premier League drop zone in 15th, but they cannot rest on their laurels, with only two points separating them from the bottom three.

Arbeloa's charge will turn their focus to a home clash against Newcastle United on Saturday, November 7.

That will be their final outing before the international window, and it will be key to pick up a positive result before they return to action with a tricky run of fixtures after the two-week break.

Fulham take on Manchester City on November 21, before going up against two teams currently in form in the shape of Bournemouth and Tottenham Hotspur.

#2045. Martin Boyle's goosebumps as Hibs hero salutes fans after downing Hearts

Jubilant Martin Boyle dedicated Hibernian's stirring Premier Sports Cup semi-final victory over Hearts to the supporters who have stood by the team through a difficult campaign.

The Easter Road hero was emotional at full-time after helping fire Hibs into the final at Hampden, where they will face Rangers on December 13.

Boyle cancelled out Claudio Braga's opener before Jamie McGrath netted the winner in a dramatic Edinburgh derby comeback that sparked wild celebrations among the green-and-white half of the national stadium.

With Hibs sitting bottom of the Premiership, Boyle believes the result can provide a major boost heading into the rest of the season.

Speaking to Premier Sports, he said: "Unbelievable. I thought we were brilliant in the first half, apart from the corner. After that, the reaction from the boys was great and I thought we probably deserved it.

Read more: Marink Reedijk challenges Hibs to 'create new history' in huge Hearts Hampden clash

"In the second half we dug in and defended the box really well. It's a derby, we knew form would go out the window and we stuck together. We always believed we could win this game and we have."

Asked how a side at the foot of the table could produce such a performance on the big stage, Boyle insisted confidence has never disappeared within the squad.

He said: "Nothing's changed, we've always had that belief.

"We're going through a bit of a transition phase at the moment and the squad is quite young, so us senior boys really need to step up.

"The experienced boys coming on helped us at the end. It's brilliant and the fans deserve it for sticking with us."

Boyle reserved special praise for the travelling support, who created a thunderous atmosphere throughout the afternoon.

He said: "Hopefully we can enjoy a cup final and get ourselves up the league table. That's the main objective.

"The noise behind us here was unbelievable."

The 33-year-old, who has made more than 400 appearances for the club, admitted the occasion brought back memories of some of the greatest days of his Hibs career.

"It's a special feeling," he said. "I've got goosebumps. It's a great day out.

"Moments like this don't come around often and you've got to create them. We did that today and the fans have stuck by us.

"I know the league performances haven't been great, but thank you to everyone who came to support us today. They can go home with a smile on their face and enjoy their night out."

Hibs will return to Hampden next month looking to lift the trophy, but Boyle is refusing to get carried away ahead of the showdown with Rangers.

He smiled: "I'm not getting carried away, fingers crossed.

"I've still got some legs in me at the tender age of 33. As long as I'm playing and contributing to this club, I can enjoy moments like this and we can all enjoy the day out in the final.":

#2043. ‘Ask him’ – Virgil van Dijk shrugs off bizarre incident with Chelsea player in Liverpool triumph

Virgil van Dijk has refused to be drawn on an incident involving him and Emmanuel Emegha in Liverpool’s Carabao Cup fourth-round clash against Chelsea on Wednesday night.

The Dutch striker came on for his senior Blues debut midway through the second half at Anfield, and within a few minutes he initiated a bizarre tussle with his compatriot.

After the Reds captain played the ball backwards to Trey Nyoni, the Chelsea substitute charged straight at our number 4 and shoved him to the ground, with the pass having been made at least a second earlier.

Speaking to reporters after the match, Van Dijk was asked about the curious incident with Emegha, and the Liverpool skipper swiftly shut down the question.

He replied (via Liverpool Echo): “Ask him. I don’t know. Maybe he’s trying to get into the national team as well and trying this way. I don’t know. You have to ask him. When he comes by, just ask him.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

We’re at a loss for an explanation as to why Emegha ran at Van Dijk well after the ball had been played, and he came from enough of a distance to have stopped himself in his tracks and realised that he’d have been better off not getting involved.

What was the Chelsea striker’s motivation to run at his fellow countryman and shove him to the ground? Beats us…

The Liverpool captain seemed momentarily irritated over the bizarre altercation but mostly bemused, just like he was at Malo Gusto’s comical play-acting after making the slightest of contact with the French left-back earlier in the second half.

Van Dijk had the last laugh as it was his team who prevailed on penalties, and although the 35-year-old had been substituted before the shootout, he’d done his bit for the Reds with a solid performance and an important interception to thwart Danny Welbeck.

We eagerly await Emegha’s explanation as to why he went over and accosted the veteran defender for no apparent reason…

#2041. Michael Carrick’s Man Utd misery compounded as continental rivals 'hijack' Old Trafford's succession masterplan

By Seye Omidiora | 01 Nov 2026 01:04, Last updated: 01 Nov 2026 05:06

Manchester United could reportedly miss out on top managerial target Julian Nagelsmann following emerging interest from Italian giants Juventus.

The Red Devils extended their miserable winless streak across all competitions after suffering a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Saturday afternoon.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring for Xabi Alonso's side early in the second half before Cole Palmer doubled the advantage from the penalty spot.

A frustrating afternoon in West London was compounded when Lisandro Martinez received a red card for raising his forearm towards Wesley Fofana to concede the decisive spot kick.

Despite losing four of their last five matches, Michael Carrick has seemingly retained the backing of the Old Trafford board for the time being.

According to Italian journalist Rudy Galetti via Manchester Evening News, Juventus have officially registered their interest in Nagelsmann as they prepare for a potential change in the dugout.

Juventus are reportedly weighing up the prospect of dismissing head coach Luciano Spalletti, following a run of just two wins in their past seven matches.

The report names the former Bayern Munich and Germany manager as the club’s leading choice to oversee a much-needed revival in Turin.

Spalletti faces a pivotal Serie A meeting with Napoli on Sunday evening, with defeat at home potentially bringing his tenure to an end.

Juventus are also said to be keeping tabs on Didier Deschamps, Stefano Pioli, Sergio Conceicao and former boss Antonio Conte as possible alternatives.

Juventus’ unexpected move poses a major headache for United’s hierarchy as they cautiously consider their options for life after Carrick.

Nagelsmann had already emerged as one of the leading contenders for the Old Trafford vacancy, alongside Eddie Howe and Unai Emery.

Should the German coach accept a lucrative offer from the Serie A side, the Premier League strugglers would have to rethink their managerial shortlist considerably.

For now, Carrick is expected to take charge of a daunting Champions League tie against Roma on Tuesday evening.

The under-pressure Englishman thanked the travelling supporters for their full-time ovation at Stamford Bridge and said his side needed to take encouragement from the performance.
